Request object passed between API and the worker thread, describing an operation to perform. It stores the request kind in 'type' and a union payload for ptrace, fork, or function execution. The ptrace and fork variants include an _errno pointer for reporting errno from the worker context.

Opaque-ish instance structure managing the worker thread and synchronization for serialized ptrace/fork/function requests. Contains a thread handle, semaphores for request/result coordination, a request object, and a union for the result. Users create/start, use via API calls, then stop it.

functions.name: ST8_DIV_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool ST8_DIV_OVFCHK(ut8 a, ut8 b)
functions.description: Checks whether a signed 8-bit division a / b would overflow or be invalid. Returns true if b is zero (division by zero) or if a and b represent the two’s-complement MIN / -1 case that overflows on division (as encoded using the project’s ut8 constants UT8_GT0 and UT8_MAX). Intended for pre-checking before performing a signed 8-bit division in this codebase’s integer types.
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid ut8 values as defined by the project.
A return value of true indicates division is unsafe (overflow or division by zero); callers should avoid performing the actual division in that case.
Semantics assume two’s-complement representation consistent with the UT8_GT0 and UT8_MAX constants.

functions.name: ST16_DIV_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool ST16_DIV_OVFCHK(ut16 a, ut16 b)
functions.description: Checks whether a signed 16-bit division a / b would overflow or be invalid. Returns true if b is zero or if a and b encode the two’s-complement MIN / -1 overflow case (using UT16_GT0 and UT16_MAX). Use to guard signed 16-bit division.
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid ut16 values as defined by the project.
True return means the division should not be performed (division by zero or overflow).
Assumes two’s-complement encoding per UT16_GT0 and UT16_MAX.

functions.name: ST32_DIV_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool ST32_DIV_OVFCHK(ut32 a, ut32 b)
functions.description: Checks whether a signed 32-bit division a / b would overflow or be invalid. Returns true on division by zero or when a and b encode MIN / -1 for two’s-complement (using UT32_GT0 and UT32_MAX).
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid ut32 values as defined by the project.
True return indicates unsafe division; do not perform the actual division.
Relies on two’s-complement representation implied by UT32_GT0 and UT32_MAX.

functions.name: ST64_DIV_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool ST64_DIV_OVFCHK(ut64 a, ut64 b)
functions.description: Checks whether a signed 64-bit division a / b would overflow or be invalid. Returns true if b is zero or if a and b encode the MIN / -1 overflow case for two’s-complement (using UT64_GT0 and UT64_MAX).
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid ut64 values as defined by the project.
A true result means the division must not be performed due to division by zero or overflow.
Assumes two’s-complement encoding consistent with UT64_GT0 and UT64_MAX.

functions.name: UT8_DIV_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool UT8_DIV_OVFCHK(ut8 a, ut8 b)
functions.description: Checks whether an unsigned 8-bit division a / b would be invalid. Returns true if b is zero (division by zero); no other overflow condition exists for unsigned division.
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid ut8 values as defined by the project.
Callers must ensure b != 0 before dividing; a true result indicates division by zero.

functions.name: UT16_DIV_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool UT16_DIV_OVFCHK(ut16 a, ut16 b)
functions.description: Checks whether an unsigned 16-bit division a / b would be invalid. Returns true only if b is zero (division by zero).
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid ut16 values as defined by the project.
Callers must ensure b != 0 before performing the division; true indicates division by zero.

functions.name: UT32_DIV_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool UT32_DIV_OVFCHK(ut32 a, ut32 b)
functions.description: Checks whether an unsigned 32-bit division a / b would be invalid. Returns true only if b is zero (division by zero).
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid ut32 values as defined by the project.
Callers must ensure b != 0 before dividing; true indicates division by zero.

functions.name: UT64_DIV_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool UT64_DIV_OVFCHK(ut64 a, ut64 b)
functions.description: Checks whether an unsigned 64-bit division a / b would be invalid. Returns true only if b is zero (division by zero).
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid ut64 values as defined by the project.
Callers must ensure b != 0 before dividing; true indicates division by zero.

functions.name: ST8_MUL_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool ST8_MUL_OVFCHK(st8 a, st8 b)
functions.description: Checks whether a signed 8-bit multiplication a * b would overflow. Returns true when the product cannot be represented in st8 based on two’s-complement bounds ST8_MIN and ST8_MAX.
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid st8 values as defined by the project.
A true result indicates the multiplication would overflow; do not perform the actual multiplication without handling this case.

functions.name: ST16_MUL_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool ST16_MUL_OVFCHK(st16 a, st16 b)
functions.description: Checks whether a signed 16-bit multiplication a * b would overflow. Returns true when the product exceeds the st16 range [ST16_MIN, ST16_MAX].
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid st16 values as defined by the project.
True indicates overflow; callers should avoid performing the multiplication or handle the error condition.

functions.name: ST32_MUL_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool ST32_MUL_OVFCHK(st32 a, st32 b)
functions.description: Checks whether a signed 32-bit multiplication a * b would overflow. Returns true when the product is outside [ST32_MIN, ST32_MAX].
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid st32 values as defined by the project.
True indicates overflow; callers must not rely on a * b fitting in st32 without handling this case.

functions.name: ST64_MUL_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool ST64_MUL_OVFCHK(st64 a, st64 b)
functions.description: Checks whether a signed 64-bit multiplication a * b would overflow. Returns true when the product is outside [ST64_MIN, ST64_MAX].
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid st64 values as defined by the project.
A true result indicates overflow; avoid performing the multiplication or use a wider type.

functions.name: SZT_MUL_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool SZT_MUL_OVFCHK(size_t a, size_t b)
functions.description: Checks whether an unsigned size_t multiplication a * b would overflow. Returns true when a > SZT_MAX / b (for b > 0), which means the product cannot be represented in size_t.
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid size_t values.
A true result indicates overflow; callers should not perform the multiplication or should handle the overflow case.

functions.name: UT8_MUL_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool UT8_MUL_OVFCHK(ut8 a, ut8 b)
functions.description: Checks whether an unsigned 8-bit multiplication a * b would overflow. Returns true when a > UT8_MAX / b for positive operands.
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid ut8 values as defined by the project.
True indicates overflow; do not perform the multiplication without handling this case.

functions.name: UT16_MUL_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool UT16_MUL_OVFCHK(ut16 a, ut16 b)
functions.description: Checks whether an unsigned 16-bit multiplication a * b would overflow. Returns true when a > UT16_MAX / b for positive operands.
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid ut16 values as defined by the project.
True indicates overflow; callers should not rely on the product fitting in ut16.

functions.name: UT32_MUL_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool UT32_MUL_OVFCHK(ut32 a, ut32 b)
functions.description: Checks whether an unsigned 32-bit multiplication a * b would overflow. Returns true when a > UT32_MAX / b for positive operands.
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid ut32 values as defined by the project.
True indicates overflow; avoid performing the multiplication if a wider type is unavailable.

functions.name: UT64_MUL_OVFCHK
functions.signature: static inline bool UT64_MUL_OVFCHK(ut64 a, ut64 b)
functions.description: Checks whether an unsigned 64-bit multiplication a * b would overflow. Returns true when a > UT64_MAX / b for positive operands.
requirements: Arguments a and b must be valid ut64 values as defined by the project.
True indicates overflow; performing the multiplication would exceed ut64 range.

functions.name: r_new_copy
functions.description: Allocates a new heap buffer of length size and copies size bytes from data into it, returning the newly allocated pointer. Useful to duplicate a fixed-size object or buffer by value. Returns NULL if allocation fails.
requirements: If size > 0, data must be non-NULL and point to at least size readable bytes.
If size == 0, behavior of malloc(0) is implementation-defined; the returned pointer may be NULL or a unique pointer. memcpy with size==0 does not dereference data.
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is owned by the caller and must be released with free().
No alignment beyond malloc’s guarantees is provided.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are the same as malloc/memcpy on the platform.

functions.name: r_run_call1
functions.description: Invokes a function pointer fcn taking one void* argument and returning void. It casts fcn to void (*)(void*) and calls it with arg1. Provides a generic, arity-1 trampoline.
requirements: fcn must be a non-NULL pointer to a function with the exact signature void (*)(void*).
arg1 is passed as-is; its validity must satisfy the callee’s contract (may be NULL if the callee permits).
Mismatched function type or NULL fcn results in undefined behavior.

functions.name: r_run_call2
functions.signature: static inline void r_run_call2(void *fcn, void *arg1, void *arg2)
functions.description: Invokes a function pointer fcn taking two void* arguments and returning void. Casts fcn to void (*)(void*, void*) and calls it with arg1, arg2. Arity-2 trampoline.
requirements: fcn must be non-NULL and point to a function with signature void (*)(void*, void*).
arg1 and arg2 are passed through; they must meet the callee’s expectations (may be NULL if allowed).
Mismatched signature or NULL fcn leads to undefined behavior.

functions.name: r_run_call3
functions.signature: static inline void r_run_call3(void *fcn, void *arg1, void *arg2, void *arg3)
functions.description: Invokes a function pointer fcn taking three void* arguments and returning void. Casts to void (*)(void*, void*, void*) and calls it.
requirements: fcn must be non-NULL and point to a function with signature void (*)(void*, void*, void*).
arg1, arg2, arg3 must satisfy the callee’s requirements; NULLs only if accepted by the callee.
Mismatched signature or NULL fcn results in undefined behavior.

functions.name: r_run_call4
functions.signature: static inline void r_run_call4(void *fcn, void *arg1, void *arg2, void *arg3, void *arg4)
functions.description: Invokes a function pointer fcn taking four void* arguments and returning void. Casts to void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*) and calls it.
requirements: fcn must be non-NULL and point to a function with signature void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*).
All argument pointers are forwarded unchanged; they must be valid per the callee’s contract.
Mismatched signature or NULL fcn causes undefined behavior.

functions.name: r_run_call5
functions.signature: static inline void r_run_call5(void *fcn, void *arg1, void *arg2, void *arg3, void *arg4, void *arg5)
functions.description: Invokes a function pointer fcn taking five void* arguments and returning void. Casts to void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*, void*) and calls it.
requirements: fcn must be non-NULL and match signature void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*, void*).
All arguments are passed through; their validity must match callee requirements.
Any mismatch in signature or NULL fcn is undefined behavior.

functions.name: r_run_call6
functions.signature: static inline void r_run_call6(void *fcn, void *arg1, void *arg2, void *arg3, void *arg4, void *arg5, void *arg6)
functions.description: Invokes a function pointer fcn taking six void* arguments and returning void. Casts to void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*) and calls it.
requirements: fcn must be non-NULL and point to a function with signature void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*).
All six arguments are forwarded; ensure they meet the callee’s expectations.
Signature mismatch or NULL fcn leads to undefined behavior.

functions.name: r_run_call7
functions.signature: static inline void r_run_call7(void *fcn, void *arg1, void *arg2, void *arg3, void *arg4, void *arg5, void *arg6, void *arg7)
functions.description: Invokes a function pointer fcn taking seven void* arguments and returning void. Casts to void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*) and calls it.
requirements: fcn must be non-NULL and match signature void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*).
All seven arguments are passed through and must be suitable for the callee.
Signature mismatch or NULL fcn is undefined behavior.

functions.name: r_run_call8
functions.signature: static inline void r_run_call8(void *fcn, void *arg1, void *arg2, void *arg3, void *arg4, void *arg5, void *arg6, void *arg7, void *arg8)
functions.description: Invokes a function pointer fcn taking eight void* arguments and returning void. Casts to void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*) and calls it.
requirements: fcn must be non-NULL and match signature void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*).
All eight arguments are forwarded unchanged and must satisfy callee requirements.
Signature mismatch or NULL fcn yields undefined behavior.

functions.name: r_run_call9
functions.signature: static inline void r_run_call9(void *fcn, void *arg1, void *arg2, void *arg3, void *arg4, void *arg5, void *arg6, void *arg7, void *arg8, void *arg9)
functions.description: Invokes a function pointer fcn taking nine void* arguments and returning void. Casts to void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*) and calls it.
requirements: fcn must be non-NULL and match signature void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*).
All nine arguments are passed directly; ensure they are valid for the callee.
Signature mismatch or NULL fcn is undefined behavior.

functions.name: r_run_call10
functions.signature: static inline void r_run_call10(void *fcn, void *arg1, void *arg2, void *arg3, void *arg4, void *arg5, void *arg6, void *arg7, void *arg8, void *arg9, void *arg10)
functions.description: Invokes a function pointer fcn taking ten void* arguments and returning void. Casts to void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*) and calls it.
requirements: fcn must be non-NULL and match signature void (*)(void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*, void*).
All ten arguments are forwarded; their correctness is determined by the callee.
Signature mismatch or NULL fcn causes undefined behavior.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,init)
functions.description: Initializes a vector instance to the empty state. Sets all internal fields to zero, preparing it for use. Use this before any other operations if the vector was stack-allocated or not yet initialized.
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise the function returns immediately (no-op).
After init, the vector is empty with zero capacity.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,new)
functions.description: Allocates a new, heap-allocated empty vector and initializes it. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: Caller must free the returned vector with R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, free) when done.
No arguments; may return NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,swap)
functions.signature: static inline void R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, swap)(vec_type *vec_a, vec_type *vec_b)
functions.description: Swaps the contents (buffers, size, capacity) of two vectors in O(1). If both pointers are the same, does nothing.
requirements: vec_a and vec_b must be non-NULL; otherwise the function returns immediately (no-op).

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,clear)
functions.description: Clears the vector contents by setting its size to zero without releasing capacity. If the vector type was created with a finalizer, calls it for each element before clearing.
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise the function returns immediately (no-op).
If a finalizer was configured (R_VEC_TYPE_WITH_FINI), it must safely handle every current element.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,fini)
functions.description: Finalizes a vector: calls the per-element finalizer if configured, frees the internal buffer, and resets the vector to an uninitialized/empty state. Does not free the vector object itself.
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise the function returns immediately (no-op).
If a finalizer was configured (R_VEC_TYPE_WITH_FINI), it must safely handle every current element.
After fini, the vector must be re-initialized (init/new) before reuse.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,free)
functions.description: Frees a heap-allocated vector: calls fini on it and then frees the vector object itself. Safe to call with NULL (no-op).
requirements: If vec is non-NULL, it must be a heap allocation compatible with free.
Do not use the vector after this call.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,length)
functions.signature: static inline ut64 R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, length)(const vec_type *vec)
functions.description: Returns the number of elements currently in the vector. Returns 0 if vec is NULL.
requirements: vec may be NULL; result is 0 in that case.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,empty)
functions.signature: static inline bool R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, empty)(const vec_type *vec)
functions.description: Returns true if the vector contains no elements, false otherwise. Returns false if vec is NULL (per guard macro semantics).
requirements: vec may be NULL; the function returns false in that case.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,at)
functions.signature: static inline type *R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, at)(const vec_type *vec, ut64 index)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the element at the given index, or NULL if out of bounds or on invalid input. The returned pointer can be used to read or write the element.
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise returns NULL.
index must be less than the current length to obtain a non-NULL pointer.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,last)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the last element, or NULL if the vector is empty or vec is NULL.
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise returns NULL.
Vector must be non-empty to obtain a non-NULL pointer.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,find)
functions.signature: static inline type *R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, find)(const vec_type *vec, void *value, R_VEC_FIND_CMP(vec_type) cmp_fn)
functions.description: Linear search for the first element equal to the provided value, using cmp_fn(element, value) == 0 for equality. Returns a pointer to the matching element or NULL if not found.
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise returns NULL.
cmp_fn must be a valid function pointer compatible with int (*)(type const*, const void*).
cmp_fn must tolerate the provided value pointer (which may be any user data).

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,find_if_not)
functions.signature: static inline type *R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, find_if_not)(const vec_type *vec, void *value, R_VEC_FIND_CMP(vec_type) cmp_fn)
functions.description: Linear search for the first element where cmp_fn(element, value) returns non-zero. Returns a pointer to that element or NULL if none match.
requirements: vec and value must not be NULL; otherwise returns NULL.
cmp_fn must be a valid function pointer compatible with int (*)(type const*, const void*).

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,find_index)
functions.signature: static inline ut64 R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, find_index)(const vec_type *vec, void *value, R_VEC_FIND_CMP(vec_type) cmp_fn)
functions.description: Returns the index of the first element equal to the provided value (cmp_fn(element, value) == 0). Returns UT64_MAX if not found or on invalid input.
requirements: vec and value must not be NULL; otherwise returns UT64_MAX.
cmp_fn must be a valid function pointer compatible with int (*)(type const*, const void*).

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,clone)
functions.description: Creates a shallow clone of the vector: allocates a new vector object and buffer sized to the source capacity, and copies the existing elements via memcpy. Returns NULL on allocation failure or invalid input.
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise returns NULL.
Cloning is shallow; element pointers/references are not deep-copied.
Caller must free the returned vector with R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, free).

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,reserve)
functions.signature: static inline bool R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, reserve)(vec_type *vec, ut64 new_capacity)
functions.description: Ensures capacity is at least new_capacity, growing the internal buffer if needed. Preserves existing elements. Returns true on success, false on allocation failure or invalid input.
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise returns false.
If new_capacity <= current capacity, the function returns true without reallocating.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,shrink_to_fit)
functions.description: Reduces capacity to match the current number of elements. If size is zero, frees the buffer and zeros the struct. No effect if capacity already equals size.
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise the function returns immediately (no-op).

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,push_back)
functions.signature: static inline void R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, push_back)(vec_type *vec, type const *value)
functions.description: Appends a copy of the given element to the end of the vector, growing capacity (by doubling, starting at 8) if needed. No-op on allocation failure.
requirements: vec and value must not be NULL; otherwise the function returns immediately (no-op).
If reallocation is required and fails, the element is not appended.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,emplace_back)
functions.description: Appends a new uninitialized element slot at the end and returns a pointer to it. Grows capacity if needed. The memory is zeroed before returning. Caller should initialize the element to valid data before further use.
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise returns NULL.
On allocation failure, returns NULL and does not change the vector.
Caller must write a valid element to the returned location before assuming meaningful content.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,push_front)
functions.signature: static inline void R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, push_front)(vec_type *vec, type *value)
functions.description: Prepends a copy of the given element to the front of the vector, shifting existing elements forward. Grows capacity if needed. Slower than push_back due to memmove.
requirements: vec and value must not be NULL; otherwise the function returns immediately (no-op).
If reallocation is required and fails, the element is not inserted.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,emplace_front)
functions.description: Inserts a new uninitialized element slot at the front of the vector, shifting existing elements. Returns a pointer to the new front element. The memory is zeroed before returning. Slower than emplace_back.
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise returns NULL.
On allocation failure, returns NULL and does not change the vector.
Caller should initialize the returned element to valid data before further use.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,append)
functions.signature: static inline void R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, append)(vec_type *vec, const vec_type *values, R_VEC_COPY(vec_type) copy_fn)
functions.description: Appends all elements from values to vec. Ensures capacity for the combined size. If copy_fn is NULL, performs a shallow memcpy; otherwise, emplaces elements one-by-one and calls copy_fn(dst, src) for each to support deep-copy semantics.
requirements: vec and values must not be NULL; otherwise the function returns immediately (no-op).
copy_fn may be NULL; if provided, it must be compatible with void (*)(type *dst, type const *src).
On allocation failure during growth, the function returns without appending.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,remove)
functions.signature: static inline void R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, remove)(vec_type *vec, ut64 index)
functions.description: Removes the element at the given index, shifting subsequent elements down by one. Calls the element finalizer for the removed element if configured.
requirements: vec must not be NULL.
Vector must be non-empty.
index must be in range [0, length-1].
If a finalizer was configured (R_VEC_TYPE_WITH_FINI), it must safely handle the element being removed.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,pop_front)
functions.description: Removes the first element of the vector (equivalent to remove(vec, 0)). May call the finalizer if configured.
requirements: Same requirements as remove: vec must be non-NULL and non-empty.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,pop_back)
functions.description: Removes the last element of the vector. May call the finalizer if configured.
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise returns immediately (no-op).
Vector must be non-empty; otherwise returns immediately (no-op).

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,erase_back)
functions.signature: static inline void R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, erase_back)(vec_type *vec, type *iter)
functions.description: Erases all elements from iter to the end of the vector (not inclusive of end), optionally calling the finalizer on each if configured. If iter == end, no elements are removed.
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise returns immediately (no-op).
iter must be within the range [vec->_start, vec->_end]. If outside, function returns immediately (no-op).
If a finalizer was configured (R_VEC_TYPE_WITH_FINI), it must safely handle each element in [iter, end).

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,lower_bound)
functions.signature: static inline ut64 R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, lower_bound)(vec_type *vec, type *value, R_VEC_CMP(vec_type) cmp_fn)
functions.description: Binary searches for the first position where value could be inserted without violating order (lower bound). Returns the index of the first element not less than value.
requirements: vec, value, and cmp_fn must not be NULL; otherwise returns 0.
cmp_fn must be compatible with int (*)(type const*, type const*) and implement a strict weak ordering consistent with the vector's sort order.
The vector must be sorted according to cmp_fn for meaningful results.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,upper_bound)
functions.signature: static inline ut64 R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, upper_bound)(vec_type *vec, type *value, R_VEC_CMP(vec_type) cmp_fn)
functions.description: Binary searches for the first index greater than value (upper bound). Returns the index of the first element greater than value.
requirements: vec, value, and cmp_fn must not be NULL; otherwise returns 0.
cmp_fn must be compatible with int (*)(type const*, type const*) and implement a strict weak ordering consistent with the vector's sort order.
The vector must be sorted according to cmp_fn for meaningful results.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,partition)
functions.signature: static inline type *R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, partition)(vec_type *vec, void *user, R_VEC_FIND_CMP(vec_type) cmp_fn)
functions.description: Partitions the vector in-place such that all elements for which cmp_fn(element, user) returns non-zero come before those for which it returns zero. Returns a pointer to the first element of the second partition (i.e., the first element for which the predicate returns zero).
requirements: vec must not be NULL; otherwise returns vec ? vec->_start : NULL (i.e., NULL).
cmp_fn must not be NULL; otherwise returns vec->_start.
cmp_fn must be compatible with int (*)(type const*, const void*) and tolerate the provided user pointer.
The function performs swaps by value; ensure type is trivially movable or that such swapping is acceptable for it.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,sort)
functions.signature: static inline void R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, sort)(vec_type *vec, R_VEC_CMP(vec_type) cmp_fn)
functions.description: Sorts the vector in place using qsort and the provided comparator. No effect if the vector is empty.
requirements: vec and cmp_fn must not be NULL; otherwise returns immediately (no-op).
cmp_fn must be compatible with int (*)(type const*, type const*) and obey a strict weak ordering.

functions.name: R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type,uniq)
functions.signature: static inline void R_VEC_FUNC(vec_type, uniq)(vec_type *vec, R_VEC_CMP(vec_type) cmp_fn)
functions.description: Removes duplicate adjacent elements from a sorted vector, keeping only unique elements. If a finalizer is configured, it is called on each removed element. Does not shrink capacity.
requirements: vec and cmp_fn must not be NULL; otherwise returns immediately (no-op).
The vector should be sorted according to cmp_fn before calling uniq for correct behavior.
If a finalizer was configured (R_VEC_TYPE_WITH_FINI), it must safely handle each removed element.

functions.name: r_vector_init
functions.signature: R_API void r_vector_init(RVector *vec, size_t elem_size, RVectorFree free, void *free_user);
functions.description: Initializes an RVector to hold elements of elem_size bytes, optionally registering a per-element free callback and its user data. Use this before any other RVector operation on a stack- or embedded-allocated RVector.
requirements: vec must be a valid, writable pointer to an RVector struct.
elem_size must be > 0 and match the size of the elements you will store.
If free is provided, it must be callable as free(element_ptr, free_user) for each element pointer inside the internal array.
Do not call on an already-initialized vector without finalizing it first (risk of leaks).

functions.name: r_vector_new
functions.signature: R_API RVector *r_vector_new(size_t elem_size, RVectorFree free, void *free_user);
functions.description: Allocates and returns a heap-allocated RVector initialized for elements of elem_size bytes, optionally with a per-element free callback and user data.
requirements: elem_size must be > 0 and match the size of the elements you will store.
If free is provided, it must be callable as free(element_ptr, free_user).
Caller must check the return value for NULL (allocation failure) and free it with r_vector_free().

functions.name: r_vector_fini
functions.description: Finalizes a vector: calls vec->free on every element if set, then clears the vector (length becomes 0). Does not free the RVector struct itself.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector.
Elements’ free callback (if set) must tolerate being called once for each element.
After this call, the vector is cleared; capacity may remain allocated.

functions.name: r_vector_free
functions.description: Finalizes a vector (calls per-element free if set) and frees the RVector object itself if it was heap-allocated. Safe counterpart to r_vector_new().
requirements: vec must be either NULL or a valid, initialized RVector pointer allocated compatibly with this API.
Do not use vec after this call.
Per-element free (if set) must be safe to call once for each element.

functions.name: r_vector_clone
functions.description: Creates a new RVector with the same capacity as vec. Semantics of how elements are copied are not documented here; likely a shallow byte-wise copy of the backing storage with the same elem_size and free callback. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector.
Caller must check for NULL (allocation failure).
Element copy semantics beyond raw bytes are unknown from this header; if elements own resources, caller must verify whether deep copy is needed.

functions.name: r_vector_copy
functions.description: Copies the contents of vector s into vector d. Returns true on success, false on failure. Exact behavior (capacity handling, element-wise copy vs. raw memory) is not fully documented; expected to copy elements and metadata so d reflects s.
requirements: Both d and s must be valid, initialized RVectors.
d->elem_size must match s->elem_size (implied by design; not explicitly stated).
Caller must check the boolean return value for success.
Copy semantics for element-owned resources are unknown; if elements own resources, ensure compatibility.

functions.name: r_vector_clear
functions.description: Clears the vector (sets length to 0). Whether it invokes the registered element free callback is not stated in this header and is unknown.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector.
After clearing, capacity is not reduced (per general hint).
Whether elements are freed during clear is unknown; callers who need free-on-clear semantics should prefer r_vector_fini() if appropriate.

functions.name: r_vector_assign
functions.description: Copies an element of size vec->elem_size from elem into the memory at p. elem points to the actual data to assign; p must point inside the vector (e.g., from r_vector_index_ptr or r_vector_at).
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector.
p must be a valid pointer to an element-sized slot within vec’s internal array (properly aligned and writable).
elem must be a non-NULL pointer to at least vec->elem_size bytes of source data.
Behavior is undefined if p is out of bounds or overlaps elem in unintended ways.

functions.name: r_vector_assign_at
functions.description: Assigns an element at the given index from the data pointed to by elem (size vec->elem_size). Returns a pointer to the element’s location inside the vector.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector.
index must be within the current vector length (0 <= index < vec->len).
elem must be a non-NULL pointer to at least vec->elem_size bytes of source data.

functions.name: r_vector_remove_at
functions.signature: R_API void r_vector_remove_at(RVector *vec, size_t index, void *into);
functions.description: Removes the element at index, shifting subsequent elements down, and writes the removed element’s raw bytes into into. Caller is responsible for freeing resources associated with the removed element, if any.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector with vec->len > 0.
index must satisfy 0 <= index < vec->len.
into must point to writable storage of at least vec->elem_size bytes to receive the removed element’s content (whether NULL is allowed to discard data is not specified).
This does not reduce capacity; call r_vector_shrink() explicitly if desired.

functions.name: r_vector_insert
functions.description: Inserts a new element at index, shifting existing elements up. x points to the actual data to copy (size vec->elem_size). Returns a pointer to the inserted element’s location inside the vector (may be invalidated by reallocation).
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector.
index must satisfy 0 <= index <= vec->len.
x must be a non-NULL pointer to at least vec->elem_size bytes containing the element to insert.
Insertion may reallocate internal storage; any previously obtained internal pointers may become invalid.

functions.name: r_vector_insert_range
functions.signature: R_API void *r_vector_insert_range(RVector *vec, size_t index, void *first, size_t count);
functions.description: Inserts count consecutive elements starting at index. first points to the start of the source range containing count elements, each of size vec->elem_size. Returns a pointer into the vector to the first inserted element (may be invalidated by reallocation).
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector.
index must satisfy 0 <= index <= vec->len.
If count > 0, first must be a non-NULL pointer to at least count * vec->elem_size bytes.
May reallocate internal storage; previously held internal pointers may be invalidated.

functions.name: r_vector_pop
functions.description: Removes the last element and writes its raw bytes into into. Equivalent to r_vector_remove_at(vec, vec->len - 1, into). Capacity is not reduced.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector with vec->len > 0.
into must point to writable storage of at least vec->elem_size bytes (whether NULL is allowed to discard data is not specified).

functions.name: r_vector_pop_front
functions.description: Removes the first element and writes its raw bytes into into. Equivalent to r_vector_remove_at(vec, 0, into). Capacity is not reduced.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector with vec->len > 0.
into must point to writable storage of at least vec->elem_size bytes (whether NULL is allowed to discard data is not specified).

functions.name: r_vector_push
functions.description: Appends a new element to the end of the vector. x points to the actual data to copy (size vec->elem_size). Returns a pointer to the stored element (may be invalidated by future reallocations).
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector.
x must be a non-NULL pointer to at least vec->elem_size bytes.
May reallocate internal storage; previously held internal pointers may be invalidated.

functions.name: r_vector_push_front
functions.description: Inserts a new element at the beginning of the vector, shifting existing elements up. x points to the actual data to copy (size vec->elem_size). Returns a pointer to the stored element (may be invalidated by reallocation).
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector.
x must be a non-NULL pointer to at least vec->elem_size bytes.
May reallocate internal storage; previously held internal pointers may be invalidated.

functions.name: r_vector_reserve
functions.description: Ensures the vector’s capacity is at least capacity. May reallocate the internal buffer. Returns a pointer (to internal storage) for convenience.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector.
capacity may be any value; if less than current capacity, capacity is unchanged; if greater, internal storage may be reallocated.
Any previously obtained internal pointers may become invalid after this call.

functions.name: r_vector_shrink
functions.description: Reduces the vector’s capacity to exactly its current length (len). May reallocate the internal buffer. Returns a pointer (to internal storage) for convenience.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector.
May reallocate; previously obtained internal pointers may be invalidated.

functions.name: r_vector_flush
functions.description: Function present but not documented in this header. Likely related to resetting or exposing internal storage; specifics (effects on len/capacity/elements and whether free callbacks are invoked) are unknown.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RVector.
Return value and side effects are unknown; caller must consult implementation or higher-level documentation before use.

functions.name: r_pvector_init
functions.description: Initializes an RPVector (a vector specialized for void* elements) with an optional per-element free callback that takes the stored pointer.
requirements: vec must be a valid, writable RPVector pointer.
If free is provided, it must be callable as free(element_ptr).
Do not reinitialize without finalizing first.

functions.name: r_pvector_fini
functions.description: Finalizes an RPVector: calls the registered free callback on each stored pointer (if set) and clears the vector. Does not free the RPVector struct itself.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RPVector.
Element free (if set) must be safe to call once for each element.

functions.name: r_pvector_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a heap-allocated RPVector initialized to store void* pointers with an optional per-element free callback.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL on allocation failure.
If free is provided, it must be callable as free(element_ptr).
Free with r_pvector_free() when done.

functions.name: r_pvector_new_with_len
functions.description: Allocates and returns a heap-allocated RPVector, with behavior parameterized by length. The header does not specify whether length refers to initial length, capacity, or pre-filled entries; details are unknown.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL on allocation failure.
If free is provided, it must be callable as free(element_ptr).
Semantics of the length parameter are unknown from this header; consult implementation/documentation before relying on it.

functions.name: r_pvector_clear
functions.description: Clears the RPVector and calls vec->v.free on every element (i.e., the registered RPVectorFree callback is invoked for each stored pointer). Capacity is not reduced.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RPVector.
Element free (if set) must be safe to call once for each element.
Capacity is unchanged; call r_pvector_shrink() to reduce capacity if desired.

functions.name: r_pvector_free
functions.description: Frees an RPVector after calling its per-element free callback (if set) on all elements. Deallocates the vector object itself.
requirements: vec must be either NULL or a valid, initialized RPVector pointer allocated compatibly with this API.
Do not use vec after this call.
Element free (if set) must be safe to call once for each element.

functions.name: r_pvector_contains
functions.description: Searches for pointer x in the RPVector. Returns a pointer to the internal slot (void**) if found, or NULL otherwise.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RPVector.
x may be any pointer value; comparison semantics appear to be by pointer equality (no comparator is provided).
Returned pointer refers to internal storage and may be invalidated by mutations that reallocate.

functions.name: r_pvector_remove_at
functions.description: Removes and returns the pointer stored at index. Does not call the free callback for the removed element.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RPVector with vec->v.len > 0.
index must satisfy 0 <= index < vec->v.len.
Caller becomes responsible for the removed pointer’s lifetime (no free callback is invoked).
Capacity is not reduced.

functions.name: r_pvector_remove_data
functions.description: Removes the element equal to pointer x if present. Does not call the free callback for the removed element.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RPVector.
x is compared by pointer identity (implied; no comparator passed).
No effect if x is not present.
Caller is responsible for freeing x if needed since the callback is not invoked.

functions.name: r_pvector_pop
functions.description: Removes and returns the last pointer in the RPVector. Does not call the free callback.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RPVector with vec->v.len > 0.
Caller is responsible for the returned pointer’s lifetime.

functions.name: r_pvector_pop_front
functions.description: Removes and returns the first pointer in the RPVector. Does not call the free callback.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RPVector with vec->v.len > 0.
Caller is responsible for the returned pointer’s lifetime.

functions.name: r_pvector_sort
functions.description: Sorts the RPVector in place using quicksort and the provided comparator. Comparator receives two const void* element pointers to compare (as stored in the vector).
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RPVector.
cmp must be a valid function pointer implementing a total/strict-weak ordering compatible with the stored pointer values.
Comparator must be safe to call multiple times and must return negative/zero/positive according to ordering.

functions.name: r_pvector_bsearch
functions.signature: R_API int r_pvector_bsearch(RPVector *vec, void *needle, RPVectorComparator cmp);
functions.description: Performs a binary search for needle in a sorted RPVector using the provided comparator. Returns an int (likely the index) but the exact return convention (e.g., -1 if not found) is not specified in this header.
requirements: vec must be a valid, initialized RPVector.
The vector must already be sorted according to cmp (as per comment).
cmp must be a valid comparator that is consistent with the vector’s sort order.
Return value semantics beyond being an int are unspecified in this header; caller must check implementation or higher-level docs.

functions.name: r_list_new
functions.description: Allocate and return a new, empty RList with default settings. Use when you need a standalone list instance.
requirements: Caller must free the list with r_list_free when done to avoid memory leaks.
Returned list is empty and must be populated via r_list_append/r_list_prepend/etc before use.

functions.name: r_list_newf
functions.description: Allocate and return a new RList with a per-item free callback set. The free callback is used by list-cleanup operations to release element payloads.
requirements: Parameter f is a function pointer of type void (*)(void *) and will be called on each element's data during purging/freeing/deletion operations that release elements.
Caller must free the list with r_list_free when done to avoid memory leaks.

functions.name: r_list_iter_get_next
functions.description: Return the next iterator node after the given iterator node in the list, or possibly NULL at the end.
requirements: Parameter list must be a valid RListIter obtained from this API (e.g., from list->head, r_list_append, r_list_get_nth, etc.).

functions.name: r_list_iter_get_prev
functions.description: Return the previous iterator node before the given iterator node in the list, or possibly NULL at the beginning.
requirements: Parameter list must be a valid RListIter obtained from this API.

functions.name: r_list_set_n
functions.description: Set/replace the data pointer at index n in the list to p. Returns an int status (exact semantics not documented).
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
n must be within the valid index range of the list (0 <= n < r_list_length(list)).
Indexing is zero-based (inferred from common C list conventions; exact base unspecified).
p is stored as-is; ownership and lifetime management of p are caller-defined except when a free callback is configured.

functions.name: r_list_iter_get_data
functions.description: Return the data pointer stored in the given iterator node.
requirements: list must be a valid RListIter.

functions.name: r_list_append
functions.description: Append a new node containing data to the end of the list and return the iterator for the new node.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
data is stored as-is; the list does not copy it.
If a free callback is set on list, it may be used later to free data when the node is removed or the list is purged/freed.

functions.name: r_list_prepend
functions.description: Prepend a new node containing data to the start of the list and return the iterator for the new node.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
data is stored as-is; the list does not copy it.
If a free callback is set on list, it may be used later to free data when the node is removed or the list is purged/freed.

functions.name: r_list_insert
functions.description: Insert a new node with data at position n within the list (between existing nodes) and return its iterator.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
n must be within or at the boundary of the list size (exact insertion semantics at bounds are not documented).
data is stored as-is; the list does not copy it.

functions.name: r_list_length
functions.description: Return the number of elements currently stored in the list.
requirements: list must be a valid RList pointer (const).

functions.name: r_list_iter_length
functions.description: Return a length/count related to the iterator region (likely the number of nodes from iter to the end). Exact semantics are not documented in the header.
requirements: iter must be a valid RListIter.

functions.name: r_list_first
functions.description: Return the data pointer stored in the first element of the list, or possibly NULL if empty.
requirements: list must be a valid RList pointer (const).

functions.name: r_list_last
functions.description: Return the data pointer stored in the last element of the list, or possibly NULL if empty.
requirements: list must be a valid RList pointer (const).

functions.name: r_list_add_sorted
functions.description: Insert data into the list according to the provided comparator so that the list remains sorted. Returns the iterator for the inserted node.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
cmp must implement a strict weak ordering and return -1, 0, or 1 indicating a<b, a==b, a>b (as documented in the header).
data is stored as-is; the list does not copy it.
All existing and new elements must be comparable by cmp.

functions.name: r_list_sort
functions.description: Sort the list in-place using the provided comparator.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
cmp must return -1, 0, or 1 indicating ordering (as documented).
All list elements must be mutually comparable by cmp.

functions.name: r_list_sort_with_user
functions.description: Sort the list in-place using a comparator that receives an extra user pointer.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
cmp must implement ordering and return -1, 0, or 1.
The comparator must tolerate being called with the provided user pointer.

functions.name: r_list_merge_sort
functions.description: Sort the list in-place using a merge sort algorithm and the provided comparator.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
cmp must return -1, 0, or 1 indicating ordering.
All elements must be comparable by cmp.

functions.name: r_list_merge_sort_with_user
functions.description: Sort the list in-place using merge sort with a comparator that receives an extra user pointer.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
cmp must return -1, 0, or 1 indicating ordering.
The comparator must tolerate being called with the provided user pointer.

functions.name: r_list_insertion_sort
functions.description: Sort the list in-place using an insertion sort algorithm and the provided comparator.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
cmp must return -1, 0, or 1 indicating ordering.
All elements must be comparable by cmp.

functions.name: r_list_insertion_sort_with_user
functions.description: Sort the list in-place using insertion sort with a comparator that receives an extra user pointer.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
cmp must return -1, 0, or 1 indicating ordering.
The comparator must tolerate being called with the provided user pointer.

functions.name: r_list_uniq
functions.description: Create and return a new list with duplicate elements removed, using cmp to map each element to a ut64 key for uniqueness. The original list is not modified.
requirements: list must be a valid RList pointer (const).
cmp must return a ut64 key representing the element for uniqueness comparisons.
Caller must free the returned list with r_list_free.

functions.name: r_list_uniq_inplace
functions.description: Remove duplicate elements from the list in-place, using cmp to map each element to a ut64 key. Returns an int status/count (exact semantics not documented).
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
cmp must return a ut64 key representing the element for uniqueness comparisons.

functions.name: r_list_init
functions.description: Initialize a pre-allocated RList structure to an empty list with default settings. Use when embedding RList in other structs or on the stack.
requirements: list must point to valid, writable memory large enough for an RList instance.
After initialization, manage lifetime manually and call r_list_free or r_list_purge as appropriate before discarding, depending on allocation model (exact obligations not documented).

functions.name: r_list_delete
functions.description: Remove the node referred to by iter from the list. If a free callback is set, it may be invoked on the node's data.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
iter must be a valid iterator currently belonging to list.

functions.name: r_list_delete_data
functions.description: Search the list for a node whose data equals ptr and delete it. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
ptr is compared by pointer equality unless implementation specifies otherwise (not documented).
If a free callback is set on list, it may be invoked on the removed data.

functions.name: r_list_iter_init
functions.description: Initialize an iterator structure for use with the given list. Exact post-conditions (e.g., where iter points) are not specified in the header.
requirements: iter must point to valid, writable memory sized for RListIter.
list must be a valid, initialized RList.

functions.name: r_list_purge
functions.description: Remove all nodes from the list, applying the list's free callback to each element's data if set, leaving the list empty but still usable.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.

functions.name: r_list_free
functions.description: Free the entire list structure and its nodes. If a free callback is set, it may be applied to each element's data before nodes are released.
requirements: list must be a valid RList pointer or NULL. If non-NULL, it must be a list created/initialized by this API.
After calling, the list pointer becomes invalid; do not use it.

functions.name: r_list_item_new
functions.description: Allocate and return a new list node (iterator) containing the provided data, not yet linked into any list.
requirements: data is stored as-is; ownership is managed by caller/list policies.
The returned node must be later inserted/linked into a list by appropriate functions (not documented here).
Caller is responsible for freeing the node through list APIs that link and manage nodes; standalone node freeing semantics are not documented.

functions.name: r_list_split
functions.description: Split the list around the node whose data equals ptr. Exact split behavior (before/after, left/right lists) is not documented in the header.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
ptr should refer to a data pointer present in the list; behavior is unspecified if not found.

functions.name: r_list_split_iter
functions.description: Split the list at the position indicated by iter. Exact resulting list arrangement is not documented in the header.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
iter must be a valid iterator that belongs to list.

functions.name: r_list_join
functions.description: Join/concatenate list2 into list1. Returns an int status/count (exact semantics not documented).
requirements: list1 and list2 must be valid, initialized RList instances.
Ownership/emptiness of list2 after the operation is not documented; caller must consult implementation for whether list2 remains usable.

functions.name: r_list_get_n
functions.description: Return the data pointer at index n in the list, or possibly NULL if out of range.
requirements: list must be a valid RList pointer (const).
n must be within valid bounds (0 <= n < r_list_length(list)); out-of-range behavior may be NULL return (not guaranteed).

functions.name: r_list_get_nth
functions.description: Return the iterator node at index n in the list, or possibly NULL if out of range.
requirements: list must be a valid RList pointer (const).
n must be within valid bounds (0 <= n < r_list_length(list)).

functions.name: r_list_del_n
functions.description: Delete the node at index n in the list. Returns an int status (exact semantics not documented).
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
n must be within valid bounds (0 <= n < r_list_length(list)).
If a free callback is set on list, it may be invoked on the removed element's data.

functions.name: r_list_iter_to_top
functions.description: Move the node referenced by iter to the head (top) of the list.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
iter must be a valid iterator currently belonging to list.

functions.name: r_list_pop
functions.description: Remove and return an element from the list (likely the last element). Exact end/pop side is not specified in the header.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.

functions.name: r_list_pop_head
functions.description: Remove and return the first element's data from the list.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.

functions.name: r_list_reverse
functions.description: Reverse the order of nodes in the list in-place.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.

functions.name: r_list_clone
functions.description: Create and return a new list cloned from the given list. The clone callback is used to duplicate each element's data.
requirements: list must be a valid RList pointer (const).
clone must be a function pointer of type void *(*)(void *) that returns a newly created copy of the provided element data (or a suitable representation).
Caller must free the returned list with r_list_free.

functions.name: r_list_to_str
functions.description: Serialize/concatenate the list elements into a string, likely joining by the delimiter character ch. Exact formatting and element-to-string conversion are not documented.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized RList.
Elements should be convertible to a string representation understood by this function (not documented).
Caller is likely responsible for freeing the returned string; ownership is not explicitly documented.

functions.name: r_list_contains
functions.description: Check whether the list contains an element whose data equals p and return its iterator if found, otherwise possibly NULL.
requirements: list must be a valid RList pointer (const).
Comparison is by pointer equality unless otherwise defined (not documented).

functions.name: r_list_find
functions.signature: RListIter *r_list_find(const RList *list, const void *p, RListComparator cmp);
functions.description: Find an element in the list using a comparator and return its iterator if found, otherwise possibly NULL. The comparator compares p with each element's data.
requirements: list must be a valid RList pointer (const).
cmp must return -1, 0, or 1 indicating ordering/equality; this function likely treats 0 as equality.
p must be a pointer meaningful to cmp with respect to list elements.

functions.name: r_regex_run
functions.signature: int r_regex_run(const char *pattern, const char *flags, const char *text);
functions.description: Compiles and runs a regular expression specified by pattern against the given text with the provided flags string. Returns an integer status code (exact semantics not documented here). Likely a convenience helper that combines compile and execute steps.
requirements: pattern must be a valid regular expression string compatible with this library’s syntax (unknown exact syntax; likely POSIX-like given flag names).
flags is a C-string that encodes compilation and/or execution options; its expected format is unspecified here (use r_regex_flags if available to parse).
text must be a valid, null-terminated C-string to be matched.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown.
Return value semantics are unspecified; caller should treat nonzero as error or non-match depending on library convention (unknown).

functions.name: r_regex_match
functions.signature: bool r_regex_match(const char *pattern, const char *flags, const char *text);
functions.description: Convenience function that tests whether text matches pattern using options provided by flags. Returns true on match, false otherwise.
requirements: pattern must be a valid regex string.
flags is a C-string encoding options; accepted format is unspecified here.
text must be a valid, null-terminated C-string.

functions.name: r_regex_flags
functions.description: Parses a flags string into a bitmask of R_REGEX_* options suitable for compilation/execution. Returns the combined bitwise OR of flags; error reporting for invalid flags is unspecified.
requirements: flags must be a null-terminated C-string. Its accepted characters/format are not documented here.
Returned bitmask corresponds to macros defined in this header (e.g., R_REGEX_EXTENDED, R_REGEX_ICASE, etc.).
Behavior on NULL or unknown flag tokens is unspecified.

functions.name: r_regex_new
functions.description: Allocates and compiles a new RRegex object from pattern using options provided via the cflags string. Returns a pointer to a compiled regex object or NULL on failure (exact failure conditions unspecified).
requirements: pattern must be a valid regex string.
cflags is a null-terminated string of options; its exact format is unspecified.
Caller owns the returned RRegex* and must release it with r_regex_free when no longer needed.
Not safe to use the returned pointer after r_regex_free or r_regex_fini.

functions.name: r_regex_free
functions.description: Frees and releases all resources associated with an RRegex object allocated by r_regex_new. After this call, the pointer must not be used.
requirements: The argument must be a pointer previously returned by r_regex_new (or otherwise heap-allocated RRegex compatible with this free routine).
Passing an invalid or already-freed pointer results in undefined behavior (unspecified).
After calling, the RRegex pointer becomes invalid; do not use it.

functions.name: r_regex_init
functions.signature: int r_regex_init(RRegex *regex, const char *pattern, int flags);
functions.description: Initializes an existing RRegex structure to compile the given pattern using the provided bitmask flags (R_REGEX_*). Intended for stack- or externally-managed RRegex objects.
requirements: regex must point to a valid, writable RRegex struct.
pattern must be a valid regex string.
flags must be a bitwise OR of supported R_REGEX_* macros defined in this header.
On success returns 0 or a non-negative code (exact convention unspecified); on failure returns an error code (e.g., R_REGEX_* constants), but exact mapping is unspecified.
If initialization fails, the state of regex is unspecified; caller should handle error and avoid use until successfully initialized.

functions.name: r_regex_fini
functions.description: Finalizes an RRegex previously initialized with r_regex_init, releasing any resources held inside but not freeing the RRegex storage itself.
requirements: Argument must be a pointer to an RRegex that was previously initialized with r_regex_init (and not yet finalized).
After calling, the RRegex contents should not be used unless re-initialized.
Do not pass an RRegex that was allocated with r_regex_new and not intended for fini (unless the library allows both); exact interplay between free and fini is unspecified.

functions.name: r_regex_check
functions.description: Checks whether the compiled regex rr matches the given string str. Returns true on match, false otherwise.
requirements: rr must point to a compiled/initialized RRegex (via r_regex_new or r_regex_init).
str must be a valid, null-terminated C-string.
rr must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: r_regex_exec
functions.signature: int r_regex_exec(const RRegex *preg, const char *string, size_t nmatch, RRegexMatch pmatch[], int eflags);
functions.description: Executes the compiled regular expression preg against string, optionally capturing up to nmatch submatches into pmatch. eflags modifies execution behavior using R_REGEX_* execution flags. Returns an integer status code (likely 0 on success and error codes on failure/non-match, following POSIX-like conventions; exact values not fully specified).
requirements: preg must point to a valid, compiled RRegex.
string must be a valid, null-terminated C-string to match against.
If nmatch > 0, pmatch must be a valid array with at least nmatch elements; if nmatch == 0, pmatch may be NULL.
Each RRegexMatch element, on successful match, will receive rm_so and rm_eo offsets (semantics follow typical POSIX regexec; exact details not guaranteed here).
eflags must be a bitwise OR of execution flags defined in this header (e.g., R_REGEX_NOTBOL, R_REGEX_NOTEOL, R_REGEX_STARTEND, etc.).
If R_REGEX_STARTEND is used, requirements on initial contents of pmatch[0] (e.g., input range) are not specified here; consult implementation if needed.

functions.name: r_regex_match_list
functions.description: Returns a list of matches for the compiled regex rx applied to text. The exact type of list elements (e.g., strings, ranges, or RRegexMatch objects) is not documented here.
requirements: rx must be a valid, compiled RRegex.
text must be a valid, null-terminated C-string.
Returned RList ownership and element ownership/lifetime are unspecified; caller must consult implementation to free correctly.

functions.name: r_regex_error
functions.description: Produces a human-readable error message string for the given errcode in the context of rx. Useful for translating R_REGEX_* error codes to text. Memory ownership/lifetime of the returned string is not specified.
requirements: rx must be a valid RRegex pointer (compiled or not; exact requirement unspecified).
errcode should be one of the error codes defined in this header (e.g., R_REGEX_NOMATCH, R_REGEX_BADPAT, etc.), though other values may be accepted.
Ownership and mutability of the returned char* are unspecified; treat as read-only and do not free unless implementation documentation specifies otherwise.

functions.name: r_getopt_init
functions.signature: void r_getopt_init(RGetopt *go, int argc, const char **argv, const char *ostr);
functions.description: Initializes a getopt-like parser state in the provided RGetopt structure. Call this once before iterating options with r_getopt_next. It binds the argc/argv pair and the option-specification string (ostr) to the parser and resets internal indices/fields (such as current index and argument pointer) so option scanning can begin. Typical usage mirrors POSIX/BSD getopt: ostr lists valid option letters, with a colon after an option to indicate a required argument, though exact option-spec syntax is not guaranteed by this header.
requirements: go must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable RGetopt storage.
argc should be >= 0 and correspond to the number of elements accessible through argv.
argv must be a valid pointer to an array of at least argc pointers to NUL-terminated C strings; all pointed-to strings and the array must remain valid for the duration of option parsing.

ostr must be a non-null pointer to a NUL-terminated string describing the accepted options; it must remain valid for the duration of option parsing. The precise option-spec format is not specified here (commonly: letters; a trailing ':' on a letter means that option requires an argument).
This function must be called before the first call to r_getopt_next for a given RGetopt instance.
The RGetopt instance and the provided argv/ostr must remain valid and unmodified (other than through r_getopt_*) while parsing proceeds.

functions.name: r_getopt_next
functions.description: Advances the getopt-like parser to the next option according to the state initialized by r_getopt_init. On each call it parses the next option from the bound argv, updates fields in the RGetopt object (e.g., current index, option character, and option argument pointer), and returns a code indicating what was found. By convention with getopt-style APIs, this typically returns the option character on success, -1 when no more options remain, and a special value (often '?') on an unrecognized/invalid option, but the exact return codes are not specified in this header. The RGetopt fields such as arg, ind, and opt are intended for the caller to read after each call.
requirements: opt must be a valid, non-null pointer to an RGetopt previously initialized with r_getopt_init.
The argv and ostr provided at initialization must still be valid for the entire iteration period.
Call repeatedly to consume options until the function indicates completion (commonly by returning -1; exact sentinel is not documented here).

After each successful parse, read results from the RGetopt fields (e.g., opt->arg for an option’s argument, opt->ind for the next argv index); do not modify internal traversal state (e.g., opt->place) between calls.
The caller must handle and check the return value each call to detect end-of-options and any parse errors; specific error codes are not documented here and may follow getopt conventions (e.g., '?').

functions.name: r_lz4_compress
functions.signature: int r_lz4_compress(ut8 *obuf, ut8 *buf, size_t buf_size, const int max_chain);
functions.description: Compresses the input buffer using an LZ4-compatible algorithm, writing the compressed data to the provided output buffer. Intended for callers that manage both input and output buffers. The max_chain parameter likely controls search depth/effort in the compressor; exact semantics are not documented here. Return value semantics are not documented in this header (typically a non-negative compressed length on success, or a negative/error code on failure), so callers should check for failure according to their build’s implementation.
requirements: obuf must point to a valid, writable buffer large enough to hold the compressed output; required capacity is not specified here (LZ4 worst-case is typically larger than input; exact bound unknown from this header).
buf must point to a valid, readable buffer containing at least buf_size bytes.
buf_size must correctly reflect the number of readable bytes in buf.
max_chain should be a non-negative integer (inferred from common compressor parameters; exact valid range is not documented).
Behavior and exact return value/error conventions are not documented in this header; callers must consult implementation or test for specifics.

functions.name: r_lz4_decompress

functions.name: r_arch_platform_unset
functions.description: Removes/unsets a named platform setting from the given RArch instance. Returns a char* related to the unset operation (exact semantics/ownership not documented here; may be the previous value or a status string). Usage: call to clear a platform-specific override before reconfiguring the architecture. Notes: ownership and lifetime of the returned string are unknown from this header.
requirements: arch must be a valid, initialized RArch* (e.g., from r_arch_new).
name should be a valid C string identifying a platform setting; NULL-handling is unspecified.
Callers must not assume ownership or lifetime of the returned char* without consulting implementation/documentation (unknown).

functions.name: r_arch_platform_set
functions.description: Sets a named platform setting on the given RArch instance. Returns a char* related to the operation (exact semantics/ownership not documented here). Usage: call to select or override the active platform for decoding/encoding. Notes: how the name is parsed and what is returned are unspecified in this header.
requirements: arch must be a valid, initialized RArch*.
name must be a valid, non-NULL C string naming the platform to set (NULL-handling unspecified).
Ownership/lifetime of the returned char* are unknown; do not free unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: r_arch_platform_list
functions.description: Lists platform settings associated with the given RArch instance. Expected usage: display or enumerate available/active platforms. Notes: Side effects (printing vs. callback/list return) are not described here.
requirements: arch must be a valid, initialized RArch*.
No return value; callers should expect side effects (unspecified).

functions.name: r_arch_load_decoder
functions.description: Loads a decoder identified by dname into the RArch instance without switching to it. Usage: preload a decoder by name; pass NULL to refer to the current decoder (per comment).
requirements: arch must be a valid, initialized RArch*.
dname is the name of the decoder to load; passing NULL refers to the current decoder (per header comment).
Returns true on success, false on failure; callers should check the return value.

functions.name: r_arch_use_decoder
functions.description: Selects/activates a decoder by name for the given RArch instance. Usage: switch the active decoder implementation.
requirements: arch must be a valid, initialized RArch*.
dname should be the name of a previously available/known decoder; behavior for NULL is not documented here.
Check the boolean return value for success/failure.

functions.name: r_arch_unload_decoder
functions.description: Unloads a decoder identified by dname from the RArch instance. Usage: free/disable decoders that are no longer needed.
requirements: arch must be a valid, initialized RArch*.
dname should be a valid decoder name; passing NULL semantics are not specified.
Returns true on success; callers must check for false on failure.

functions.name: r_arch_info
functions.description: Deprecated. Queries architecture information values for the given RArch. Usage: pass a query code (e.g., R_ARCH_INFO_MINOP_SIZE, R_ARCH_INFO_MAXOP_SIZE, alignment constants, flags) to retrieve an integer property.
requirements: arch must be a valid, initialized RArch*.
query should be one of the defined R_ARCH_INFO_* constants.
Callers must interpret the returned int according to the query; negative/error codes are not documented.

functions.name: r_arch_decode
functions.signature: R_API bool r_arch_decode(RArch *a, RAnalOp *op, RArchDecodeMask mask);
functions.description: Deprecated. Decodes a single instruction into the provided RAnalOp based on the active architecture/decoder. The mask controls which analysis fields are filled (basic, ESIL, value info, hints, opex, disassembly).
requirements: a must be a valid, initialized RArch*.
op must point to a valid RAnalOp structure prepared with the necessary input (e.g., address and buffer) as required by the implementation (exact fields unspecified here).
mask is a bitmask of R_ARCH_OP_MASK_* values; use R_ARCH_OP_MASK_ALL to request all available info.
Returns true on successful decode; callers must handle false (e.g., invalid/unsupported instruction).

functions.name: r_arch_encode
functions.signature: R_API bool r_arch_encode(RArch *a, RAnalOp *op, RArchEncodeMask mask);
functions.description: Deprecated. Encodes an instruction from the information in RAnalOp for the active architecture/encoder. The mask can control encoding options (unspecified).
requirements: a must be a valid, initialized RArch*.
op must be a valid RAnalOp with fields populated for encoding (exact requirements unspecified).
mask is an implementation-defined bitmask (typedef RArchEncodeMask).
Returns true on success; false indicates encoding failure.

functions.name: r_arch_esilcb
functions.description: Invokes an ESIL-related callback on the active architecture with the given action (init, maps, reset, fini). Useful to integrate ESIL lifecycle with an RArch instance.
requirements: a must be a valid, initialized RArch*.
action must be a valid RArchEsilAction value (e.g., R_ARCH_ESIL_ACTION_INIT, MAPS, RESET, FINI).
Check the boolean return value for success.

functions.name: r_arch_session
functions.description: Creates an RArchSession bound to an RArch, with the provided configuration and optional explicit plugin. Use sessions to isolate per-decoder state and configuration.
requirements: arch must be a valid, initialized RArch*.
cfg should be a valid RArchConfig* (created via r_arch_config_new/clone) or NULL if permitted by implementation (unspecified).
ap may specify the plugin to use; passing NULL uses the decoder selected in arch (implementation-dependent).
Returns a new RArchSession* on success; NULL on failure.

functions.name: r_arch_session_decode
functions.signature: R_API bool r_arch_session_decode(RArchSession *as, RAnalOp *op, RArchDecodeMask mask);
functions.description: Decodes an instruction using a specific RArchSession. The mask selects which analysis details to populate in op.
requirements: as must be a valid RArchSession*, created by r_arch_session.
op must be a valid RAnalOp with required input fields set (exact requirements unspecified).
mask is a bitmask of R_ARCH_OP_MASK_* values.
Returns true on success; false on decode failure.

functions.name: r_arch_session_encode
functions.signature: R_API bool r_arch_session_encode(RArchSession *as, RAnalOp *op, RArchEncodeMask mask);
functions.description: Encodes an instruction using a specific RArchSession from the data in RAnalOp. Mask controls encoding options (unspecified).
requirements: as must be a valid RArchSession*.
op must be a valid RAnalOp prepared for encoding (exact fields unspecified).
mask is an implementation-defined bitmask.
Returns true on success; false on failure.

functions.name: r_arch_session_patch

functions.description: Applies a modification/patch to an instruction or buffer represented by RAnalOp using the session. Mask controls modification options (unspecified).
requirements: as must be a valid RArchSession*.
op must be a valid RAnalOp describing the target of the patch (details unspecified).
mask is a bitmask (typedef RArchModifyMask).
Returns true on success; false on failure.

functions.name: r_arch_session_info

requirements: as must be a valid RArchSession*.
q is an integer query code; expected to match the same R_ARCH_INFO_* constants or implementation-defined values (unspecified).
Callers should interpret the returned int per the query; error codes are unspecified.

functions.name: r_arch_session_preludes

Caller must check for NULL return on failure.

requirements: a must be a valid RAsm* with a parser/filter plugins available.
data must be a valid, null-terminated string.
f and hint may be NULL if not available (behavior not specified in header).
addr provides the address context for relative substitutions and should be set to the intended instruction address.
Caller must check for NULL return on failure.
Ownership of the returned string is unknown from this header (unknown).
