functions.name: r_fs_shell_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new RFSShell structure, zero-initialized (via R_NEW0). Intended to be paired with r_fs_shell_free for cleanup.
requirements: Call r_fs_shell_free to release the returned RFSShell when no longer needed.
The returned pointer may be NULL on allocation failure; callers should check the result before use.

functions.name: r_fs_shell_free
functions.description: Frees an RFSShell previously created by r_fs_shell_new, releasing s->cwd and the RFSShell itself.
requirements: s must be a pointer obtained from r_fs_shell_new (or otherwise compatible with the expected layout).
s may be NULL-unsafe per the inline body; caller must ensure s is non-NULL before calling.
After calling, the pointer must not be used again.

functions.name: r_fs_new
functions.description: Creates and returns a new RFS (filesystem manager) instance, initializing internal bindings, plugin/root lists, and state as required by the library.
requirements: Caller must free the returned RFS with r_fs_free.
Caller should check for NULL in case allocation or initialization fails before using the instance.

functions.name: r_fs_free
functions.description: Frees an RFS instance created by r_fs_new and any resources owned by it.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS pointer previously created by r_fs_new.
fs must not be used after this call.
If there are mounted roots or open files, library-specific behavior is unknown; callers should ensure proper teardown (e.g., umount/close) before freeing if required by implementation.

functions.name: r_fs_view
functions.description: Sets the active view/filter for directory listings or operations, using R_FS_VIEW_* flags (NORMAL, DELETED, SPECIAL, ALL).
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS pointer.
view should be one of the defined R_FS_VIEW_* values (R_FS_VIEW_NORMAL, R_FS_VIEW_DELETED, R_FS_VIEW_SPECIAL, or R_FS_VIEW_ALL).

functions.name: r_fs_plugin_add
functions.description: Registers an RFSPlugin with the RFS instance so it can handle filesystem operations for supported paths/types.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
p must point to a properly initialized RFSPlugin with function pointers consistent with its expectations.

functions.name: r_fs_plugin_remove
functions.description: Unregisters a previously added RFSPlugin from the RFS instance.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
p must be a plugin that was previously added to fs via r_fs_plugin_add.

functions.name: r_fs_del
functions.description: Deletes/unlinks the specified plugin from the RFS, similar to removing it from the internal plugin list.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
p should reference an RFSPlugin known to fs.

functions.name: r_fs_mount
functions.signature: RFSRoot *r_fs_mount(RFS *fs, const char *fstype, const char *path, ut64 delta)
functions.description: Mounts a filesystem of type fstype at the given path within the RFS, with an optional offset/delta, returning an RFSRoot handle.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
fstype must be a non-NULL string matching a registered plugin type.
path must be a non-NULL mount path string.
Caller should check the return value for NULL to detect failure.
The returned RFSRoot must eventually be released via r_fs_root_free or r_fs_umount depending on the API’s ownership rules.

functions.name: r_fs_umount
functions.description: Unmounts a previously mounted filesystem root at the specified path.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
path must be a non-NULL string referring to a mount that exists in fs.

functions.name: r_fs_open
functions.description: Opens a file at path within the mounted filesystems managed by fs. If create is true, the file may be created if it does not exist (plugin-dependent). Returns an RFSFile handle.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
path must be a non-NULL, valid path string within a mounted root.
Call r_fs_close to release the returned RFSFile when finished.
Caller should check for NULL to detect open/creation failure.

functions.name: r_fs_close
functions.description: Closes an open RFSFile handle and releases associated resources.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
file must be a valid RFSFile previously returned by r_fs_open or related functions.
After closing, file must not be used again.

functions.name: r_fs_read
functions.signature: int r_fs_read(RFS *fs, RFSFile *file, ut64 addr, int len)
functions.description: Reads up to len bytes from the file starting at offset addr using the responsible plugin. Returns the number of bytes read or a negative value on error (plugin-dependent).
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
file must be a valid, opened RFSFile.
len should be >= 0.
addr is an unsigned 64-bit offset within the file or filesystem space; exact bounds behavior is plugin-specific.
Caller should handle partial reads and negative return values as errors.

functions.name: r_fs_write
functions.signature: int r_fs_write(RFS *fs, RFSFile *file, ut64 addr, const ut8 *data, int len)
functions.description: Writes len bytes from data to the file at offset addr. Returns the number of bytes written or a negative value on error (plugin-dependent).
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
file must be a valid, opened RFSFile with write permissions as enforced by the plugin.
data must be a non-NULL pointer when len > 0.
len should be >= 0.
addr is an unsigned 64-bit offset; bounds and permissions are plugin-specific.
Caller should handle partial writes and negative return values as errors.

functions.name: r_fs_slurp
functions.description: Loads the contents and metadata of the file at path into an RFSFile structure (conventionally a whole-file read/"slurp").
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
path must be a non-NULL, valid path string.
Caller should check for NULL to detect failure.
The returned RFSFile must be released with r_fs_close or r_fs_file_free depending on implementation; consult plugin semantics.

functions.name: r_fs_dir
functions.description: Returns a directory listing for the given path as an RList (list of entries, typically RFSFile or plugin-specific structs).
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
path must be a non-NULL path string within a mounted root.
Caller should check the return value for NULL to detect failure.
Ownership and element types of the returned list are plugin-specific; caller must follow library conventions when freeing.

functions.name: r_fs_dir_dump
functions.signature: bool r_fs_dir_dump(RFS *fs, const char *path, const char *name)
functions.description: Dumps or exports a directory (path) to a destination identified by name (plugin-specific behavior). Returns true on success.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
path must be a non-NULL path string.
name must be a non-NULL destination identifier or filename, depending on plugin behavior.

functions.name: r_fs_mkdir
functions.description: Creates a directory at the specified path within the mounted filesystem(s).
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
path must be a non-NULL, valid path string.
Directory creation semantics (intermediate dirs, permissions) are plugin-specific.

functions.name: r_fs_find_name
functions.description: Searches for files/directories matching name and/or glob patterns and returns results in an RList.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
name may be NULL or non-NULL depending on usage; glob may be a glob-style pattern string; exact matching semantics are unspecified and plugin-specific.
Caller must check for NULL return on failure and manage/free the returned list per library conventions.

functions.name: r_fs_find_off
functions.description: Searches for filesystem entries associated with a specific offset off, optionally filtered by name. Returns an RList of matches.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
name may be NULL or a filter; exact semantics are unspecified.
Caller must check for NULL return on failure and free the returned list according to library conventions.

functions.name: r_fs_partitions
functions.description: Enumerates partitions of type ptype with an optional offset delta, returning an RList of RFSPartition entries.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
ptype should match a known partition type name (plugin/registry specific).
Caller must check for NULL return and free the returned list per library conventions.

functions.name: r_fs_type_index
functions.description: Returns information about a filesystem type by index i, as a pointer to a constant RFSType entry. Marked R_MUSTUSE indicating callers should not ignore the return value.
requirements: i must be a valid index within the available filesystem type table; out-of-range behavior is unspecified.
Caller must not modify the returned RFSType.

functions.name: r_fs_name
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated string naming the filesystem or entry at a given offset, or similar context-derived name.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
Caller must free the returned string when done.
Caller should handle NULL return on failure.

functions.name: r_fs_check
functions.description: Checks whether the path or parameter p is valid/accessible/recognized within fs (exact semantics are plugin-dependent).
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
p must be a non-NULL string.

functions.name: r_fs_shell
functions.description: Runs an interactive filesystem shell bound to fs, using the provided RFSShell callbacks/bindings and starting at root path. Returns true on success/normal completion.
requirements: shell must be a valid RFSShell pointer, typically created by r_fs_shell_new and populated with required callbacks as needed.
fs must be a valid RFS instance.
root must be a non-NULL root path string.

functions.name: r_fs_file_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new RFSFile object associated with the given root and path (metadata-only until opened/slurped depending on plugin).
requirements: root must be a valid RFSRoot pointer.
path must be a non-NULL path string.
Caller should check for NULL on failure and free with r_fs_file_free when done.

functions.name: r_fs_file_free
functions.description: Frees an RFSFile object previously allocated/returned by r_fs_file_new/r_fs_open/r_fs_slurp, releasing any associated buffers and metadata.
requirements: file must be a valid RFSFile pointer.
After calling, file must not be used again.

functions.name: r_fs_file_copy_abs_path
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated copy of the absolute path for the given RFSFile.
requirements: file must be a valid RFSFile pointer with path metadata initialized.
Caller must free the returned string.
Caller should check for NULL return indicating failure.

functions.name: r_fs_cmd
functions.description: Runs a command against registered filesystem plugins (plugin-specific commands; e.g., the comment mentions m:cmd). Returns true if a plugin handled the command.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
cmd must be a non-NULL command string.

functions.name: r_fs_root
functions.description: Returns a list of roots matching or related to the given path, likely RFSRoot entries.
requirements: fs must be a valid RFS instance.
path must be a non-NULL path string.
Caller must check for NULL and manage/free the returned list per library conventions.

functions.name: r_fs_root_new
functions.description: Creates a new RFSRoot object for a base path with an offset delta.
requirements: path must be a non-NULL string.
Caller should check for NULL return and later free the root with r_fs_root_free.

functions.name: r_fs_root_free
functions.description: Frees an RFSRoot object created by r_fs_root_new or returned by mount operations, releasing internal resources.
requirements: root must be a valid RFSRoot pointer.
After calling, root must not be used again.

functions.name: r_fs_partition_new
functions.signature: RFSPartition *r_fs_partition_new(int num, ut64 start, ut64 length)
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new RFSPartition descriptor with the given number, start, and length.
requirements: Caller should check for NULL return indicating allocation failure.
num should be a valid partition number; exact valid ranges are unspecified.
start and length should describe a valid region; no explicit constraints provided.

functions.name: r_fs_partition_free
functions.description: Frees an RFSPartition previously created by r_fs_partition_new.
requirements: p must be a valid RFSPartition pointer.
After calling, p must not be used again.

functions.name: r_fs_partition_type
functions.description: Returns a human-readable name for a partition of a given type within a partitioning scheme identified by part.
requirements: part must be a non-NULL string identifying a partition scheme/type registry.
type is an integer code within that scheme; exact valid values are unspecified.
Returned pointer refers to static/constant data; caller must not free or modify it (implied by const).

functions.name: r_fs_partition_type_get
functions.description: Returns a human-readable partition type name by index n from the built-in table.
requirements: n must be a valid index into the internal partition type table; out-of-range behavior is unspecified.
Returned pointer is constant; caller must not free or modify it.

functions.name: r_socket_new_from_fd
functions.description: Create an RSocket wrapper around an existing OS socket/file descriptor. Useful to adopt a socket accepted/created elsewhere.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open socket/file descriptor appropriate for use with this library
The returned RSocket* must be released with r_socket_free when no longer needed

functions.name: r_socket_new
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new RSocket object, optionally enabling SSL/TLS support for subsequent operations.
requirements: Call r_socket_free to release the returned RSocket*
If is_ssl is true, an SSL-capable build and proper subsequent configuration (e.g., certificates for servers) are required before connect/listen

functions.name: r_socket_spawn
functions.signature: bool r_socket_spawn(RSocket *s, const char *cmd, unsigned int timeout);
functions.description: Spawn/connect to a process or service using the socket wrapper. Exact behavior is not documented here; likely runs a command and ties I/O to the socket instance.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, initialized RSocket*
cmd must be a non-NULL command string
timeout is in milliseconds or seconds (unknown); use non-negative values
Behavioral details (I/O redirection, lifecycle) are unknown from this header

functions.name: r_socket_connect
functions.signature: bool r_socket_connect(RSocket *s, const char *host, const char *port, int proto, unsigned int timeout);
functions.description: Connect an RSocket to a remote endpoint using the given protocol (TCP/UDP/UNIX/etc.).
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, initialized RSocket* (e.g., from r_socket_new)
host must be a non-NULL address/hostname appropriate for the chosen proto
port must be a non-NULL service/port string (or path for UNIX sockets per macro usage)
proto should be one of the R_SOCKET_PROTO_* constants
timeout should be non-negative; unit unspecified
For SSL connections, s should be created with is_ssl=true

functions.name: r_socket_connect_serial
functions.signature: int r_socket_connect_serial(RSocket *sock, const char *path, int speed, int parity);
functions.description: Open and configure a serial port connection via the RSocket abstraction.
requirements: sock must be a non-NULL RSocket*
path must be a valid serial device path
speed should be a supported baud rate
parity must be a valid parity setting value (exact encoding unknown)
Returns an integer status/descriptor; exact semantics not documented

functions.name: r_socket_listen
functions.signature: bool r_socket_listen(RSocket *s, const char *port, const char *certfile);
functions.description: Bind and listen for incoming connections on the specified port. If SSL is enabled, an optional certificate file may be used.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, initialized RSocket*
port must be a non-NULL service/port string to listen on
If s is SSL-enabled, certfile should reference a valid certificate/key as required by the underlying SSL setup (details not specified)
Call r_socket_accept or r_socket_accept_timeout to accept clients

functions.name: r_socket_port_by_name
functions.description: Resolve a service name (e.g., "http") to its numeric port.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL service name string
Return value semantics (e.g., -1 on failure) are not documented here

functions.name: r_socket_close_fd
functions.description: Close the underlying socket/file descriptor of the RSocket without necessarily freeing the structure.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL RSocket* that has been opened/connected/listening
After closing, further I/O calls on s will fail
Use r_socket_free to fully release the structure when done

functions.name: r_socket_close
functions.description: Close the connection represented by the RSocket, performing any necessary cleanup of the OS-level socket/SSL state.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL RSocket*
After closing, the RSocket should not be used for I/O
To release memory, call r_socket_free

functions.name: r_socket_free
functions.description: Free an RSocket object and its associated resources.
requirements: s may be NULL (behavior unspecified); if non-NULL, it must not be used after this call
If the socket is still open, it should be closed (e.g., via r_socket_close) before freeing to avoid leaks (behavior unspecified)

functions.name: r_socket_accept
functions.description: Accept an incoming connection on a listening RSocket and return a new connected RSocket for the client.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL RSocket* that is already listening
Blocks or non-blocks depending on socket configuration (unspecified)
Returned RSocket* must be freed with r_socket_free

functions.name: r_socket_accept_timeout
functions.description: Accept an incoming connection with a timeout, returning a connected RSocket or NULL on timeout/error.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL RSocket* in listening state
timeout should be non-negative (unit unspecified)
Returned RSocket* must be freed with r_socket_free

functions.name: r_socket_block_time
functions.signature: bool r_socket_block_time(RSocket *s, bool block, int sec, int usec);
functions.description: Configure blocking mode and/or I/O timeout on the socket.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL RSocket*
sec and usec should be non-negative if used as timeouts; semantics depend on implementation
If block is false, socket may become non-blocking

functions.name: r_socket_flush
functions.description: Flush pending I/O on the socket. Exact semantics (write vs read buffer) are not specified.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL RSocket*
Return value semantics are unspecified

functions.name: r_socket_ready
functions.signature: int r_socket_ready(RSocket *s, int secs, int usecs);
functions.description: Poll/check readiness (e.g., for reading) on the socket with a timeout.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL RSocket*
secs and usecs specify a timeout; use non-negative values
Return value semantics (e.g., >0 ready, 0 timeout, <0 error) are not documented here but follow common patterns

functions.name: r_socket_tostring
functions.description: Return a textual representation of the socket (e.g., remote/local address).
requirements: s must be a non-NULL RSocket*
Ownership/lifetime of the returned string is unknown; caller responsibilities are unspecified

functions.name: r_socket_write
functions.signature: int r_socket_write(RSocket *s, const void *buf, int len);
functions.description: Write len bytes from buf to the socket.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, connected RSocket*
buf must point to a valid memory region of at least len bytes
len must be >= 0
Return value is the number of bytes written or an error code (exact error semantics unspecified)

functions.name: r_socket_puts
functions.description: Write a null-terminated string to the socket (likely without automatic newline handling; not specified).
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, connected RSocket*
buf must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string
Return value indicates bytes written or error (unspecified)

functions.name: r_socket_printf
functions.description: Formatted print to the socket using printf-style formatting.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, connected RSocket*
fmt must be a non-NULL format string compatible with the provided varargs
Follows printf formatting rules; format/argument mismatches are undefined behavior

functions.name: r_socket_read
functions.description: Read up to len bytes from the socket into the provided buffer.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL RSocket*
read must point to a valid buffer of at least len bytes
len must be >= 0
Return value is bytes read or error/EOF indicator (unspecified)

functions.name: r_socket_read_block
functions.signature: int r_socket_read_block(RSocket *s, unsigned char *buf, int len);
functions.description: Blocking read of exactly up to len bytes into buf (blocking semantics implied by name).
requirements: s must be a non-NULL RSocket*
buf must be a valid buffer of at least len bytes
len must be >= 0
Exact blocking and return semantics are not documented

functions.name: r_socket_gets
functions.description: Read a line or up to size-1 bytes into a char buffer, null-terminating it (typical gets-like behavior; details not specified).
requirements: s must be a non-NULL RSocket*
buf must be a valid buffer with capacity >= size
size must be > 0
Return value semantics (length read or error) are unspecified

functions.name: r_socket_slurp
functions.description: Read all available data from the socket and return it in a newly allocated buffer, setting length via len.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL RSocket*
len must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the data length
Ownership/lifetime of the returned buffer is unspecified (likely heap-allocated)

functions.name: r_socket_is_connected
functions.description: Return whether the socket is currently connected.
requirements: Argument must be a non-NULL RSocket*

functions.name: r_socket_proc_open
functions.description: Spawn a process with pipes for I/O and return a process I/O handle.
requirements: argv must point to a NULL-terminated argument vector (program path and args)
Returned RSocketProc* must be closed with r_socket_proc_close when done

functions.name: r_socket_proc_close
functions.description: Close the process I/O pipes and reap/cleanup the spawned process.
requirements: sp must be a non-NULL RSocketProc* obtained from r_socket_proc_open
After closing, sp should not be used

functions.name: r_socket_proc_read
functions.signature: int r_socket_proc_read(RSocketProc *sp, unsigned char *buf, int len);
functions.description: Read from the spawned process's stdout/stderr pipe into buf.
requirements: sp must be a non-NULL RSocketProc*
buf must be a valid buffer of at least len bytes
len must be >= 0
Return value semantics (bytes read or error) are unspecified

functions.name: r_socket_proc_gets
functions.description: Read a line or up to size-1 bytes from the process pipe into a char buffer, null-terminating it (details unspecified).
requirements: sp must be a non-NULL RSocketProc*
buf must be a valid buffer with capacity >= size
size must be > 0

functions.name: r_socket_proc_write
functions.description: Write len bytes from buf to the spawned process's stdin pipe.
requirements: sp must be a non-NULL RSocketProc*
buf must point to a valid memory region of at least len bytes
len must be >= 0

functions.name: r_socket_proc_printf
functions.description: Formatted write to the spawned process's stdin using printf-style formatting.
requirements: sp must be a non-NULL RSocketProc*
fmt must be a non-NULL format string compatible with the provided varargs

functions.name: r_socket_proc_ready
functions.signature: int r_socket_proc_ready(RSocketProc *sp, int secs, int usecs);
functions.description: Check whether there is data ready to read from the process pipe with a timeout.
requirements: sp must be a non-NULL RSocketProc*
secs and usecs specify timeout; use non-negative values

functions.name: r_socket_http_get
functions.signature: char *r_socket_http_get(const char *url, const char **headers, int *code, int *rlen);
functions.description: Perform an HTTP GET request and return the response body as a string. Optionally pass extra request headers; receive response code and body length.
requirements: url must be a non-NULL URL string
headers may be NULL or a pointer to a NULL-terminated array of header strings; exact format unspecified
code and rlen may be NULL or pointers to ints to receive status code and length
Ownership/lifetime of the returned string is unspecified

functions.name: r_socket_http_post
functions.signature: char *r_socket_http_post(const char *url, const char **headers, const char *data, int *code, int *rlen);
functions.description: Perform an HTTP POST request with optional body and headers; return response body.
requirements: url must be non-NULL
headers may be NULL or a pointer to a NULL-terminated array of header strings; exact format unspecified
data may be NULL or a pointer to request body
code and rlen may be NULL or pointers to ints to receive status code and length
Ownership/lifetime of the returned string is unspecified

functions.name: r_socket_http_download
functions.signature: bool r_socket_http_download(const char *url, const char **headers, const char *filepath);
functions.description: Download the content from the given URL to the specified filepath.
requirements: url must be non-NULL
headers may be NULL or a pointer to a NULL-terminated array of header strings
filepath must be a non-NULL, writable destination path

functions.name: r_socket_http_server_set_breaked
functions.description: Provide a boolean flag pointer to allow the HTTP server loop to be externally interrupted/stopped.
requirements: b must be a non-NULL pointer to a boolean flag that remains valid while the server runs

functions.name: r_socket_http_accept
functions.description: Accept and parse an incoming HTTP request on a listening socket, returning a request object with parsed fields and raw data.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, listening RSocket*
so may be NULL or a pointer to options affecting parsing/behavior
Returned RSocketHTTPRequest* must be closed/freed using r_socket_http_close/r_socket_http_free as appropriate

functions.name: r_socket_http_response
functions.signature: void r_socket_http_response(RSocketHTTPRequest *rs, int code, const char *out, int x, const char *headers);
functions.description: Send an HTTP response for a previously accepted request, with status code, body, and optional headers. Parameter x meaning is not documented.
requirements: rs must be a non-NULL RSocketHTTPRequest* produced by r_socket_http_accept
code should be a valid HTTP status code integer
out may be NULL or a pointer to response body data
headers may be NULL or a headers string; exact format unspecified
Meaning of parameter x is unknown from this header

functions.name: r_socket_http_close
functions.description: Close the HTTP request/connection represented by rs.
requirements: rs must be a non-NULL RSocketHTTPRequest*
After closing, rs should not be used for further I/O

functions.name: r_socket_http_handle_upload
functions.description: Process/parse an HTTP upload payload and return extracted data. Exact behavior depends on implementation (e.g., multipart parsing).
requirements: str must point to a buffer of at least len bytes
len must be >= 0
olen must be a non-NULL pointer to receive output length
Ownership/lifetime of the returned buffer is unspecified

functions.name: r_socket_http_free
functions.description: Free an RSocketHTTPRequest structure and any associated allocations.
requirements: rs may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must not be used after this call
Typically called after r_socket_http_close

functions.name: r_socket_rap_server_new
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new RAP (remote access protocol) server bound to a port, optionally with SSL.
requirements: port must be a non-NULL service/port string
Returned RSocketRapServer* must be freed with r_socket_rap_server_free
If is_ssl is true, SSL support must be available and properly configured for later listen

functions.name: r_socket_rap_server_create
functions.description: Create a RAP server based on a configuration file or path. Exact semantics not documented in this header.
requirements: pathname must be a non-NULL path string
Returned RSocketRapServer* must be freed with r_socket_rap_server_free

functions.name: r_socket_rap_server_free
functions.description: Free a RAP server instance and its resources.
requirements: rap_s may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must not be used after this call

functions.name: r_socket_rap_server_listen
functions.description: Bind and listen for RAP client connections. If SSL is enabled, use the provided certificate file.
requirements: rap_s must be a non-NULL RAP server instance
certfile may be NULL or a path as required for SSL-enabled servers

functions.name: r_socket_rap_server_accept
functions.description: Accept an incoming RAP connection and return a connected RSocket for the client.
requirements: rap_s must be a non-NULL RAP server instance that is already listening
Returned RSocket* must be freed with r_socket_free

functions.name: r_socket_rap_server_continue
functions.description: Process/continue serving RAP protocol interactions. Exact event loop semantics are not documented.
requirements: rap_s must be a non-NULL RAP server instance

functions.name: r_socket_rap_client_open
functions.signature: int r_socket_rap_client_open(RSocket *s, const char *file, int rw);
functions.description: In a RAP client, open a remote file or resource via the RAP protocol.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, connected RSocket* to a RAP server
file must be a non-NULL remote path
rw should specify access mode flags; exact values unspecified
Return semantics (fd or status) are not documented

functions.name: r_socket_rap_client_command
functions.description: Send a command string to the RAP server and return its textual response. May use RCoreBind for integration.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, connected RSocket*
cmd must be a non-NULL command string
c may be NULL or a valid RCoreBind pointer
Ownership/lifetime of the returned string is unspecified

functions.name: r_socket_rap_client_write
functions.signature: int r_socket_rap_client_write(RSocket *s, const ut8 *buf, int count);
functions.description: Write bytes to the RAP server connection.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, connected RSocket*
buf must be a valid buffer of at least count bytes
count must be >= 0

functions.name: r_socket_rap_client_read
functions.description: Read bytes from the RAP server connection into buf.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, connected RSocket*
buf must be a valid buffer of at least count bytes
count must be >= 0

functions.name: r_socket_rap_client_seek
functions.signature: ut64 r_socket_rap_client_seek(RSocket *s, ut64 offset, int whence);
functions.description: Seek to a position in the remote file/resource on the RAP server side.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, connected RSocket*
whence should be a valid seek constant (e.g., SEEK_SET/SEEK_CUR/SEEK_END; exact values unspecified)

functions.name: r_run_new
functions.description: Create a new run profile, optionally initialized from a profile string.
requirements: str may be NULL or a profile string
Returned RRunProfile* must be freed with r_run_free

functions.name: r_run_parse
functions.description: Parse a full run profile specification string into an existing RRunProfile.
requirements: pf must be a non-NULL RRunProfile*
profile must be a non-NULL profile string

functions.name: r_run_free
functions.description: Free an RRunProfile and all associated allocations.
requirements: r may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must not be used after this call

functions.name: r_run_parseline
functions.description: Parse and apply a single line of run profile configuration.
requirements: p must be a non-NULL RRunProfile*
b must be a non-NULL configuration line string

functions.name: r_run_help
functions.description: Return a help/usage string describing the run profile syntax and options.
requirements: Returned string is constant; do not modify or free it

functions.name: r_run_config_env
functions.description: Apply environment-related configuration from the run profile (e.g., environment variables, paths).
requirements: p must be a non-NULL RRunProfile* with parsed settings

functions.name: r_run_start
functions.description: Start a process according to the run profile settings (daemonization, stdio redirection, etc.).
requirements: p must be a non-NULL RRunProfile* properly configured
Side effects include process creation; errors should be handled by checking the boolean result

functions.name: r_run_reset
functions.description: Reset/clear fields in the run profile to defaults.
requirements: p must be a non-NULL RRunProfile*

functions.name: r_run_fini
functions.description: Finalize/cleanup internal state of a run profile, without freeing the structure itself.
requirements: p must be a non-NULL RRunProfile*

functions.name: r_run_parsefile
functions.description: Parse a run profile from a file path or file-like input (exact semantics of b are not specified).
requirements: p must be a non-NULL RRunProfile*
b must be a non-NULL string argument (likely a file path)

functions.name: r_run_get_environ_profile
functions.description: Construct a run profile string from an environment array.
requirements: env must be a NULL-terminated environment array (char**), typically from main's envp
Ownership/lifetime of the returned string is unspecified

functions.name: rap_open

Returned R2Pipe* must be closed with rap_close or r2pipe_close

functions.name: rap_open_corebind

functions.name: rap_close

requirements: rap must be a non-NULL R2Pipe* obtained from rap_open/rap_open_corebind

functions.name: rap_cmd

functions.name: rap_cmdf

functions.name: rap_write

functions.name: rap_read

functions.name: r2pipe_write
functions.description: Write a raw string to a r2pipe handle (alias family).
requirements: r2pipe must be a non-NULL R2Pipe*
str must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string

functions.name: r2pipe_read
functions.description: Read available output from a r2pipe handle and return it as a string.
requirements: r2pipe must be a non-NULL R2Pipe*
Ownership/lifetime of the returned string is unspecified

functions.name: r2pipe_close
functions.description: Close a r2pipe handle and release associated resources.
requirements: r2pipe must be a non-NULL R2Pipe*
After closing, the handle must not be used

functions.name: r2pipe_open_corebind
functions.description: Open a r2pipe handle using an existing RCoreBind binding (in-process).
requirements: coreb must be a non-NULL RCoreBind*
Returned R2Pipe* must be closed with r2pipe_close

functions.name: r2pipe_open
functions.description: Open a r2pipe handle by spawning the given command and connecting to its I/O endpoints.

Returned R2Pipe* must be closed with r2pipe_close

functions.name: r2pipe_open_dl
