Returned R2Pipe* must be closed with r2pipe_close

functions.name: r2pipe_cmd
functions.description: Send a command string over a r2pipe handle and return the textual response.
requirements: r2pipe must be a non-NULL R2Pipe*
str must be a non-NULL command string
Ownership/lifetime of the returned string is unspecified

functions.name: r2pipe_cmdf
functions.description: Format a command with printf-style arguments and send it over a r2pipe handle; return the textual response.
requirements: r2pipe must be a non-NULL R2Pipe*
fmt must be a non-NULL format string compatible with varargs
Ownership/lifetime of the returned string is unspecified

functions.name: r_socket_connect_tcp
functions.signature: bool r_socket_connect_tcp(RSocket *s, const char *host, const char *port, unsigned int timeout);
functions.description: Convenience macro wrapping r_socket_connect(...) to establish a TCP connection to host:port, with a timeout. Use this after creating/initializing an RSocket (e.g., via r_socket_new). Returns true on successful connection, false otherwise. Notes: implemented as a macro that passes R_SOCKET_PROTO_TCP as the protocol.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSocket* (e.g., from r_socket_new or r_socket_new_from_fd)
host must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string
port must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string (exact format/units are not specified here; typically a service name or numeric string)
timeout must be provided (unsigned int); time unit is not specified in this header (unknown)
Caller should check the boolean return value for success/failure before using the socket further

functions.name: r_socket_connect_udp
functions.signature: bool r_socket_connect_udp(RSocket *s, const char *host, const char *port, unsigned int timeout);
functions.description: Convenience macro wrapping r_socket_connect(...) to associate the UDP socket with a default remote peer at host:port, with a timeout. Use after creating/initializing an RSocket. Returns true on success, false otherwise. Notes: implemented as a macro that passes R_SOCKET_PROTO_UDP as the protocol.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSocket* (e.g., from r_socket_new or r_socket_new_from_fd)
host must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string
port must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string (exact format/units are not specified here)
timeout must be provided (unsigned int); time unit is not specified in this header (unknown)
Caller should check the boolean return value for success/failure before using the socket further

functions.name: r_socket_connect_unix
functions.description: Convenience macro to connect an RSocket to a UNIX domain socket at the given filesystem path. On UNIX platforms it wraps r_socket_connect(...) passing the path as both host and port and the protocol R_SOCKET_PROTO_UNIX with timeout 0. On non-UNIX platforms, this macro is defined to always evaluate to false (no-op connection).
requirements: This macro is only functional on UNIX platforms (R2__UNIX__ defined); on non-UNIX it always returns false
s must be a valid, initialized RSocket* (e.g., from r_socket_new)
path must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string referring to a UNIX domain socket path
Caller must check the boolean result; if false, the connection did not succeed (and on non-UNIX it will always be false)
Timeout is effectively 0 in this macro expansion (no configurable timeout via this helper)

functions.name: r2p_cmd
functions.description: Backward-compatibility macro aliasing r2pipe_cmd. Sends the command string to the underlying r2pipe endpoint (e.g., a spawned process or HTTP endpoint) and returns the textual response. Return ownership/encoding are not specified here; check the implementation in your build.
requirements: r2pipe must be a valid, opened R2Pipe* obtained from r2p_open/r2pipe_open or equivalent
str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated command string
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL to detect errors
Memory ownership of the returned char* is not specified in this header (unknown); caller should consult implementation to know whether it must be freed

functions.name: r2p_open
functions.description: Backward-compatibility macro aliasing r2pipe_open. Opens an r2pipe connection, typically by spawning the given command and setting up IPC (or using an alternate transport per configuration). Returns an R2Pipe handle on success, or NULL on failure.
requirements: cmd should be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string specifying the program/command to execute or connect to
Caller must check the returned R2Pipe* for NULL before further use
The resulting R2Pipe* must be closed with r2p_close/r2pipe_close when no longer needed

functions.name: r2p_close
functions.description: Backward-compatibility macro aliasing r2pipe_close. Closes the r2pipe connection and releases associated resources. Returns an int status (exact semantics not specified here).
requirements: r2pipe must be a valid R2Pipe* previously returned by r2p_open/r2pipe_open
After a successful close, the R2Pipe* must not be used again
Caller should check the integer return value to detect errors (exact convention unknown)

functions.name: r_syscall_item_new_from_string
functions.description: Create and initialize a syscall item record from a name and a serialized argument description string. Intended for constructing an RSyscallItem entry programmatically or while loading a database of syscalls.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string.
s must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string describing the syscall’s arguments (exact format is unknown from this header).
The returned RSyscallItem*, when no longer needed, should be released with r_syscall_item_free().
On allocation or parse failure, the function may return NULL (behavior not documented here; caller should be prepared for NULL).
The exact expected format of s is unknown; callers should use the same format as produced/consumed by the surrounding library.

functions.name: r_syscall_item_free
functions.description: Release all resources held by an RSyscallItem previously created (e.g., by r_syscall_item_new_from_string).
requirements: si must be either NULL or a valid pointer previously obtained from this library (e.g., via r_syscall_item_new_from_string).
Do not double-free the same RSyscallItem pointer.
After this call, si must not be used.

functions.name: r_syscall_new
functions.description: Allocate and return a new syscall database/context handle used to query syscall metadata for a given architecture/OS.
requirements: Returns a newly allocated RSyscall* that must be eventually released by r_syscall_free().
Before querying for syscalls, initialize the context with r_syscall_setup().
On allocation failure, may return NULL; callers should check the return value.

functions.name: r_syscall_free
functions.description: Release a syscall context and its associated resources. Likely decreases an internal reference count and frees when it reaches zero.
requirements: ctx must be a valid RSyscall* previously obtained from r_syscall_new() or r_syscall_ref().
Call exactly once for each successful acquisition (the initial r_syscall_new() and each r_syscall_ref() must be balanced by a corresponding r_syscall_free()).
After this call, ctx must not be used.

functions.name: r_syscall_ref
functions.description: Increase the reference count of an RSyscall context and return the same context pointer. Use to share the context safely across components.
requirements: sc must be a valid, initialized RSyscall* (obtained from r_syscall_new()).
Each successful r_syscall_ref() must be balanced with a matching r_syscall_free() to avoid leaks.
Return value may be NULL if sc is NULL (not specified here); caller should handle NULL defensively.

functions.name: r_syscall_setup
functions.signature: bool r_syscall_setup(RSyscall *s, const char *arch, int bits, const char *cpu, const char *os);
functions.description: Initialize an RSyscall context for a specific architecture/CPU/OS/bitness so that syscall queries operate against the appropriate database.
requirements: s must be a valid RSyscall* returned by r_syscall_new().
arch must be a non-NULL string naming the target architecture (e.g., "x86", "arm"; exact accepted values are unknown here).
bits must specify the target bitness (typical values: 16/32/64; exact constraints unknown).
cpu may be architecture-specific; acceptable values are unknown from this header.
os must be a non-NULL string naming the target operating system (exact accepted values unknown).
Must be called (and succeed) before calling r_syscall_get(), r_syscall_get_num(), r_syscall_get_i(), r_syscall_sysreg(), r_syscall_list(), r_syscall_get_swi(), or r_syscall_get_io().
Return value indicates success (true) or failure (false); callers must check and handle a false result.

functions.name: r_syscall_get
functions.description: Lookup and return metadata for a syscall identified by its numeric ID and software interrupt (SWI) selector in the configured context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid RSyscall* successfully initialized with r_syscall_setup().
num should be the syscall number for the configured ABI; valid range/values are ABI-dependent and not specified here.
swi should be the SWI or selector appropriate for the architecture; acceptable values are unknown here.
Caller should expect NULL if the syscall is not found or on error (not explicitly documented, but typical for such getters).
Returned RSyscallItem is owned by the context; do not free it directly unless documentation states otherwise (ownership not specified here; treat as read-only).

functions.name: r_syscall_get_num
functions.description: Resolve a syscall’s numeric ID from a string identifier (typically a syscall name) within the configured context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid RSyscall* successfully initialized with r_syscall_setup().
str must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string (presumably a syscall name).
Return value on failure is unknown from this header (commonly -1); caller should handle negative or special values defensively.

functions.name: r_syscall_get_i
functions.signature: const char *r_syscall_get_i(RSyscall *ctx, int num, int swi);
functions.description: Retrieve a string associated with a syscall identified by number and SWI, likely the syscall’s name or signature, from the configured context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid RSyscall* successfully initialized with r_syscall_setup().
num and swi must correspond to the target ABI; valid ranges are unknown.
The returned string is owned by the context; do not modify or free it (ownership not explicitly documented; treat as read-only).
May return NULL if the syscall is not found or on error (not documented here; caller should handle NULL).

functions.name: r_syscall_sysreg
functions.signature: const char* r_syscall_sysreg(RSyscall *s, const char *type, ut64 num);
functions.description: Lookup a system register or related metadata by type and numeric identifier for the configured architecture (exact semantics unknown).
requirements: s must be a valid RSyscall* successfully initialized with r_syscall_setup().
type must be a non-NULL string denoting a category (e.g., register type); accepted values are not defined in this header.
num is a 64-bit identifier/index whose valid range depends on type and architecture (unspecified here).
Returns a const char* owned by the context; do not free or modify (ownership not explicitly documented; treat as read-only).
May return NULL if the item is not found or on error (not specified; caller should handle NULL).

functions.name: r_syscall_list
functions.description: Return a list of syscalls available in the configured context. The list contents are likely RSyscallItem entries (exact element type not specified in this header).
requirements: ctx must be a valid RSyscall* successfully initialized with r_syscall_setup().
The ownership and lifetime of the returned RList and its elements are not specified here; callers should not free elements unless documented elsewhere. Treat returned data as read-only.
The function may return NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL.

functions.name: r_syscall_get_swi
functions.description: Obtain the SWI (software interrupt) selector or default value used for the currently configured context (exact meaning may vary by architecture).
requirements: s must be a valid RSyscall* successfully initialized with r_syscall_setup().
Return value range/semantics are architecture-specific and not described here; callers should handle unexpected values defensively.

functions.name: r_syscall_get_io
functions.description: Map an IO port/index to a descriptive string for the configured context (e.g., a port name or class). Exact semantics are unspecified in this header.
requirements: s must be a valid RSyscall* successfully initialized with r_syscall_setup().
ioport must be an integer within the valid range for the configured architecture/OS (exact range unknown).
Returns a const char* owned by the context; do not modify or free it (ownership not explicitly documented; treat as read-only).
May return NULL if the mapping is not found or on error; callers should handle NULL.

functions.name: r_event_new
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new REvent dispatcher/context. The user pointer is stored in the REvent and will be passed to callbacks when events are fired. Typical usage: create once per component that wants to register hooks and dispatch events, then pass the returned REvent* to hook and send functions.
requirements: Must be called to obtain a valid REvent* before using r_event_hook or r_event_send.
The returned REvent* must later be released with r_event_free to avoid memory leaks.
The user argument may be NULL; it is opaque and passed back to callbacks unchanged.

functions.name: r_event_free
functions.description: Releases all resources associated with the given REvent instance, including any internal containers of hooks. Intended to destroy a context created by r_event_new.
requirements: ev must be a pointer previously returned by r_event_new, or NULL-safe behavior is unknown (not documented).
After calling r_event_free, the ev pointer and any callback handles associated with it must not be used.
Should not be called concurrently with r_event_send or r_event_hook on the same REvent (thread-safety not documented).

functions.name: r_event_hook
functions.signature: R_API bool r_event_hook(REvent *ev, ut32 type, REventCallback cb, void *data);
functions.description: Registers a callback to be invoked when an event of the given type is dispatched on this REvent instance. The callback receives the REvent*, the event type, the user pointer supplied here (data), and the event-specific payload pointer supplied to r_event_send. Event types generally come from REventType, but values greater than R_EVENT_LAST are also supported via the internal "other_events" map.
requirements: ev must be a valid REvent* created by r_event_new.
cb must be non-NULL and must remain callable for as long as it may be invoked.
type should be a valid event identifier (typically a value from REventType, or a library/user-defined value > R_EVENT_LAST).
The data argument may be NULL; it will be provided as the user parameter to cb on invocation.
The function returns a bool indicating success or failure; callers should check the return value.

functions.name: r_event_unhook
functions.signature: R_API bool r_event_unhook(REvent * R_NULLABLE ev, ut32 event_hook, REventCallback cb);
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered callback for the specified event type on the given REvent instance. The parameter name event_hook is the event type identifier; cb selects which callback to remove.
requirements: If ev is NULL, behavior is library-defined (the parameter is annotated R_NULLABLE); callers should be prepared for a false return and avoid relying on side effects.
cb must be non-NULL and should match a callback previously registered with r_event_hook for the given event_hook (type).
event_hook should be the same event type value used during registration.
The function returns a bool indicating whether the unhook operation succeeded; callers should check the return value.

functions.name: r_event_send
functions.signature: R_API void r_event_send(REvent *ev, ut32 type, void *data);
functions.description: Dispatches an event of the given type to all callbacks registered on the REvent instance. Each matching callback is invoked with (REvent *ev, int type, void *user, void *data), where user is the pointer supplied when the hook was registered, and data is the event payload supplied here. For events defined in REventType, the payload typically points to the corresponding REventXXX structure (e.g., REventFunction, REventVariable, etc.).
requirements: ev must be a valid REvent* created by r_event_new.
type must match the value used for registration; values may be from REventType or higher for user-defined events.

data must point to the correct event payload structure expected by the callbacks for this type, or be NULL if the event semantics permit no payload. The memory referenced by data must remain valid for the duration of the callbacks.
May invoke multiple callbacks; callers should ensure reentrancy and avoid destroying ev or freeing data while callbacks are executing.

functions.name: r_search_new
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new RSearch context configured with the given search mode. Typical usage: create the search object, configure it (keywords, ranges, callbacks), then feed data and run searches.
requirements: mode should be one of the R_SEARCH_* enum values (e.g., R_SEARCH_KEYWORD, R_SEARCH_STRING).
The caller owns the returned pointer and must release it with r_search_free().

functions.name: r_search_set_mode
functions.description: Changes the search mode of an existing RSearch context. Use this to switch between search backends (e.g., keyword, regexp, string).
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
mode should be one of the R_SEARCH_* enum values.

functions.name: r_search_free
functions.description: Releases an RSearch context and all associated resources.
requirements: s may be NULL (if non-NULL, it must be a valid RSearch pointer returned by r_search_new).
After calling, s must not be used again.

functions.name: r_search_find
functions.signature: RList *r_search_find(RSearch *s, ut64 addr, const ut8 *buf, int len);
functions.description: Runs a search over the provided memory buffer using the configuration of RSearch (mode, keywords, etc.) and returns a list of matches. The search is interpreted as starting at the given base address (addr).
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer with appropriate mode/keywords configured.
buf must point to at least len bytes readable memory if len > 0.
len must be >= 0.
addr is the base address associated with the start of buf (used for hit addresses).
Returned RList ownership and element types are library-defined (likely hits); caller must follow library’s list ownership conventions.

functions.name: r_search_find_uds
functions.signature: RList *r_search_find_uds(RSearch *search, ut64 addr, const ut8 *data, size_t size, bool verbose);
functions.description: Finds patterns (UDS: unknown/undocumented search; likely heuristic/stride-based) in a given data buffer, producing a list of results. Accepts a base address and optional verbosity.
requirements: search must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
data must point to at least size bytes readable memory if size > 0.
size must be >= 0.
addr is the base address associated with the start of data.
Returned RList ownership and element types are library-defined; caller must follow library’s list ownership conventions.

functions.name: r_search_update
functions.signature: int r_search_update(RSearch *s, ut64 from, const ut8 *buf, long len);
functions.description: Feeds a chunk of data to the search engine starting at address ‘from’. Use when streaming data into the search context for incremental processing.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
buf must point to at least len bytes readable memory if len > 0.
len must be >= 0.
from is the address corresponding to buf[0].
Check return value for success/failure as per library conventions (non-zero likely indicates success).

functions.name: r_search_update_read
functions.signature: int r_search_update_read(RSearch *s, ut64 from, ut64 to);
functions.description: Requests the search engine to read/process data from the bound IO between addresses [from, to) or [from, to], depending on implementation, and update search state accordingly.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer, with its IO bindings configured (s->iob).
from and to must specify a valid non-empty or empty range; from <= to is expected.
Check return value for success/failure.

functions.name: r_search_maps
functions.description: Configures or processes a list of IO maps for searching. The list is expected to contain RIOMap entries.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
maps must be a valid RList pointer that contains RIOMap elements (library-defined).
Check return value for success/failure.

functions.name: r_search_keyword_free
functions.description: Frees an RSearchKeyword object and any internal allocations.
requirements: kw may be NULL (if non-NULL, it must be a valid RSearchKeyword pointer obtained from the r_search_keyword_new* family).
After calling, kw must not be used again.

functions.name: r_search_keyword_new
functions.signature: RSearchKeyword* r_search_keyword_new(const ut8 *kw, int kwlen, const ut8 *bm, int bmlen, const char *data);
functions.description: Creates a new RSearchKeyword from a raw binary pattern (kw) with an optional binary mask (bm) and optional user data (data).
requirements: kw must point to at least kwlen bytes readable memory if kwlen > 0.
kwlen must be >= 0 (non-zero for a meaningful keyword).
bm may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to at least bmlen bytes, and bmlen must be >= 0.
If both kw and bm are provided, their lengths should be compatible for masked searching (library-defined).
Returned keyword must be freed with r_search_keyword_free().

functions.name: r_search_keyword_new_str
functions.signature: RSearchKeyword* r_search_keyword_new_str(const char *kw, const char *bm, const char *data, bool icase);
functions.description: Creates a new RSearchKeyword from a C string pattern, with optional textual mask string and user data, and optional case-insensitive matching.
requirements: kw must be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer.
bm may be NULL or a valid NUL-terminated mask string understood by the library.
data may be NULL or a valid pointer to user data string (stored/associated).
Returned keyword must be freed with r_search_keyword_free().

functions.name: r_search_keyword_new_hexstr
functions.description: Creates a new RSearchKeyword from a textual hex string (e.g., "90 90 ?? EB FE") optionally with wildcards, and attaches user data.
requirements: xs must be a valid NUL-terminated hex-encoded pattern string understood by the library.
data may be NULL or a valid pointer to user data string.
Returned keyword must be freed with r_search_keyword_free().

functions.name: r_search_keyword_new_wide
functions.signature: RSearchKeyword* r_search_keyword_new_wide(const char *kw, const char *bm, const char *data, bool icase, bool be);
functions.description: Creates a new RSearchKeyword for wide-character string searches, with optional mask, case-insensitivity, and endianness selection (be for big-endian).
requirements: kw must be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer representing the text to search in wide format.
bm may be NULL or a valid NUL-terminated mask string understood by the library.
data may be NULL or a valid pointer to user data string.
Returned keyword must be freed with r_search_keyword_free().

functions.name: r_search_keyword_new_hex
functions.signature: RSearchKeyword* r_search_keyword_new_hex(const char *kwstr, const char *bmstr, const char *data);
functions.description: Creates a new RSearchKeyword from a hex-encoded pattern string and an optional hex-encoded mask string.
requirements: kwstr must be a valid NUL-terminated hex string understood by the library.
bmstr may be NULL or a valid NUL-terminated hex mask string understood by the library.
data may be NULL or a valid pointer to user data string.
Returned keyword must be freed with r_search_keyword_free().

functions.name: r_search_keyword_new_hexmask
functions.description: Creates a new RSearchKeyword from a hex string pattern with an implied mask format supported by the library, attaching user data.
requirements: kwstr must be a valid NUL-terminated hex string pattern understood by the library.
data may be NULL or a valid pointer to user data string.
Returned keyword must be freed with r_search_keyword_free().

functions.name: r_search_keyword_new_regexp
functions.description: Creates a new RSearchKeyword representing a regular expression pattern.
requirements: str must be a valid NUL-terminated string containing a regular expression supported by the library/engine.
data may be NULL or a valid pointer to user data string.
Returned keyword must be freed with r_search_keyword_free().

functions.name: r_search_kw_add
functions.description: Adds a prepared keyword object to the given search context for subsequent searches.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
kw must be a valid RSearchKeyword pointer created by one of the r_search_keyword_new* functions and not yet freed.
Check boolean return for success (true) or failure (false).

functions.name: r_search_reset
functions.description: Resets the search context to a clean state and sets a new search mode. Typically clears internal state and keywords/hits as appropriate.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
mode should be one of the R_SEARCH_* enum values.

functions.name: r_search_kw_reset
functions.description: Clears/removes any keywords from the search context, resetting keyword-related state.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.

functions.name: r_search_string_prepare_backward
functions.description: Prepares internal data structures to perform backward string searches in the current context.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
Should be called before performing backward string searches.

functions.name: r_search_range_add
functions.signature: int r_search_range_add(RSearch *s, ut64 from, ut64 to);
functions.description: Adds a search range [from, to] (or library-defined inclusive/exclusive bounds) to the search context.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
from and to must define a valid range; from <= to is expected.
Check return value for success/failure.

functions.name: r_search_range_set
functions.signature: int r_search_range_set(RSearch *s, ut64 from, ut64 to);
functions.description: Sets the active search range to [from, to], replacing any existing ranges.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
from and to must define a valid range; from <= to is expected.
Check return value for success/failure.

functions.name: r_search_range_reset
functions.description: Clears any previously defined search ranges in the context.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
Check return value for success/failure.

functions.name: r_search_hit_new
functions.description: Registers a new search hit at the specified address for the given keyword. Returns 2 if search.maxhits is reached, 0 on error, otherwise 1.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
kw must be a valid RSearchKeyword pointer (can be a placeholder if backend doesn’t use it, per comments).
addr is the address of the hit.
Caller should handle return values: 0 = error, 1 = success, 2 = success but max hits reached (stop or adapt accordingly).

functions.name: r_search_set_distance
functions.description: Sets the allowed edit/approximate matching distance for searches that support fuzzy matching.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
dist should be a non-negative integer; large values may be limited by the implementation (R_SEARCH_DISTANCE_MAX is defined as 10).

functions.name: r_search_strings
functions.signature: int r_search_strings(RSearch *s, ut32 min, ut32 max);
functions.description: Scans for printable strings within the configured ranges or data sources, using the specified minimum and maximum lengths.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
min and max are string length limits; min <= max is expected; min/max are in characters/bytes as supported by implementation.
Check return value for success/failure.

functions.name: r_search_set_string_limits
functions.signature: bool r_search_set_string_limits(RSearch *s, ut32 min, ut32 max);
functions.description: Configures the minimum and maximum string lengths for subsequent string-search operations.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
min and max are string length limits; min <= max is expected.
Check boolean return for success (true) or failure (false).

functions.name: r_search_set_callback
functions.description: Sets the legacy/deprecated per-hit callback and associated user pointer for the search context. The callback receives the keyword (may be a dummy) and hit address. Marked as TODO: deprecate in favor of length-aware callbacks.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
callback should be a valid function pointer matching RSearchCallback or NULL to clear (inferred).
user is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback.

functions.name: r_search_set_read_cb
functions.description: Sets the match callback (length-aware) and user pointer used during read/update-based searches. The callback is invoked with the keyword, match length, user data, and address.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
cb should be a valid function pointer matching RSearchRCb or NULL to clear (inferred).
user is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback.

functions.name: r_search_begin
functions.description: Initializes or starts the search process with the current configuration. Use before feeding data or invoking find routines as required by the backend.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.

functions.name: r_search_pattern_size
functions.description: Sets the expected pattern size for pattern-based searches.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized RSearch pointer.
size should be a non-negative integer appropriate for the active search mode.

functions.name: r_bp_new
functions.description: Constructs and returns a new RBreakpoint context used to manage breakpoints and related state. Typical usage: call r_bp_new(), configure plugins/architecture, then add/enable breakpoints.
requirements: Must be paired with r_bp_free() to avoid memory leaks.
Return value must be checked for NULL to handle allocation failures.
The returned RBreakpoint must be used as the bp handle for other r_bp_* APIs.

functions.name: r_bp_free
functions.description: Destroys and releases all resources associated with an RBreakpoint context created by r_bp_new(). After this call, the bp pointer must not be used.
requirements: bp must be a pointer returned by r_bp_new() or NULL.
bp must not be used after calling r_bp_free().
It is safe to pass NULL (behavior not explicitly documented; treat as unknown).

functions.name: r_bp_del
functions.description: Deletes a breakpoint at the specified address from the breakpoint context.
requirements: bp must be a valid pointer to an initialized RBreakpoint.
addr must correspond to an existing breakpoint; otherwise returns false (exact behavior unknown).

functions.name: r_bp_del_all
functions.description: Deletes all breakpoints from the breakpoint context.
requirements: bp must be a valid pointer to an initialized RBreakpoint.

functions.name: r_bp_plugin_add
functions.description: Registers a breakpoint plugin (architecture-specific or backend) with the breakpoint context.
requirements: bp must be a valid RBreakpoint pointer.
plugin must point to a properly initialized RBreakpointPlugin structure (fields like meta, arch, type, nbps, bps should be set as required by the plugin).
The same plugin should not be added multiple times (behavior if duplicated is unknown).

functions.name: r_bp_use
functions.signature: bool r_bp_use(RBreakpoint *bp, const char *name, int bits);
functions.description: Selects and activates a registered breakpoint plugin by name and bitness (architecture width) for subsequent breakpoint operations.
requirements: bp must be valid.
name must match a previously added plugin’s arch/name string.
bits must be compatible with the chosen plugin (exact allowed values unknown; typically 8/16/32/64).

functions.name: r_bp_plugin_remove
functions.description: Unregisters the given breakpoint plugin instance from the context.
requirements: bp must be valid.
plugin must be a plugin previously added to bp.

functions.name: r_bp_plugin_del
functions.description: Unregisters a breakpoint plugin by name from the context.
requirements: bp must be valid.
name must identify a plugin previously added to bp.

functions.name: r_bp_plugin_list
functions.description: Returns a string listing available/registered breakpoint plugins for this context. Intended for introspection or UI display.
requirements: bp must be valid.
Caller takes ownership of the returned string and must free it with the appropriate deallocator (exact allocator unknown).
Return may be NULL on error.

functions.name: r_bp_in
functions.signature: int r_bp_in(RBreakpoint *bp, ut64 addr, int perm);
functions.description: Checks if a breakpoint exists at a given address with permission constraints, or whether the address falls within a breakpointed region. Returns an integer status code.
requirements: bp must be valid.
perm is a permission mask; semantics align with R_PERM or deprecated R_BP_PROT_* flags (exact values unknown).
addr must be a valid address in the target address space.

functions.name: r_bp_list
functions.description: Returns a textual listing of current breakpoints. The rad parameter likely controls the output format (e.g., radare2 format vs plain).
requirements: bp must be valid.
Caller owns the returned string and must free it with the proper deallocator (exact allocator unknown).
rad parameter semantics are unknown; use 0/1 conservatively.
May return NULL on error.

functions.name: r_bp_size
functions.description: Returns the number of breakpoints currently stored in the context, or the size of the breakpoints collection.
requirements: bp must be valid.

functions.name: r_bp_get_bytes
functions.signature: int r_bp_get_bytes(RBreakpoint *bp, ut8 *buf, int len, int endian, int idx);
functions.description: Retrieves breakpoint bytes (or original bytes) into buf for the breakpoint at index idx, respecting the specified endianness. Returns number of bytes written or a status code.
requirements: bp must be valid.
buf must be a valid writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len must be non-negative and should not exceed the actual bytes size for that breakpoint.
endian must be a valid endianness indicator (e.g., 0/1; exact semantics unknown).
idx must be a valid index into the breakpoint list (use r_bp_get_index/r_bp_get_index_at to discover).

functions.name: r_bp_set_trace
functions.signature: bool r_bp_set_trace(RBreakpoint *bp, ut64 addr, int set);
functions.description: Enables or disables tracing for the breakpoint at the given address.
requirements: bp must be valid.
addr must reference an existing breakpoint.
set is a boolean-like flag (0 to disable, non-zero to enable; exact semantics unknown).

functions.name: r_bp_set_trace_all
functions.description: Enables or disables tracing for all breakpoints in the context.
requirements: bp must be valid.
set is a boolean-like flag (0/1; exact semantics unknown).

functions.name: r_bp_enable
functions.signature: RBreakpointItem *r_bp_enable(RBreakpoint *bp, ut64 addr, int set, int count);
functions.description: Enables or disables a breakpoint at the given address. Optionally configures a toggle counter (count) to auto-disable after a number of hits. Returns the affected breakpoint item.
requirements: bp must be valid.
addr must reference an existing breakpoint or a place where enabling is meaningful (exact behavior unknown).
set is a boolean-like flag to enable (non-zero) or disable (0).
count should be non-negative; when >0 it likely decrements on each hit (exact semantics inferred).

functions.name: r_bp_enable_all
functions.description: Enables or disables all breakpoints in the context.
requirements: bp must be valid.
set is a boolean-like flag (0/1; exact semantics unknown).

functions.name: r_bp_stepy_continuation
functions.description: Returns or updates the internal step-continuation mode used by software single-stepping. Exact semantics unknown; likely indicates how to continue after a step.
requirements: bp must be valid.

functions.name: r_bp_get_index
functions.description: Returns the breakpoint item at the given index in the internal index/table.
requirements: bp must be valid.
idx must be within the valid index range [0, r_bp_size(bp)-1].

functions.name: r_bp_del_index
functions.description: Deletes the breakpoint corresponding to the given index from the internal structures.
requirements: bp must be valid.
idx must be a valid index into the breakpoints collection.

functions.name: r_bp_get_index_at
functions.description: Returns the internal index for a breakpoint at the specified address, or a negative value if not found.
requirements: bp must be valid.
addr is the address to query.

functions.name: r_bp_item_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new breakpoint item associated with the context. Typically used internally before adding/configuring a breakpoint.
requirements: bp must be valid.
Return must be checked for NULL.

functions.name: r_bp_get_at
functions.description: Returns the breakpoint item located exactly at the given address, or NULL if none exists.
requirements: bp must be valid.
addr is the address to query.

functions.name: r_bp_get_in
functions.description: Returns the breakpoint item that covers the given address with the specified permission constraints (e.g., execute/read/write), or NULL if none.
requirements: bp must be valid.
addr is the address to query.
perm is a permission mask; exact flags unknown (R_PERM or deprecated R_BP_PROT_*).

functions.name: r_bp_is_valid
functions.description: Checks whether a breakpoint item is valid for the current context (e.g., properly initialized and consistent).
requirements: bp must be valid.
b must be a pointer to a breakpoint item (may be NULL; returns false).

functions.name: r_bp_add_cond
functions.description: Adds a conditional breakpoint based on the provided condition expression string.
requirements: bp must be valid.
cond must be a non-NULL, well-formed condition string; exact syntax unknown.

functions.name: r_bp_del_cond
functions.description: Deletes a conditional breakpoint by index.
requirements: bp must be valid.
idx must refer to an existing conditional breakpoint entry (exact index space unknown).

functions.name: r_bp_add_fault
functions.signature: void r_bp_add_fault(RBreakpoint *bp, ut64 addr, int size, int perm);
functions.description: Adds a fault breakpoint/region at the specified address range with given permissions. Likely used to detect access faults.
requirements: bp must be valid.
addr is the start address of the fault region.
size must be positive.
perm is a permission mask; exact flags unknown.

functions.name: r_bp_add_sw
functions.signature: RBreakpointItem *r_bp_add_sw(RBreakpoint *bp, ut64 addr, int size, int perm);
functions.description: Adds a software breakpoint at the specified address (or region) with the given size and permissions. Returns the created breakpoint item.
requirements: bp must be valid and configured with a suitable plugin via r_bp_use().
addr must be a valid address to place a software breakpoint.
size must be positive and match the architecture’s trap size (exact expectations unknown).
perm should include execute for instruction breakpoints (inferred; exact requirement unknown).
Return must be checked for NULL.

functions.name: r_bp_add_hw
functions.signature: RBreakpointItem *r_bp_add_hw(RBreakpoint *bp, ut64 addr, int size, int perm);
functions.description: Adds a hardware breakpoint/watchpoint at the specified address with the given size and permissions. Returns the created breakpoint item.
requirements: bp must be valid and the backend/target must support hardware breakpoints.
addr must be valid for a hardware breakpoint.
size must be positive and conform to hardware alignment/size constraints (exact constraints unknown).
perm encodes the access type (execute/read/write) expected by the backend (exact flags unknown).
Return must be checked for NULL.

functions.name: r_bp_restore_one
functions.description: Restores or reapplies the instruction bytes for a single breakpoint item, depending on the set flag. Useful when toggling or upon context changes.
requirements: bp must be valid.
b must be a valid breakpoint item belonging to bp.
set indicates whether to set (true) or restore original bytes (false); exact semantics inferred.

functions.name: r_bp_restore
functions.description: Restores or reapplies all breakpoints in the context depending on set. Returns a status or count (exact meaning unknown).
requirements: bp must be valid.
set indicates whether to set (true) or restore/remove (false); exact semantics inferred.

functions.name: r_bp_restore_except
functions.signature: bool r_bp_restore_except(RBreakpoint *bp, bool set, ut64 addr);
functions.description: Restores or reapplies all breakpoints except the one at the specified address. Useful for temporary stepping over a breakpoint.
requirements: bp must be valid.
addr is the address to exclude.
set flag semantics as in r_bp_restore (inferred).

functions.name: r_bp_traptrace_free
functions.description: Frees a traptrace-related allocation. Intended as a deallocator for structures created/returned by traptrace functions.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer previously returned by a traptrace allocation function (exact pairing unknown).
Safe to pass NULL (behavior unknown).

functions.name: r_bp_traptrace_enable
functions.description: Enables or disables trap tracing for the breakpoint context.
requirements: bp must be valid.
enable is a boolean-like flag (0/1; exact semantics unknown).

functions.name: r_bp_traptrace_reset
functions.description: Resets the traptrace state. A hard reset may clear buffers and state more aggressively (exact semantics unknown).
requirements: bp must be valid.
hard is a flag controlling reset strength (0/1; exact semantics unknown).

functions.name: r_bp_traptrace_next
functions.description: Returns the next traptrace address after the given address, or possibly the next recorded trap. Exact return semantics unknown.
requirements: bp must be valid.
addr is the current/reference address.

functions.name: r_bp_traptrace_add
functions.signature: int r_bp_traptrace_add(RBreakpoint *bp, ut64 from, ut64 to);
functions.description: Adds a traptrace range or transition from address 'from' to 'to'. Returns a status code or index.
requirements: bp must be valid.
from and to must be valid addresses in the trace context.

functions.name: r_bp_traptrace_free_at
functions.description: Frees/removes traptrace data starting at the specified 'from' address. Returns a status code.
requirements: bp must be valid.
from must be a valid address in the traptrace dataset.

functions.name: r_bp_traptrace_list
functions.description: Lists or dumps the traptrace entries associated with the breakpoint context, likely to the core’s output/log facility.
requirements: bp must be valid.

functions.name: r_bp_traptrace_at
functions.signature: bool r_bp_traptrace_at(RBreakpoint *bp, ut64 from, int len);
functions.description: Checks or marks a traptrace segment starting at 'from' of length 'len'. Returns true on success/match.
requirements: bp must be valid.
from must be a valid address.
len must be non-negative.

functions.name: r_bp_traptrace_new
functions.description: Creates and returns a new traptrace list/container for managing traptrace entries.
requirements: Return must be checked for NULL.
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned list, likely using r_bp_traptrace_free() or RList APIs (exact pairing unknown).

functions.name: r_bp_watch_add
functions.signature: RBreakpointItem *r_bp_watch_add(RBreakpoint *bp, ut64 addr, int size, int hw, int rw);
functions.description: Adds a watchpoint (typically hardware) at the specified address, watching a region of 'size' bytes for read/write/execute as specified by flags. Returns the created breakpoint item.
requirements: bp must be valid and the backend must support watchpoints.
addr must be a valid address.
size must be positive and meet hardware alignment/size constraints (exact constraints unknown).
hw flag indicates hardware use; values/semantics unknown.
rw encodes access types to watch (read/write/execute; exact flags unknown).
Return must be checked for NULL.

functions.name: r_lang_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new RLang context used to manage language plugins and sessions. Typical usage: create with r_lang_new(), optionally call r_lang_setup(), add/select plugins, run code, then free with r_lang_free().
requirements: Caller must free the returned RLang pointer with r_lang_free() to avoid memory leaks.
The returned pointer may be NULL on allocation failure (behavior not documented here); caller should check for NULL before use (inferred).

functions.name: r_lang_free
functions.description: Releases all resources held by an RLang context created by r_lang_new(), including any associated sessions, definitions, and plugin state managed by the context.
requirements: lang must be a pointer previously obtained from r_lang_new().
lang must not be used after this call (use-after-free).
Do not call r_lang_free() more than once on the same pointer (double free).

functions.name: r_lang_setup
functions.description: Initializes the RLang context for use (e.g., preparing internal structures and/or built-in plugins). Use after creating the context and before running code or manipulating plugins. Exact initialization details are not documented in this header.
requirements: lang must be a valid, initialized RLang pointer (typically from r_lang_new()).
Should be called before operations that rely on a fully initialized context (inferred from the name).
Return value must be checked; false indicates setup failed.

functions.name: r_lang_plugin_add
functions.description: Registers a language plugin with the given RLang context, making it available for selection and use.
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer.
plugin must be a valid RLangPlugin pointer with fields appropriate for use (function pointers expected to be compatible; exact mandatory fields not specified).
The plugin object must remain valid for as long as it is registered with the RLang context (lifetime/ownership not specified; inferred common pattern).
Return value must be checked; false indicates the plugin was not added.

functions.name: r_lang_plugin_remove
functions.description: Unregisters a previously added language plugin from the RLang context.
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer.
plugin must refer to a plugin that has been previously added to this RLang context.
Do not use the plugin through this RLang context after it has been removed.
Return value must be checked; false indicates the plugin was not removed.

functions.name: r_lang_use
functions.description: Selects/activates a plugin by name for subsequent operations (e.g., running code, prompt).
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string corresponding to a registered plugin's name or alias.
A plugin with the given name must have been added/available; otherwise the function may fail (check return).
Return value must be checked; false indicates selection failed.

functions.name: r_lang_use_plugin
functions.description: Selects/activates the specified plugin handle for subsequent operations without looking it up by name.
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer.
h must be a valid RLangPlugin pointer, typically one that has been added to this RLang context.
Return value must be checked; false indicates selection failed.

functions.name: r_lang_run
functions.signature: bool r_lang_run(RLang *lang, const char *code, int len);
functions.description: Executes a code buffer using the currently selected language plugin. len is the number of bytes of code to execute. Use when the input is not necessarily null-terminated or contains embedded NULs.
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer with a plugin selected (via r_lang_use or r_lang_use_plugin) that supports run.
code must be a valid pointer to a buffer containing code to execute.
len must be a non-negative integer specifying the number of bytes in code (inferred from type and common conventions).
Return value must be checked; false indicates execution failed.

functions.name: r_lang_run_string
functions.description: Executes a null-terminated code string using the currently selected language plugin. Convenience wrapper when code is a standard C string.
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer with a plugin selected that supports running strings.
code must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string.
Return value must be checked; false indicates execution failed.

functions.name: r_lang_set_user_ptr
functions.description: Associates an opaque user pointer with the RLang context. Marked in the header as TODO to deprecate; use with caution.
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer.
user is an opaque pointer; its lifetime and ownership are managed by the caller.
Callers should not rely on long-term availability of this API as it is marked for deprecation (comment note).

functions.name: r_lang_set_argv
functions.description: Sets the argument vector to pass to the active language plugin/session, analogous to process argv. Enables scripts to receive command-line-like arguments.
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer.
argc must be >= 0 (inferred from conventional argv semantics).
argv must point to an array of argc char* pointers; each element should be a null-terminated string (conventional requirement).
The memory for argv and its strings must remain valid for the duration required by the implementation (lifetime not specified).
Return value must be checked; false indicates arguments were not accepted/applied.

functions.name: r_lang_run_file
functions.description: Executes a script file using the currently selected language plugin.
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer with a plugin selected that supports file execution.
file must be a non-NULL, null-terminated path string.
The referenced file should exist and be readable by the process; path resolution and working directory semantics follow the host environment (inferred).
Return value must be checked; false indicates execution failed.

functions.name: r_lang_prompt
functions.description: Starts an interactive prompt (REPL) using the currently selected language plugin, if supported.
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer with a plugin selected that supports a prompt/REPL.
May block until the prompt session ends (typical REPL behavior; exact details unknown).
Return value must be checked; false indicates prompt could not be started or failed.

functions.name: r_lang_get_by_name
functions.description: Looks up and returns a plugin handle by its registered name or alias within the given RLang context.
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string.
Caller must handle a NULL return (plugin not found).
If a non-NULL pointer is returned, do not free it directly; its lifetime is managed by the RLang context (inferred).

functions.name: r_lang_get_by_extension
functions.description: Looks up and returns a plugin handle by file extension (e.g., the extension a plugin declares it handles) within the given RLang context.
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer.
ext must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string representing a file extension (format specifics unknown).
Caller must handle a NULL return (no matching plugin).
If a non-NULL pointer is returned, do not free it directly; its lifetime is managed by the RLang context (inferred).

functions.name: r_lang_define
functions.signature: bool r_lang_define(RLang *lang, const char *type, const char *name, void *value);
functions.description: Defines/registers a named value of a given type in the RLang context, making it available to plugins/scripts (e.g., variables, symbols, or host-provided objects). Exact semantics are not documented in this header.
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer.
type must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string describing the definition type (exact accepted values unknown).
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string naming the definition.
value is an opaque pointer associated with the definition; lifetime/ownership are caller-managed unless specified elsewhere (unknown).
Return value must be checked; false indicates the definition was not recorded.

functions.name: r_lang_undef
functions.description: Removes/un-defines a previously defined named value from the RLang context.
requirements: lang must be a valid RLang pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string corresponding to an existing definition (if none exists, behavior is unspecified here).

functions.name: r_lang_def_free
functions.description: Frees an RLangDef structure previously allocated/returned by this API. Does not remove it from the RLang context; use r_lang_undef() for removal, and r_lang_def_free() to free standalone RLangDef objects.
requirements: def must be a valid pointer to an RLangDef allocated/owned by this API.
Do not use def after this call (use-after-free).
Do not call multiple times on the same pointer (double free).

functions.name: r_cmd_new
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new RCmd command-dispatch context, optionally associating an opaque user-data pointer with it. Typical usage: create an RCmd, register commands/aliases, then call r_cmd_call to execute commands.
requirements: May return NULL on allocation failure; callers must check the return value before use.
The returned RCmd instance must be released with r_cmd_free when no longer needed.
The data argument is an opaque pointer; the function does not validate or take ownership of it (it is merely stored).

functions.name: r_cmd_free
functions.description: Release all resources held by an RCmd instance. Returns NULL for convenience so callers can write cmd = r_cmd_free(cmd).
requirements: cmd may be NULL (no effect).
After successful return, the RCmd object and its internal resources must no longer be accessed.
Return value is expected to be NULL to ease chaining; callers should not dereference it.

functions.name: r_cmd_call
functions.description: Dispatch and execute a command string within the given RCmd context, invoking the registered callback for the matching command.
requirements: cmd must be a valid, initialized RCmd pointer created by r_cmd_new.
command must be a valid, null-terminated UTF-8/ASCII string; empty or NULL commands are not valid inputs.
Return value is an int status code; callers should check it for success/failure per library conventions (specific codes not documented here).
Expected that relevant commands have been added via r_cmd_add prior to calling.

functions.name: r_cmd_set_data
functions.description: Set or replace the opaque user-data pointer stored in an RCmd context. This user data may be passed to command callbacks.
requirements: cmd must be a valid, initialized RCmd pointer.
The function does not manage the lifetime of the data pointer; callers remain responsible for its validity and lifetime.

functions.name: r_cmd_add
functions.signature: bool r_cmd_add(RCmd *cmd, const char *command, RCmdCb callback);
functions.description: Register a command string and its callback in the RCmd context so that r_cmd_call can dispatch to it.
requirements: cmd must be a valid, initialized RCmd pointer.
command must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string identifying the command to register; it should be non-empty.
callback must be a valid function pointer with signature int(void *user, const char *input).
Returns a boolean indicating success; callers should check the return value.

functions.name: r_cmd_macro_item_new
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new, empty macro item container (RCmdMacroItem) for use with the macro subsystem.
requirements: May return NULL on allocation failure; callers must check the return value.
The returned object must be freed with r_cmd_macro_item_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: r_cmd_macro_item_free
functions.description: Free an RCmdMacroItem and any resources it owns.
requirements: item may be NULL (no effect).
After calling, the item pointer must not be used.

functions.name: r_cmd_macro_init
functions.description: Initialize an RCmdMacro structure for later use (e.g., adding, listing, or invoking macros).
requirements: mac must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to storage that the caller owns.
Must be called before other r_cmd_macro_* operations that use this RCmdMacro.

functions.name: r_cmd_macro_add
functions.description: Add/register a new macro with the given name into the provided RCmdMacro context. Exact behavior and macro content population are not documented here.
requirements: mac must be a valid, initialized RCmdMacro (initialized via r_cmd_macro_init).
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string; should be non-empty.
Returns a boolean indicating success; callers should check the result.

functions.name: r_cmd_macro_rm
functions.description: Remove/unregister a macro identified by name from the RCmdMacro context.
requirements: mac must be a valid, initialized RCmdMacro.
_name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string corresponding to an existing macro name for successful removal.
Returns a boolean indicating success; callers should check the result.

functions.name: r_cmd_macro_list
functions.description: List macros from the given macro context in a mode-dependent textual form. Returns a character buffer with the listing. Exact format and mode semantics are not documented here.
requirements: mac must be a valid, initialized RCmdMacro.
mode controls output format; valid values are not documented here and should be derived from library usage.
Return value may be NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL.
Ownership and lifetime of the returned buffer are not documented here; callers should consult implementation to determine whether they must free it.

functions.name: r_cmd_macro_call
functions.description: Invoke/execute a macro by name within the given macro context.
requirements: mac must be a valid, initialized RCmdMacro.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string naming an existing macro for successful execution.
Returns an int status code; callers should check it for success/failure per library conventions (specific codes not documented).

functions.name: r_cmd_macro_break
functions.description: Signal or set a break/stop condition for macro execution, optionally using a string value (e.g., a condition or counter). Specific semantics are not documented here and are inferred from the name and fields in RCmdMacro.
requirements: mac must be a valid, initialized RCmdMacro.
value should be a valid, null-terminated string; exact accepted values/ranges are not documented.
Returns an int status code; callers should check it for success/failure.

functions.name: r_cmd_alias_del
functions.description: Delete an existing alias identified by key k from the RCmd alias table.
requirements: cmd must be a valid, initialized RCmd pointer.
k must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string key for the alias to delete.
Returns a boolean indicating success; callers should check the result.

functions.name: r_cmd_alias_keys
functions.description: Retrieve the set of alias keys currently stored in the RCmd alias table. Returns a pointer to a list/array of string keys. The array format and termination are not documented here.
requirements: cmd must be a valid, initialized RCmd pointer.
Return value may be NULL if there are no aliases or on failure; callers must check for NULL.
The caller must treat the returned strings as read-only. Ownership/lifetime of the returned array and strings are not documented; avoid modifying or freeing them without consulting implementation.

functions.name: r_cmd_alias_set_cmd
functions.signature: bool r_cmd_alias_set_cmd(RCmd *cmd, const char *k, const char *v);
functions.description: Create or update an alias such that key k maps to a command string v (to be dispatched when the alias is used).
requirements: cmd must be a valid, initialized RCmd pointer.
k and v must be non-NULL, null-terminated strings; v must represent a command (not arbitrary binary).
Returns a boolean indicating success; callers should check the result.

functions.name: r_cmd_alias_set_str
functions.signature: int r_cmd_alias_set_str(RCmd *cmd, const char *k, const char *v);
functions.description: Create or update an alias such that key k maps to a string value v (string-safe data).
requirements: cmd must be a valid, initialized RCmd pointer.
k and v must be non-NULL, null-terminated strings.
Return value is an int status/result; callers should check it (specific meaning not documented).

functions.name: r_cmd_alias_set_raw
functions.signature: int r_cmd_alias_set_raw(RCmd *cmd, const char *k, const ut8 *v, int sz);
functions.description: Create or update an alias such that key k maps to raw binary data v of size sz.
requirements: cmd must be a valid, initialized RCmd pointer.
k must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string.
If sz > 0, v must be a non-NULL pointer to at least sz bytes of readable memory; sz must be >= 0.
Return value is an int status/result; callers should check it (specific meaning not documented).

functions.name: r_cmd_alias_get
functions.description: Look up an alias by key and return an RCmdAliasVal describing the stored value (command, string, or raw data).
requirements: cmd must be a valid, initialized RCmd pointer.
k must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string key.
May return NULL if the alias does not exist or on failure; callers must check the return value.
The returned RCmdAliasVal is owned by the alias table; unless otherwise documented, do not free or modify it directly. Use r_cmd_alias_val_strdup* helpers to copy data out.

functions.name: r_cmd_alias_append_str
functions.signature: bool r_cmd_alias_append_str(RCmd *cmd, const char *k, const char *a);
functions.description: Append string data a to the existing string-type alias value identified by key k.
requirements: cmd must be a valid, initialized RCmd pointer.
k and a must be non-NULL, null-terminated strings.
The target alias must exist and be a string-type value for the append to succeed (inferred from function name).
Returns a boolean indicating success; callers should check the result.

functions.name: r_cmd_alias_append_raw
functions.signature: bool r_cmd_alias_append_raw(RCmd *cmd, const char *k, const ut8 *a, int sz);
functions.description: Append raw binary data a (length sz) to the existing raw-type alias value identified by key k.
requirements: cmd must be a valid, initialized RCmd pointer.
k must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string.
If sz > 0, a must be a non-NULL pointer to at least sz bytes; sz must be >= 0.
The target alias must exist and be a raw-data type for the append to succeed (inferred from function name).
