requirements: dbg must be valid and attached.
buf must point to an executable code buffer of length len.
len must be > 0.
ret may be NULL; if non-NULL, receives a return value.
Behavior depends on backend support.

functions.name: r_debug_map_sync
functions.description: Synchronize the debugger's memory map list with the target process.
requirements: dbg must be valid and attached.

functions.name: r_debug_stop
functions.description: Request the target to stop/interrupt execution.
requirements: dbg must be valid and target should be running/continuable.

functions.name: r_debug_frames
functions.description: Obtain a backtrace/frame list, optionally starting at address 'at'.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
Caller must free the returned list according to conventions (unknown specifics).

functions.name: r_debug_is_dead
functions.description: Return whether the debugged process/thread has terminated.
requirements: dbg must be valid.

functions.name: r_debug_map_protect
functions.signature: R_API bool r_debug_map_protect(RDebug *dbg, ut64 addr, int size, int perms)
functions.description: Change memory protection of a region starting at addr for size bytes to perms.
requirements: dbg must be valid and attached.
addr must be mapped; size > 0.
perms is a permission bitmask understood by backend.

functions.name: r_debug_arg_get
functions.signature: R_API ut64 r_debug_arg_get(RDebug *dbg, const char *cc, int num)
functions.description: Get a function argument value according to calling convention cc and ordinal num.
requirements: dbg must be valid and stopped at a call site or within a function.
cc must be a known calling convention string.
num must be >= 0 and within argument count.

functions.name: r_debug_arg_set
functions.signature: R_API bool r_debug_arg_set(RDebug *dbg, const char *cc, int num, ut64 value)
functions.description: Set a function argument value according to calling convention cc and ordinal num.
requirements: dbg must be valid and stopped in a context where arguments can be modified.
cc must be known.
num must be >= 0.

functions.name: r_debug_bp_add
functions.signature: R_API RBreakpointItem *r_debug_bp_add(RDebug *dbg, ut64 addr, int hw, bool watch, int rw, char *module, st64 m_delta)
functions.description: Add a breakpoint or watchpoint at address addr. Supports hardware/software and r/w watch flags.
requirements: dbg must be valid and attached.
addr must be a valid address in the target.
hw indicates hardware bp usage; watch/rw indicate watchpoint and access type.
module and m_delta adjust module-relative placement (usage backend-specific).
Returns an item managed by the breakpoint subsystem.

functions.name: r_debug_bp_rebase
functions.signature: R_API void r_debug_bp_rebase(RDebug *dbg, ut64 old_base, ut64 new_base)
functions.description: Rebase all breakpoints from old_base to new_base (e.g., after ASLR or module reload).
requirements: dbg must be valid.

functions.name: r_debug_bp_update
functions.description: Refresh/reinstall breakpoints after state changes.
requirements: dbg must be valid.

functions.name: r_debug_thread_list
functions.signature: R_API bool r_debug_thread_list(RDebug *dbg, int pid, char fmt)
functions.description: List threads of a process with a given format character.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
pid must refer to a process under debug.
fmt must be a supported listing format.

functions.name: r_debug_tracenodes_reset
functions.description: Reset internal trace node storage/state.
requirements: dbg must be valid.

functions.name: r_debug_trace_reset
functions.description: Reset or clear debugging instruction trace information.
requirements: dbg must be valid.

functions.name: r_debug_trace_pc
functions.description: Record or query a tracepoint at the specified program counter address.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
pc must be a valid code address.

functions.name: r_debug_trace_op
functions.description: Trace a decoded instruction (RAnalOp) for analysis/tracking.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
op must point to a valid decoded instruction structure.

functions.name: r_debug_trace_at
functions.description: Set up tracing based on an address expression or filter string.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
str must be a non-NULL expression string.

functions.name: r_debug_trace_get
functions.description: Get the tracepoint item data for a specific address, if any.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
addr is the address of interest.

functions.name: r_debug_trace_list
functions.signature: R_API void r_debug_trace_list(RDebug *dbg, int mode, ut64 offset, RTable *t)
functions.description: List tracepoints/trace data with a given mode and output into RTable.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
t may be NULL or a valid RTable* to receive rows.
mode selects listing format.
offset can filter by address.

functions.name: r_debug_trace_add
functions.signature: R_API RDebugTracepointItem *r_debug_trace_add(RDebug *dbg, ut64 addr, int size)
functions.description: Add a tracepoint covering 'size' bytes at address 'addr'.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
addr must be a valid address.
size must be > 0.

functions.name: r_debug_trace_new
functions.description: Create a new RDebugTrace container structure.
requirements: Caller must free with r_debug_trace_free().

functions.name: r_debug_trace_free
functions.description: Free an RDebugTrace container and its items.
requirements: dbg must be a pointer returned by r_debug_trace_new() or managed by library.
Do not use after freeing.

functions.name: r_debug_trace_tag
functions.description: Set or get a tag for tracing (implementation-specific).
requirements: dbg must be valid.
tag is an integer tag identifier.

functions.name: r_debug_child_fork
functions.description: Request the debuggee to fork, returning the child's PID (backend-dependent).
requirements: dbg must be valid and attached.
Underlying OS/backend must support forking under debug.

functions.name: r_debug_child_clone
functions.description: Request the debuggee to clone (create a new thread/process) and return identifier.
requirements: dbg must be valid and attached.
Backend must support clone under debug.

functions.name: r_debug_drx_list
functions.description: List hardware debug registers/watchpoints (DRx) configuration.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
Target/arch must support DRx registers.

functions.name: r_debug_drx_set
functions.signature: R_API bool r_debug_drx_set(RDebug *dbg, int idx, ut64 addr, int len, int rwx, int g)
functions.description: Configure a hardware debug register/watchpoint at index idx for address addr with length len, access rwx, and global/local flag g.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
idx must be a valid hardware debug register index for the arch.
addr must be aligned/valid for hardware watchpoints (exact alignment unspecified).
len must be supported length by hardware (e.g., 1,2,4,8).
rwx and g must be valid flag values per backend.

functions.name: r_debug_drx_get
functions.description: Return the index of a hardware debug register matching addr, or -1 if none.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
addr is a watched address.

functions.name: r_debug_drx_unset
functions.description: Disable/clear a hardware debug register at index idx.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
idx must be a valid DRx index currently in use.

functions.name: r_debug_esil_stepi
functions.description: Perform a single ESIL emulation step (instruction).
requirements: dbg must be valid.
ESIL must be initialized for the current target state (inferred).

functions.name: r_debug_esil_step
functions.description: Perform 'count' ESIL emulation steps and return a status/value.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
count may be >= 1.

functions.name: r_debug_esil_continue
functions.description: Continue ESIL emulation until a stop condition, returning a status/value.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
ESIL emulation must be configured.

functions.name: r_debug_esil_watch
functions.signature: R_API void r_debug_esil_watch(RDebug *dbg, int rwx, int dev, const char *expr)
functions.description: Set an ESIL watch on memory/register accesses matching expr with specific access flags and device id.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
expr must be a non-NULL ESIL expression string.
rwx must be a valid access mask; dev identifies the watch (semantics unspecified).

functions.name: r_debug_esil_watch_reset
functions.description: Clear all ESIL watches.
requirements: dbg must be valid.

functions.name: r_debug_esil_watch_list
functions.description: List configured ESIL watches.
requirements: dbg must be valid.

functions.name: r_debug_esil_watch_empty
functions.description: Return whether there are no ESIL watches configured.
requirements: dbg must be valid.

functions.name: r_debug_esil_prestep
functions.description: Perform pre-step ESIL hooks or configuration before stepping p times.
requirements: d must be valid.
p is the number of steps to prepare for.

functions.name: r_debug_add_checkpoint
functions.description: Create a new checkpoint of registers and memory snapshots in the current session.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
Session recording must be initialized in dbg (inferred).

functions.name: r_debug_session_add_reg_change
functions.signature: R_API bool r_debug_session_add_reg_change(RDebugSession *session, int arena, ut64 offset, ut64 data)
functions.description: Record a register change into the session at a specific arena/type and offset with the given data value.
requirements: session must be valid.
arena must be a valid R_REG_TYPE_* index.
offset must be within the register bank width for the arena (unspecified).

functions.name: r_debug_session_add_mem_change
functions.signature: R_API bool r_debug_session_add_mem_change(RDebugSession *session, ut64 addr, ut8 data)
functions.description: Record a memory byte change at address addr into the session log.
requirements: session must be valid.
addr is the address of the changed byte.

functions.name: r_debug_session_restore_reg_mem
functions.description: Restore registers and memory to the state captured at checkpoint number cnum.
requirements: dbg must be valid and have a session with checkpoints.
cnum must refer to an existing checkpoint index.

functions.name: r_debug_session_list_memory
functions.description: List recorded memory changes in the current session.
requirements: dbg must be valid and have a session.

functions.name: r_debug_session_serialize
functions.description: Serialize the debugging session to an Sdb database.
requirements: session must be valid.
db must be a valid Sdb* ready for writes.

functions.name: r_debug_session_deserialize
functions.description: Load session state from an Sdb database into the given session.
requirements: session must be valid.
db must contain a session serialization.

functions.name: r_debug_session_save
functions.description: Save the debugging session to a file.
requirements: session must be valid.
file must be a writable filesystem path.

functions.name: r_debug_session_load
functions.description: Load a debugging session from a file into dbg->session.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
file must be a readable session file path.

functions.name: r_debug_trace_ins_before
functions.description: Enable or perform instruction tracing before execution of instructions.
requirements: dbg must be valid.

functions.name: r_debug_trace_ins_after
functions.description: Enable or perform instruction tracing after execution of instructions.
requirements: dbg must be valid.

functions.name: r_debug_session_new
functions.description: Create a new empty RDebugSession for record/replay.
requirements: Caller must free with r_debug_session_free().

functions.name: r_debug_session_free
functions.description: Free an RDebugSession and associated resources.
requirements: session must be a pointer created by r_debug_session_new() or owned by dbg.
Do not use after freeing.

functions.name: r_debug_snap_map
functions.description: Create a memory snapshot of the specified map from the target process.
requirements: dbg must be valid and attached.
map must be a valid mapping from dbg's maps.
Returned RDebugSnap must be freed with r_debug_snap_free().

functions.name: r_debug_snap_contains
functions.description: Return whether the snapshot contains the specified address.
requirements: snap must be valid.
addr is the address to test.

functions.name: r_debug_snap_get_hash
functions.description: Compute and return a hash buffer for the snapshot's data.
requirements: snap must be valid.
Returned pointer points to hash data managed by snap or newly allocated (ownership unspecified).

functions.name: r_debug_snap_is_equal
functions.description: Compare two snapshots for equality (size/content/metadata).
requirements: a and b must be valid snapshots.

functions.name: r_debug_snap_free
functions.description: Free a snapshot and its resources.
requirements: snap must be a snapshot returned by r_debug_snap_map or stored in dbg.
Do not use after freeing.

functions.name: r_debug_snap_delete
functions.description: Delete a stored snapshot by index from dbg.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
idx must refer to an existing snapshot index.

functions.name: r_debug_snap_list
functions.signature: R_API void r_debug_snap_list(RDebug *dbg, int idx, int mode)
functions.description: List snapshots; optionally focus on idx and format according to mode.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
mode controls output style (unspecified).

functions.name: r_debug_snap_diff
functions.description: Compute and show differences between snapshots or between a snapshot and current memory.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
idx must refer to an existing snapshot.

functions.name: r_debug_snap
functions.description: Create a snapshot at or around a specific address (or full snapshot depending on configuration).
requirements: dbg must be valid and attached.
addr indicates region of interest; may be 0 for default behavior (unspecified).

functions.name: r_debug_snap_comment
functions.signature: R_API int r_debug_snap_comment(RDebug *dbg, int idx, const char *msg)
functions.description: Attach a comment string to a snapshot identified by idx.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
idx must be a valid snapshot index.
msg must be a non-NULL string.

functions.name: r_debug_snap_all
functions.description: Create snapshots of all maps matching permissions mask perms.
requirements: dbg must be valid and attached.
perms is a permission bitmask.

functions.name: r_debug_step_back
functions.description: Reverse-step execution by restoring previous checkpoints/states.
requirements: dbg must be valid and have checkpoints/session support.
steps should be >= 1.

functions.name: r_debug_goto_cnum
functions.description: Restore and jump to a specific checkpoint number cnum in the session.
requirements: dbg must be valid.
cnum must refer to an existing checkpoint.

functions.name: r_debug_step_cnum
functions.description: Move forward/backward between checkpoints by a number of steps (session-based stepping).
requirements: dbg must be valid and session initialized.
steps can be positive or negative depending on semantics (unspecified).

functions.name: r_debug_continue_back
functions.description: Reverse-continue execution until a previous stop condition using recorded state.
requirements: dbg must be valid and have a session with checkpoints.

functions.name: r_debug_ptrace
functions.signature: static inline long r_debug_ptrace(RDebug *dbg, r_ptrace_request_t request, pid_t pid, void *addr, r_ptrace_data_t data)
functions.description: Thin wrapper that forwards to the bound IO ptrace implementation: dbg->iob.ptrace(...). Only available when HAVE_PTRACE is defined.
requirements: HAVE_PTRACE must be enabled at compile time.
dbg must be valid and dbg->iob.ptrace must be initialized.
request, pid, addr, data must be valid for the platform ptrace API.

functions.name: r_debug_ptrace_func
functions.description: Invoke a function via the backend's ptrace_func trampoline, useful for running code under ptrace context.
requirements: HAVE_PTRACE must be enabled at compile time.
dbg must be valid and dbg->iob.ptrace_func must be initialized.
func must be a valid callable pointer; user is passed through.

functions.name: r_egg_new
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new REgg context used to build/compile shellcode or small binaries. Typical usage: create with r_egg_new, configure/load, then compile/assemble and free with r_egg_free.
requirements: Returns a newly allocated REgg pointer on success or NULL on failure.
Caller is responsible for releasing the object with r_egg_free.

functions.name: r_egg_lang_init
functions.description: Initialize the language subsystem inside an existing REgg context (parser/emitter state). Usually called by setup routines; call explicitly if you manually prepare REgg internals.
requirements: egg must be a valid, initialized REgg* (e.g., from r_egg_new).
Must not be called with NULL.

functions.name: r_egg_lang_free
functions.description: Release language/parser-related resources held inside the REgg context without destroying the REgg itself.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
After this call, language-specific operations may not be valid until reinitialized.
Must not be called with NULL.

functions.name: r_egg_tostring
functions.description: Return a textual representation of the current egg state or generated code as a newly allocated string. Exact content is implementation-defined.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
Returned char* must be freed by the caller using the appropriate deallocator for this library (typically free or r_* equivalent).
May return NULL on failure.

functions.name: r_egg_free
functions.description: Destroy and free an REgg context and all resources owned by it.
requirements: egg may be NULL (then no action).
Do not use the REgg* after this call (dangling pointer).

functions.name: r_egg_plugin_add
functions.description: Register an REgg plugin (e.g., encoder or shellcode provider) with the given REgg instance.
requirements: a must be a valid REgg*.
plugin must be a valid REggPlugin* with required fields initialized (meta, type, build callback).
Returns true on success, false on failure (e.g., duplicate or invalid).

functions.name: r_egg_plugin_remove
functions.description: Unregister a previously added plugin from the REgg instance.
requirements: a must be a valid REgg*.
plugin must be a valid REggPlugin* that was previously added to this REgg.
Returns true on success, false on failure.

functions.name: r_egg_reset
functions.description: Reset the REgg context to a clean state, clearing accumulated source/output and parser state while keeping the object allocated.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
After reset, previously obtained pointers to internal buffers (e.g., source/assembly) may become invalid.

functions.name: r_egg_setup
functions.signature: bool r_egg_setup(REgg *egg, const char *arch, int bits, int endian, const char *os)
functions.description: Configure the target architecture, bitness, endianness, and OS for code generation/assembly.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
arch must reference a supported architecture string (e.g., "x86", "arm"); exact accepted values are implementation-defined.
bits typically must match target (e.g., 32 or 64).
endian should be 0/1 or library-defined values indicating endianness; exact semantics implementation-defined.
os must be a supported OS string (e.g., "linux", "windows", "darwin") or NULL to use defaults.
Returns true on success, false if configuration is unsupported/invalid.

functions.name: r_egg_include
functions.signature: bool r_egg_include(REgg *egg, const char *file, int format)
functions.description: Include a file (source or binary) into the egg, using a specified format identifier.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
file must be a non-NULL path to a readable file.
format must be a valid format code for this API; acceptable values are implementation-defined.
Returns true on success, false on failure (e.g., file not found/invalid format).

functions.name: r_egg_include_str
functions.description: Include inline content (e.g., source snippet or directive) specified by a string into the egg.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
arg must be a non-NULL, properly formatted include specification; exact syntax is implementation-defined.
Returns true on success, false on failure.

functions.name: r_egg_load
functions.signature: void r_egg_load(REgg *egg, const char *code, int format)
functions.description: Load source code or data into the egg using the specified format. This stages content for later compile/assemble.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
code may be NULL or a non-NULL string according to format expectations; exact format semantics are implementation-defined.
format must be a valid format code for this API.

functions.name: r_egg_syscall
functions.description: Append or emit a syscall via the language/emitter using a format-like specifier and variadic arguments. Used when building shellcode that performs system calls.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
arg must be a non-NULL format/spec string; expected format and argument types are implementation-defined.
Variadic arguments must match the spec in arg to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: r_egg_alloc
functions.description: Allocate space/resources within the egg for variables or buffer of size n (semantics depend on current language/emitter).
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
n should be non-negative; exact constraints are implementation-defined.

functions.name: r_egg_label
functions.description: Define a label in the generated code for branching or calls.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
name must be a non-NULL label identifier acceptable to the target language/emitter (exact constraints implementation-defined).

functions.name: r_egg_raw
functions.signature: bool r_egg_raw(REgg *egg, const ut8 *b, int len)
functions.description: Append raw bytes to the output buffer being built by the egg.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
If len > 0, b must be a non-NULL pointer to at least len bytes.
len must be >= 0.
Returns true on success, false on failure (e.g., allocation error).

functions.name: r_egg_encode
functions.description: Apply a named encoder plugin to the current output (e.g., to obfuscate shellcode).
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
name must be a non-NULL encoder name corresponding to a registered encoder plugin.
Returns true on success, false if the encoder is not found or fails.

functions.name: r_egg_shellcode
functions.description: Select or build a named shellcode from registered shellcode plugins and add it to the egg.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
name must be a non-NULL shellcode plugin name.
Returns true on success, false on failure (e.g., plugin not found).

functions.name: r_egg_option_set
functions.signature: void r_egg_option_set(REgg *egg, const char *k, const char *v)
functions.description: Set a key/value option in the egg context that affects compilation/assembly or plugins.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
k must be a non-NULL option key string.
v may be NULL or a string depending on the option; semantics implementation-defined.

functions.name: r_egg_option_get
functions.description: Get the current value of an option by key. Returns a string (ownership/alloc semantics implementation-defined).
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
k must be a non-NULL option key string.
May return NULL if the key is unset or on failure.

functions.name: r_egg_if
functions.signature: void r_egg_if(REgg *egg, const char *reg, char cmp, int v)
functions.description: Emit a conditional construct comparing a register/value to an integer using a comparison operator, influencing subsequent emitted control flow.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
reg must be a non-NULL register/operand name understood by the emitter.
cmp is a comparison operator character; accepted values are implementation-defined (e.g., '=', '!', '<', '>').
v is the integer to compare against.

functions.name: r_egg_printf
functions.description: Append a formatted comment or directive to the egg using printf-style formatting. Often used to add assembly comments via the emitter.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
fmt must be a non-NULL printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: r_egg_compile
functions.description: Compile the loaded source or language constructs into target code or intermediate assembly ready for assembly/output.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
Returns true on success, false on failure (e.g., parse/compile error).
Caller should have previously configured the target (e.g., r_egg_setup) and loaded/added content; exact prerequisites implementation-defined.

functions.name: r_egg_padding
functions.description: Apply padding policy/content to the output (e.g., NOP sled), according to a pad specification string.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
pad must be a non-NULL padding specification; exact syntax implementation-defined.
Returns true on success, false on failure.

functions.name: r_egg_assemble
functions.description: Assemble generated assembly into machine code and store it in the egg's output buffer.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
Returns true on success, false on failure (e.g., assembler error).
Typically called after r_egg_compile or after appending assembly directly.

functions.name: r_egg_assemble_asm
functions.description: Assemble a provided list/array of assembly strings into machine code using the egg's assembler configuration.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
asm_list must be a non-NULL pointer to a sequence of strings; exact termination convention (e.g., NULL-terminated) is implementation-defined.
Returns true on success, false on failure.

functions.name: r_egg_pattern
functions.description: Generate and append a recognizable pattern of given size to the output (e.g., for offset discovery).
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
size must be >= 0; very large sizes may fail due to memory limits.

functions.name: r_egg_get_bin
functions.description: Return the current binary output buffer containing compiled/assembled bytes.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
May return NULL if no output is available or on failure.
The returned RBuffer is owned by the REgg; do not free directly unless API specifies otherwise.

functions.name: r_egg_get_source
functions.description: Retrieve the current source text accumulated in the egg as a C-string.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
Returned pointer may be owned by the REgg or newly allocated; ownership semantics are implementation-defined.
May return NULL if no source or on failure.

functions.name: r_egg_get_assembly
functions.description: Retrieve the generated assembly text produced by compile steps.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
May return NULL if assembly is not available or on failure.
Ownership/lifetime semantics of the returned string are implementation-defined.

functions.name: r_egg_append
functions.description: Append source or assembly text to the egg's source buffer.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
src must be a non-NULL C-string to append.

functions.name: r_egg_run
functions.description: Execute or emulate the generated code in a controlled context. Exact behavior and return value semantics are implementation-defined.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
Typically requires successful assemble/compile and a runnable payload.
Returns an integer status/result; negative or specific values may indicate errors (implementation-defined).

functions.name: r_egg_run_rop
functions.description: Execute or emulate a ROP-chain built in the egg context. Exact behavior and return semantics are implementation-defined.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
Requires that a valid ROP chain has been prepared within the egg.
Returns an integer status/result (implementation-defined).

functions.name: r_egg_patch
functions.signature: bool r_egg_patch(REgg *egg, int off, const ut8 *b, int l)
functions.description: Patch the output buffer at the given offset with l bytes from b.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
off must be >= 0 and within current buffer bounds for the patch range; exact boundary handling is implementation-defined.
If l > 0, b must be non-NULL and point to at least l bytes.
l must be >= 0.
Returns true on success, false on failure (e.g., out-of-range).

functions.name: r_egg_finalize
functions.description: Finalize the egg after build/assemble, performing any pending fixups or cleanups required before retrieval or execution.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
Should be called after all modifications; exact necessity and effects are implementation-defined.

functions.name: r_egg_cfile_parser
functions.signature: char *r_egg_cfile_parser(const char *file, const char *arch, const char *os, int bits)
functions.description: Parse a C source file and produce egg-compatible source or directives tailored for the specified target arch/os/bits. Returns a newly allocated string with the parsed output.
requirements: file must be a non-NULL path to a readable C source file.
arch/os must be strings acceptable to the parser; bits indicates target bitness (e.g., 32 or 64).
Returns NULL on failure.
Returned string must be freed by the caller.

functions.name: r_egg_mkvar
functions.signature: char *r_egg_mkvar(REgg *egg, char *out, const char *_str, int delta)
functions.description: Create/format a variable name or reference based on input string and a context delta, writing it into out and returning out.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
out must be a non-NULL buffer large enough to hold the resulting string.
_str must be a non-NULL input string.
delta is an integer adjustment; exact semantics are implementation-defined.
Returns out on success; may return NULL on failure.

functions.name: r_egg_lang_parsechar
functions.description: Feed a single character to the egg language parser/state machine, advancing parsing and returning a status code.
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
Function is typically called repeatedly for each input character.
Return value semantics are implementation-defined (e.g., 0/1 or error codes).

functions.name: r_egg_lang_include_path
functions.description: Add a directory path to the include search paths used by the egg language (e.g., for #include).
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
path must be a non-NULL string to an existing directory (existence may be checked at use time).

functions.name: r_egg_lang_include_init
functions.description: Initialize include handling for the egg language (e.g., default paths or tables).
requirements: egg must be a valid REgg*.
Must not be called with NULL.

functions.name: r_codemeta_item_fini
functions.description: Finalize (tear down) an RCodeMetaItem in place by releasing any resources owned by the item (e.g., strings within union fields) without freeing the item memory itself. Use when an item’s lifetime ends but the memory is managed externally or embedded in a container.
requirements: e must point to a valid, initialized RCodeMetaItem instance.
Caller must not pass NULL unless the implementation explicitly tolerates it (behavior otherwise unknown).
After calling, the fields inside e should be considered cleared; do not reuse without reinitialization.
This does not free e itself; if heap-allocated, free it separately (e.g., with r_codemeta_item_free if appropriate).

functions.name: r_codemeta_new
functions.description: Create a new RCodeMeta object to hold decompiled code and its annotations. The resulting object owns its internal code string as per the structure comment.
requirements: code should be a valid, null-terminated C string; passing NULL is unspecified.
Returned pointer must be released with r_codemeta_free when no longer needed.
The RCodeMeta instance owns its internal code buffer and is responsible for freeing it (caller must not free or modify internal pointers directly).

functions.name: r_codemeta_free
functions.description: Destroy and free an RCodeMeta, releasing its code string, annotations vector, tree, and any associated resources.
requirements: code must be a pointer previously obtained from r_codemeta_new or r_codemeta_clone (or otherwise valid).
After calling, code becomes invalid and must not be used.
Calling with NULL is unspecified (likely a no-op in many APIs but not guaranteed).

functions.name: r_codemeta_item_new
functions.description: Allocate and return a new, heap-allocated RCodeMetaItem, typically initialized to defaults for later population and insertion into RCodeMeta.
requirements: Returned pointer must be freed with r_codemeta_item_free (or finalized with r_codemeta_item_fini if embedded and freed elsewhere).
Initialize fields as needed before use if not already zero-initialized by the implementation (initialization details unknown).

functions.name: r_codemeta_item_free
functions.description: Free a heap-allocated RCodeMetaItem, releasing any internal resources and the item’s memory.
requirements: e must be a pointer previously allocated by r_codemeta_item_new or equivalent.
After calling, e is invalid and must not be used.
Passing NULL is unspecified.

functions.name: r_codemeta_item_is_reference
functions.description: Return true if the given annotation item encodes a reference (e.g., function/global/local/constant with name/offset) rather than plain metadata. Likely checks the type/union to determine if it uses the 'reference' variant.
requirements: annotation must point to a valid, initialized RCodeMetaItem.
Behavior for NULL is unspecified.
Does not modify the item.

functions.name: r_codemeta_item_is_variable
functions.description: Return true if the given annotation item represents a variable (e.g., function parameter, local, global, constant) based on its type. Likely checks R_CODEMETA_TYPE_*_VARIABLE or FUNCTION_PARAMETER and related fields.
requirements: annotation must point to a valid, initialized RCodeMetaItem.
Behavior for NULL is unspecified.
Does not modify the item.

functions.name: r_codemeta_add_item
functions.description: Add an annotation item to the RCodeMeta’s annotations collection and update any related indexing structures (e.g., tree). Provided as r_codemeta_add_annotation for compatibility.
requirements: code must be a valid RCodeMeta pointer (created by r_codemeta_new/clone).
annotation must be a valid, initialized RCodeMetaItem describing a range within code->code; start/end should form a valid range (exact constraints unknown).

Ownership transfer of annotation after insertion is unknown; assume the RCodeMeta will manage the item’s lifetime once added (based on typical container semantics), but this is not explicitly documented.

functions.name: r_codemeta_print
functions.description: Render the annotated decompiled code as a printable string, likely applying or embedding annotations and optionally returning line offset mapping via line_offsets.
requirements: code must be a valid RCodeMeta with populated code and annotations.
line_offsets, if non-NULL, should be a valid RVecCodeMetaOffset pointer prepared according to the vector API; ownership and fill behavior are unspecified.
Returns a char* string; allocation/ownership of the returned buffer is not documented—callers likely must free it, but this is unknown.

functions.name: r_codemeta_print2
functions.description: Render the annotated code with additional analysis context anal (e.g., to resolve names or formats) and optionally produce line offset mapping.
requirements: code must be a valid RCodeMeta.
anal must be a valid analysis/context pointer for the expected backend; exact type and lifetime are unknown.
line_offsets usage as in r_codemeta_print; ownership of returned char* is not documented (likely needs to be freed).

functions.name: r_codemeta_print_disasm
functions.description: Render a disassembly-oriented view of the code/annotations using analysis context anal, optionally providing line offset mapping.
requirements: code must be a valid RCodeMeta.
anal must be a valid analysis/context pointer compatible with disassembly rendering; exact type unknown.
line_offsets handling as in r_codemeta_print; ownership of returned char* is not documented (likely needs to be freed).

functions.name: r_codemeta_print_comment_cmds
functions.description: Generate a textual list of comment commands derived from annotations (e.g., commands to attach comments/metadata in an external tool).
requirements: code must be a valid RCodeMeta.
Returns a char* string; allocation/ownership policy is not documented (likely caller-freed).

functions.name: r_codemeta_print_json
functions.description: Serialize the annotations and code metadata to a JSON string for consumption by external tools or UIs.
requirements: code must be a valid RCodeMeta.
Returns a char* JSON string; allocation/ownership policy is not documented (likely caller-freed).

functions.name: r_codemeta_at
functions.description: Retrieve the list (vector) of annotation items that are associated with a given character offset within the decompiled code.
requirements: code must be a valid RCodeMeta.
offset should be within the bounds of the code string (0 <= offset < strlen(code->code)); exact bounds handling on out-of-range is unknown.
Returns a pointer to a vector (RVecCodeMetaItemPtr*); ownership and lifetime of the returned vector are not documented (may be newly allocated or borrowed; unknown).

functions.name: r_codemeta_in
functions.signature: R_API RVecCodeMetaItemPtr *r_codemeta_in(RCodeMeta *code, size_t start, size_t end);
functions.description: Retrieve the list (vector) of annotation items that intersect or lie within the [start, end) range of the decompiled code.
requirements: code must be a valid RCodeMeta.
start and end should define a valid range with start <= end and within the bounds of the code string; exact inclusion and out-of-range behavior unknown.
Returns a pointer to a vector (RVecCodeMetaItemPtr*); ownership/lifetime unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: r_codemeta_line_offsets
functions.description: Compute or return the vector of line start offsets for the current code representation, useful for mapping byte/char offsets to line numbers.
requirements: code must be a valid RCodeMeta with a non-NULL code string.
Returns a pointer to RVecCodeMetaOffset; whether this is owned by caller or by code is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: r_codemeta_item_clone
functions.description: Deep-clone an RCodeMetaItem, duplicating its range, type, and any referenced data (e.g., strings) to produce an independent copy.
requirements: code must be a valid, initialized RCodeMetaItem pointer.
Returned item must be freed with r_codemeta_item_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: r_codemeta_clone
functions.description: Deep-clone an RCodeMeta, duplicating its code string, annotations, and internal indices/structures to produce an independent metadata object.
requirements: code must be a valid RCodeMeta pointer.
Returned RCodeMeta must be freed with r_codemeta_free when no longer needed.
Cloned object’s internal data are independent; callers should not share or free internal pointers directly.

functions.name: r_magic_new
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new magic context. The context controls how subsequent identification operations behave via the flags bitmask (R_MAGIC_*). Typical usage: create the context, load magic data (r_magic_load or r_magic_load_buffer), then query files/buffers, and finally free the context.
requirements: flags is a bitmask composed of R_MAGIC_* constants defined in this header; values outside these bits are unspecified.
Must be called before any other r_magic_* operations that require a valid RMagic instance.
The returned RMagic* must later be released with r_magic_free to avoid leaks.
If allocation fails, the function may return NULL; callers must handle a NULL return.

functions.name: r_magic_free
functions.description: Releases a magic context created by r_magic_new, freeing associated resources.
requirements: The argument must be a valid RMagic* previously returned by r_magic_new and not already freed.
After this call, the RMagic* must not be used again.
Passing NULL is unspecified by this header; caller should avoid passing NULL unless implementation guarantees it is safe.

functions.name: r_magic_file
functions.description: Identifies the type of a filesystem object given its path and returns a human-readable description or MIME information depending on flags. Expected usage: create context, load magic data, then call this to classify a file path.
requirements: The RMagic* must be a valid, initialized magic context (typically from r_magic_new) and not freed.
The magic database should be loaded (e.g., via r_magic_load or r_magic_load_buffer) before calling, otherwise results are unspecified.
The path argument should be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string referencing an accessible file. Behavior for non-existent or inaccessible paths is unspecified here.
The returned const char* points to internal storage whose lifetime/ownership is unspecified in the header; callers should copy the string if they need to retain it.

functions.name: r_magic_descriptor
functions.description: Identifies the type of data referenced by an open file descriptor and returns a descriptive string (or MIME) depending on flags.
requirements: The RMagic* must be a valid, initialized magic context and not freed.
The magic database should be loaded before calling, otherwise results are unspecified.
The descriptor must be a valid open file descriptor referring to a readable object; the header does not define whether the current file offset is used or preserved.
The returned const char* points to internal storage; lifetime/ownership is unspecified—copy if you need to keep it.

functions.name: r_magic_buffer
functions.description: Identifies the type of the given in-memory buffer and returns a descriptive string (or MIME) depending on flags. Useful for classifying data without touching the filesystem.
requirements: The RMagic* must be a valid, initialized magic context and not freed.
The magic database should be loaded before calling, otherwise results are unspecified.
The buffer pointer must be non-NULL if size > 0; size is the number of bytes available at buffer.
The returned const char* points to internal storage; lifetime/ownership is unspecified—copy if you need to retain it.

functions.name: r_magic_error
functions.description: Returns a textual description of the last error that occurred in the magic context, or possibly NULL if no error is recorded. Intended for diagnostics after a failing operation such as load or classification.
requirements: The RMagic* must be a valid magic context.
Callers should not assume a non-NULL return; handle NULL as 'no error' or unavailable message.
The returned pointer refers to internal storage; lifetime is unspecified—copy if you need to retain it.

functions.name: r_magic_setflags
functions.description: Sets or updates the behavior flags for a magic context. Flags control output format and checking behavior (e.g., R_MAGIC_MIME, R_MAGIC_RAW, R_MAGIC_CONTINUE).
requirements: The RMagic* must be a valid magic context.
flags is a bitmask composed of R_MAGIC_* constants defined in this header; semantics of each flag follow their names (e.g., R_MAGIC_MIME returns MIME info).
May be called before classification operations to affect their behavior; ordering relative to r_magic_load is not specified.

functions.name: r_magic_from_ebcdic
functions.signature: void r_magic_from_ebcdic(const ut8 *src, size_t src_len, ut8 *dst);
functions.description: Converts EBCDIC-encoded bytes to another encoding (likely ASCII/UTF-8) into dst. Intended to preprocess data for classification. Exact mapping is not detailed in the header.
requirements: src must point to at least src_len bytes of readable memory.
dst must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the converted output; the exact required size is unknown from this header.
Behavior for overlapping src and dst is unspecified.
The conversion mapping and whether output is NUL-terminated are not specified.

functions.name: r_magic_load
functions.description: Loads magic pattern data (the database used for type identification) from a path. Must generally be called before performing identification. The path may refer to a magic file or directory; exact search behavior is not specified here.
requirements: The RMagic* must be a valid magic context.
The path should be a valid NUL-terminated string referencing readable magic data. Whether NULL uses a default path is unspecified in this header.
Returns true on success, false on failure; on failure, callers may query r_magic_error and r_magic_errno.

functions.name: r_magic_load_buffer
functions.signature: bool r_magic_load_buffer(RMagic *, const ut8 *data, size_t len);
functions.description: Loads magic pattern data from an in-memory buffer instead of a file. Useful for embedded or prepackaged magic databases.
requirements: The RMagic* must be a valid magic context.
data must point to at least len bytes of readable memory containing a valid magic database format; format details are not specified here.
Returns true on success, false on failure; on failure, callers may query r_magic_error and r_magic_errno.

functions.name: r_magic_compile
functions.description: Compiles magic source files into a compiled form. This is typically used to preprocess or validate magic definitions. Exact output and destination are not defined by this header.
requirements: The RMagic* must be a valid magic context.
The path should name a magic source file or directory; specifics are not provided.
Returns true on success, false on failure; consult r_magic_error/r_magic_errno on failure.

functions.name: r_magic_check
functions.description: Checks the syntax/consistency of magic files at the given path. Intended for validating magic definitions without loading them for classification.
requirements: The RMagic* must be a valid magic context.
The path should reference magic files/directories to check; specifics are not provided.
Returns true on success, false on failure; consult r_magic_error/r_magic_errno on failure.

functions.name: r_magic_errno
functions.description: Returns an implementation-defined error code associated with the last failure on this magic context. Can be used in conjunction with r_magic_error for diagnostics.
requirements: The RMagic* must be a valid magic context.
The meaning and range of the returned int are not specified in this header; callers should treat non-zero as an error by convention, but this is not guaranteed.

functions.name: r_muta_init
functions.description: Initialize an RMuta context, preparing it to register and use crypto/base/hash/sign plugins and create sessions. Typical usage: allocate an RMuta with r_muta_new(), then call r_muta_init() before adding plugins or creating sessions.
requirements: cry must be a valid, writable pointer to an RMuta structure (typically created by r_muta_new()).
Call before using other RMuta operations that depend on initialization (e.g., r_muta_add, creating sessions).

functions.name: r_muta_add
functions.description: Register a plugin (algorithm implementation) with the RMuta context so it can be discovered/used by name or directly. Returns true on success.
requirements: cry must be a valid, initialized RMuta pointer (e.g., after r_muta_init).
h must point to a valid RMutaPlugin (usually one of the provided extern plugin symbols or a correctly populated plugin struct).

functions.name: r_muta_new
functions.description: Allocate and construct a new RMuta context. Use r_muta_init() on the returned object before adding plugins or creating sessions. Free with r_muta_free().
requirements: Must be paired with r_muta_free() to avoid leaks.
Check the return value for NULL to handle allocation failure.

functions.name: r_muta_free
functions.description: Free an RMuta context and any resources it owns. After this call, the pointer must not be used.
requirements: cry must be a valid RMuta pointer previously obtained from r_muta_new().
All associated sessions should be properly ended/freed before freeing the parent context (exact ownership semantics beyond this are unknown).

functions.name: r_muta_list
functions.description: Return a textual listing of available algorithms/plugins in the RMuta context filtered by type and mode. The string format and ownership are not specified in this header.
requirements: cry must be a valid RMuta pointer.
type must be a valid RMutaType (e.g., R_MUTA_TYPE_HASH, R_MUTA_TYPE_CRYPTO, etc., or R_MUTA_TYPE_ALL).
mode is expected to be one of the R_CRYPTO_MODE_* values when relevant; exact filtering semantics are not documented here.
Caller must handle a possible NULL return on failure.
Memory ownership/lifetime of the returned char* is unknown from this header (whether the caller must free it is unspecified).

functions.name: r_muta_use
functions.description: [Deprecated] Create a session for a named algorithm registered in the RMuta context. Superseded by r_muta_new_session().
requirements: cry must be a valid RMuta pointer with the desired plugin already registered via r_muta_add().
algo must be a non-NULL, null-terminated algorithm name recognized by a registered plugin.
Caller must check for NULL return to handle lookup or creation failure.
As deprecated, prefer using r_muta_new_session().

functions.name: r_muta_session_set_key
functions.signature: bool r_muta_session_set_key(RMutaSession *cry, const ut8 *key, int keylen, int mode, int direction);
functions.description: Set the key (and mode/direction) on an existing RMutaSession for encryption/decryption or hashing as applicable. Returns true on success.
requirements: cry must be a valid RMutaSession pointer.
key must point to at least keylen bytes; must be non-NULL when keylen > 0.
keylen must be >= 0; the correct size may be constrained by the plugin’s get_key_size() (not specified here).
mode should be one of R_CRYPTO_MODE_ECB/CBC/OFB/CFB when applicable to the algorithm.
direction should be one of R_CRYPTO_DIR_DECRYPT/R_CRYPTO_DIR_ENCRYPT/R_CRYPTO_DIR_HASH as appropriate for the algorithm.
Caller must handle false return on invalid parameters or unsupported configuration.

functions.name: r_muta_session_set_iv
functions.signature: bool r_muta_session_set_iv(RMutaSession *cry, const ut8 *iv, int ivlen);
functions.description: Set the initialization vector (IV) for the current session when required by the algorithm/mode. Returns true on success.
requirements: cry must be a valid RMutaSession pointer.
iv must point to at least ivlen bytes; must be non-NULL when ivlen > 0.
ivlen must be >= 0; the correct size is algorithm/mode-specific and not specified here.
Caller must handle false return on invalid IV size or when IV is not applicable.

functions.name: r_muta_new_session
functions.description: Create and initialize a new RMutaSession for the named algorithm, optionally using RMutaOptions (e.g., key, IV, direction). Returns the new session or NULL on failure.
requirements: mu must be a valid RMuta pointer with plugins registered.
algo must be a non-NULL, null-terminated algorithm name supported by a registered plugin.
opt may be NULL or point to an options struct; when provided, fields such as key/iv/key_len/direction should match the algorithm’s expectations (specifics not detailed in this header).
Caller must check for NULL return and handle failure.

functions.name: r_muta_session_new
functions.description: Create a new session directly from a specific plugin instance rather than by name. Returns a session or NULL on failure.
requirements: cry must be a valid RMuta pointer.
cp must be a valid RMutaPlugin pointer corresponding to an implementation added/available for use.
Caller must check for NULL return.

functions.name: r_muta_session_free
functions.description: Free a session and any resources/buffers it holds. After this call the session pointer must not be used.
requirements: cj must be a valid RMutaSession pointer created by one of the session creation functions.
If the algorithm requires a finalize step, ensure it is performed before freeing (e.g., via r_muta_session_end); exact requirements are not specified here.

functions.name: r_muta_begin
functions.description: Begin a new, generic session on the RMuta context (plugin/algorithm selection and configuration likely performed later via other calls). Returns the session or NULL on failure.
requirements: cry must be a valid RMuta pointer.
Caller must check for NULL return.
Subsequent configuration (key, IV, mode, direction, plugin) may be required before update/end; exact sequence is not specified in this header.

functions.name: r_muta_session_update
functions.signature: bool r_muta_session_update(RMutaSession *cry, const ut8 *buf, int len);
functions.description: Process (incrementally) a chunk of input data in the active session. Returns true on success. Intended to be called zero or more times prior to r_muta_session_end().
requirements: cry must be a valid RMutaSession pointer.
buf must point to at least len bytes; may be NULL only if len == 0 (conservative inference from common patterns).
len must be >= 0.
Caller must handle false return and not assume output is produced for every call (depends on algorithm).

functions.name: r_muta_session_end
functions.signature: bool r_muta_session_end(RMutaSession *cry, const ut8 *buf, int len);
functions.description: Finalize the session, optionally processing a final chunk of input and producing any final output (e.g., padding, digest). Returns true on success.
requirements: cry must be a valid RMutaSession pointer.
buf must point to at least len bytes; may be NULL only if len == 0 (conservative inference).
len must be >= 0.
Must be called at most once per session to finalize; further updates after end are invalid (exact enforcement unspecified).
Caller must handle false return on failure.

functions.name: r_muta_session_append
functions.signature: int r_muta_session_append(RMutaSession *cry, const ut8 *buf, int len);
functions.description: Append raw data to the session’s output buffer (or feed-and-append, depending on implementation). Returns an integer (likely the number of bytes appended or a status code).
requirements: cry must be a valid RMutaSession pointer.
buf must point to at least len bytes; should not be NULL unless len == 0 (inferred).
len must be >= 0.
Caller must check the return value for failure (negative or zero semantics are not specified in this header).

functions.name: r_muta_session_get_output
functions.description: Obtain a pointer to the session’s accumulated output buffer and optionally its current size. Ownership and lifetime of the returned buffer are not specified in this header; likely managed by the session.
requirements: cry must be a valid RMutaSession pointer.
size is an output parameter for the buffer length; whether NULL is allowed is unspecified.
Caller must not assume the returned pointer is valid after subsequent session operations unless documented elsewhere (ownership/lifetime unspecified).
Caller must handle a possible NULL return on error or when no output is available.

functions.name: r_main_new
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new RMain structure representing a program entrypoint wrapper, identified by name. Use this to set up an RMain before running it via r_main_run. Returns a pointer to the newly created RMain or NULL on failure.
requirements: name should be a non-NULL pointer to a null-terminated string
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use
The returned RMain* must be released with r_main_free to avoid leaks

functions.name: r_main_free
functions.description: Releases resources associated with an RMain created by r_main_new. After this call, the pointer must not be used.
requirements: m must be a valid pointer previously returned by r_main_new (and not already freed)
Do not use m after calling this function

functions.name: r_main_run
functions.signature: R_API int r_main_run(RMain *m, int argc, const char **argv);
functions.description: Runs the RMain entrypoint with the provided command-line arguments. Typically dispatches to the configured main-like callback inside RMain. Returns a process-like exit status code.
requirements: m must be a valid, initialized RMain pointer (e.g., from r_main_new)
argc must be >= 0
argv must point to an array with at least argc elements
Each argv[i] for 0 <= i < argc must be a valid null-terminated string
Caller should handle the returned status code (0 for success, non-zero for error as per the underlying tool’s conventions)

functions.name: r_main_version_print
functions.signature: R_API int r_main_version_print(const char *program, int rad);
functions.description: Prints version information for the specified program (and possibly radare2 components), controlled by the rad flag. Returns an exit status compatible integer.
requirements: program should be a non-NULL pointer to a null-terminated string naming the program
rad is an integer flag; non-zero typically enables additional radare2-related version output (inferred)
Caller should handle the integer return code

functions.name: r_main_ravc2
functions.signature: R_API int r_main_ravc2(int argc, const char **argv);
functions.description: Entry point wrapper for the ravc2 tool, taking standard argc/argv and returning an exit status. Intended to be called like a main() for that tool.
requirements: argc must be >= 0
argv must point to an array with at least argc elements
Each argv[i] for 0 <= i < argc must be a valid null-terminated string
Caller should interpret the return value as an exit status

functions.name: r_main_rax2

functions.description: Entry point wrapper for the rax2 tool (radare2 hex/arith converter). Accepts argc/argv and returns an exit status.

functions.name: r_main_rarun2
functions.signature: R_API int r_main_rarun2(int argc, const char **argv);
functions.description: Entry point wrapper for the rarun2 tool. Processes command-line arguments and returns an exit status.
requirements: argc must be >= 0
argv must point to an array with at least argc elements
Each argv[i] must be a valid null-terminated string

functions.name: r_main_rahash2
functions.signature: R_API int r_main_rahash2(int argc, const char **argv);
functions.description: Entry point wrapper for the rahash2 hashing tool. Standard main-like signature; returns exit status.
requirements: argc must be >= 0
argv must point to an array with at least argc elements

functions.name: r_main_rabin2
functions.signature: R_API int r_main_rabin2(int argc, const char **argv);
functions.description: Entry point wrapper for the rabin2 binary inspection tool. Standard main-like signature; returns exit status.

functions.signature: R_API int r_main_radare2(int argc, const char **argv);
functions.description: Entry point wrapper for the radare2 executable itself. Accepts command-line arguments and returns a process-like exit status.

functions.name: r_main_rasm2
functions.signature: R_API int r_main_rasm2(int argc, const char **argv);
functions.description: Entry point wrapper for the rasm2 assembler/disassembler tool. Uses standard argc/argv; returns exit status.
requirements: argc must be >= 0

functions.name: r_main_r2agent
functions.signature: R_API int r_main_r2agent(int argc, const char **argv);
functions.description: Entry point wrapper for the r2agent tool/service. Processes command-line arguments, returns exit status.
requirements: argc must be >= 0
argv must point to an array with at least argc elements
Each argv[i] must be a valid null-terminated string
Caller should handle the exit status

functions.name: r_main_rafind2
functions.signature: R_API int r_main_rafind2(int argc, const char **argv);
functions.description: Entry point wrapper for the rafind2 searching tool. Standard main-like signature; returns exit status.
requirements: argc must be >= 0
argv must point to an array with at least argc elements
Each argv[i] must be a valid null-terminated string
Caller should handle the exit status

functions.name: r_main_radiff2
functions.signature: R_API int r_main_radiff2(int argc, const char **argv);
functions.description: Entry point wrapper for the radiff2 diffing tool. Standard main-like signature; returns exit status.
requirements: argc must be >= 0
