functions.name: r_th_channel_read
functions.description: Blocking read that dequeues the next message from the given thread channel for the consumer side. Intended for the channel's consumer thread created/managed via r_th_channel_new.
requirements: tc must be a non-NULL pointer to a channel created by r_th_channel_new.
May block until a message is available; callers should be prepared for indefinite wait depending on producer activity.
Only the designated consumer thread for tc should call this to avoid race conditions (inferred from channel design).

functions.name: r_th_channel_message_free
functions.description: Frees a channel message and any associated resources. Use after a message has been processed or when discarding a message.
requirements: cm must be either NULL or a valid message obtained from r_th_channel_message_new, r_th_channel_read, r_th_channel_message_read, or r_th_channel_write.
After freeing, cm must not be used again.

functions.name: r_th_channel_write
functions.description: Enqueues a message into the channel for consumption by the consumer thread. Returns a message object (typically the same cm) or NULL on failure (exact return semantics depend on implementation).
requirements: tc must be a non-NULL pointer to a channel created by r_th_channel_new.
cm must be a non-NULL, valid message (e.g., created by r_th_channel_message_new).
cm->msg must reference a buffer of length cm->len (len >= 0).
The function may block if internal flow-control applies (unknown).

functions.name: r_th_channel_message_read
functions.description: Waits for and reads the response corresponding to a previously posted message on the channel. Useful for request/response interactions.
requirements: tc must be a non-NULL pointer to a channel created by r_th_channel_new.
cm must be a non-NULL message that was previously posted to tc (e.g., via r_th_channel_write or r_th_channel_post).
May block until a corresponding response is available.

functions.name: r_th_channel_message_new
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new channel message carrying the given payload for use with r_th_channel_write/post/query.
requirements: tc must be a non-NULL pointer to a channel created by r_th_channel_new (used for internal bookkeeping, e.g., IDs).
msg may be NULL only if len == 0; otherwise must point to at least len bytes.
len must be >= 0.

functions.name: r_th_channel_new
functions.description: Creates a new message channel, setting up a consumer thread/function to process incoming messages. The consumer function is invoked with an RThread representing the consumer context and can read messages via the channel APIs.
requirements: consumer must be a non-NULL function of type RThreadFunction.
The consumer function must adhere to the RThreadFunction contract (returning RThreadFunctionRet values to control its loop, unknown specifics).
user is an opaque pointer passed to/associated with the consumer thread; if used, it must remain valid as required by the consumer logic.

functions.name: r_th_channel_free
functions.description: Destroys a thread channel, freeing internal resources and stopping its consumer as needed.
requirements: tc may be NULL (no-op) or must be a valid channel returned by r_th_channel_new.
Should not be called while other threads are concurrently using tc (writing/reading), to avoid races.
Any outstanding messages/promises should be resolved or canceled before freeing to prevent leaks (inferred).

functions.name: r_th_channel_query
functions.description: Posts a message to the channel and returns a promise that can be waited on to obtain the corresponding response.
requirements: tc must be a valid, non-NULL channel created by r_th_channel_new.
cm must be a non-NULL message destined for tc (e.g., from r_th_channel_message_new).
Caller must later wait on and/or free the returned promise to avoid leaks.

functions.name: r_th_channel_post
functions.description: Posts a message to the channel without creating or expecting a response/promise. Fire-and-forget send.
requirements: tc must be a valid, non-NULL channel created by r_th_channel_new.
cm must be a non-NULL message suitable for tc (e.g., created by r_th_channel_message_new).

functions.name: r_th_channel_promise_new
functions.description: Creates a new promise object associated with the given channel for coordinating a future response.
requirements: tc must be a valid, non-NULL channel created by r_th_channel_new.
Caller is responsible for freeing the promise via r_th_channel_promise_free.

functions.name: r_th_channel_promise_wait
functions.description: Blocks until the promise is fulfilled, returning the response message associated with the promise.
requirements: promise must be a non-NULL promise obtained from r_th_channel_query or r_th_channel_promise_new and properly posted/associated with a message.
May block indefinitely until the response is produced.

functions.name: r_th_channel_promise_free
functions.description: Frees a promise object and any internal resources once no longer needed.
requirements: cp may be NULL (no-op) or must be a valid promise created by r_th_channel_query or r_th_channel_promise_new.
Do not free a promise that is still being waited on or that has not yet been fulfilled, unless the API guarantees safe cancellation (unknown).

functions.name: r_th_new
functions.description: Allocates a new thread object configured to run the given function, with an optional startup delay. Does not start the thread until r_th_start is called.
requirements: fun must be a non-NULL function pointer of type RThreadFunction.
delay specifies a startup delay in seconds or time units as used by the implementation (header comment suggests seconds); must fit in ut32.
user is an opaque pointer stored in the thread object; if referenced by the thread function, it must remain valid for the thread’s lifetime.

functions.name: r_th_start
functions.description: Starts the given thread object, invoking its configured RThreadFunction in a new thread of execution.
requirements: th must be a non-NULL thread object created by r_th_new.
Must not be called more than once per thread object (inferred typical constraint).
Thread function should be prepared to honor r_th_break/r_th_kill requests (inferred).

functions.name: r_th_wait
functions.description: Blocks until the specified thread terminates (joins it). Returns an implementation-defined status code.
requirements: th must be a non-NULL thread that has been started with r_th_start.
Caller should not call r_th_wait from the same thread represented by th to avoid deadlock.
Should be called at most once per thread’s lifecycle (inferred).

functions.name: r_th_wait_async
functions.description: Non-blocking or asynchronously-coordinated wait for a thread’s termination (exact semantics depend on implementation). Intended to check/join without blocking indefinitely.
requirements: th must be a non-NULL thread object created by r_th_new (typically started).
Return value semantics are implementation-defined; callers should handle nonzero/zero or error codes appropriately (unknown specifics).

functions.name: r_th_break
functions.description: Requests cooperative interruption of the given thread by setting an internal break/interrupt flag that the thread function can check and honor.
requirements: th must be a non-NULL thread object.
Has no immediate effect unless the running thread function periodically checks for the break request and exits appropriately (inferred).

functions.name: r_th_free
functions.description: Frees the thread object and its resources. Returns an auxiliary pointer (likely the user pointer) or NULL depending on implementation.
requirements: th may be NULL (no-op) or must be a thread created by r_th_new.
Should not be called while the thread is still running; stop/join or kill first.
Return value semantics are implementation-defined; callers must not assume a specific pointer without checking documentation.

functions.name: r_th_set_running
functions.description: Sets the thread’s running state flag. Typically used internally by the threading framework to track lifecycle.
requirements: th must be non-NULL.
Intended for internal use; external callers should avoid manual state manipulation unless required (inferred).

functions.name: r_th_is_running
functions.description: Returns whether the given thread is currently marked as running.
requirements: th must be non-NULL.

functions.name: r_th_kill_free
functions.description: Attempts to terminate the thread and free its resources in one step. Returns an auxiliary pointer (likely the user pointer) or NULL depending on implementation.
requirements: th must be a non-NULL thread object.
May forcibly terminate the thread; ensure resources/state can tolerate abrupt termination (inferred).
Return value semantics are implementation-defined; do not dereference without validation.

functions.name: r_th_kill
functions.description: Requests termination of the specified thread. If force is true, may use a non-cooperative/forceful method depending on platform.
requirements: th must be non-NULL.
Forceful kill can leave shared state inconsistent; use with caution (inferred).
May fail depending on platform or thread state; caller should check the return value.

functions.name: r_th_self
functions.description: Returns the calling thread’s native/threading-abstraction identifier.

functions.name: r_th_setname
functions.description: Sets the OS-visible name of the given thread, if supported by the platform.
requirements: th must be non-NULL and should refer to an existing thread (started or at least created).
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string. Platform-specific length limits may apply (unknown).

functions.name: r_th_getname
functions.description: Retrieves the OS-visible name of the given thread into the provided buffer.
requirements: th must be non-NULL and refer to a valid thread.
name must be a non-NULL buffer with capacity len bytes.
len must be > 0; on success, output will be null-terminated if space allows (exact behavior platform-dependent, unknown).

functions.name: r_th_setaffinity
functions.description: Sets the CPU affinity of the given thread to the specified CPU/core index, if supported by the platform.
requirements: th must be non-NULL and refer to a valid thread.
cpuid must be a valid processor/core index for the running system; negative values are invalid.
May fail on platforms without affinity support or due to permission constraints; caller should check return value.

functions.name: r_th_sem_new
functions.description: Creates a new semaphore with the given initial count.
requirements: initial is the initial semaphore count; must be a valid non-negative count representable by the underlying semaphore implementation.

functions.name: r_th_sem_free
functions.description: Destroys a semaphore and frees associated resources.
requirements: sem may be NULL (no-op) or must be a semaphore created by r_th_sem_new.
Should not be freed while other threads may be blocked on it (to avoid undefined behavior).

functions.name: r_th_sem_post
functions.description: Increments (signals) the semaphore, potentially waking a waiting thread.
requirements: sem must be a non-NULL semaphore created by r_th_sem_new.

functions.name: r_th_sem_wait
functions.description: Decrements the semaphore, blocking if the count is zero until it becomes available.
requirements: sem must be a non-NULL semaphore created by r_th_sem_new.
May block indefinitely until a post occurs.

functions.name: r_th_lock_new
functions.description: Creates a new mutex/lock object. If recursive is true, the lock may be re-entered by the owning thread (subject to platform support).
requirements: recursive selects the lock type; behavior depends on platform support.
Caller must free the lock with r_th_lock_free.

functions.name: r_th_lock_wait
functions.description: Waits for the lock to become active/initialized before use. Intended to synchronize with lazy initialization of the lock (based on struct fields).
requirements: th must be a non-NULL lock object (typically from r_th_lock_new).

functions.name: r_th_lock_tryenter
functions.description: Attempts to acquire the lock without blocking; returns true on success.
requirements: thl must be a non-NULL lock created by r_th_lock_new.
If the lock is recursive, re-entry by the owning thread is allowed; otherwise, caller must not re-enter (depends on creation).

functions.name: r_th_lock_enter
functions.description: Blocks until the lock can be acquired, then acquires it. Returns true on success.
requirements: thl must be a non-NULL lock created by r_th_lock_new.
If the lock is non-recursive, the same thread must not call enter twice without leaving.

functions.name: r_th_lock_leave
functions.description: Releases the previously acquired lock.
requirements: thl must be a non-NULL lock created by r_th_lock_new.
Must only be called by the thread that currently holds the lock and after a successful enter/tryenter.

functions.name: r_th_lock_free
functions.description: Frees a lock object and associated resources. Returns an auxiliary pointer (implementation-defined) or NULL.
requirements: thl may be NULL (no-op) or must be a lock created by r_th_lock_new.
Lock should not be held by any thread when freeing to avoid undefined behavior.
Return value semantics are implementation-defined; caller should not rely on a specific pointer.

functions.name: r_th_cond_new
functions.description: Creates a new condition variable object for thread synchronization.
requirements: Caller must free the condition with r_th_cond_free.
To use with r_th_cond_wait, pair with a compatible RThreadLock.

functions.name: r_th_cond_signal
functions.description: Wakes one thread waiting on the condition variable, if any.
requirements: cond must be a non-NULL condition created by r_th_cond_new.
Typically used while holding the associated lock to avoid missed wakeups (recommended; exact requirement unknown).

functions.name: r_th_cond_signal_all
functions.description: Wakes all threads waiting on the condition variable.
requirements: cond must be a non-NULL condition created by r_th_cond_new.
Typically used while holding the associated lock to avoid races (recommended; exact requirement unknown).

functions.name: r_th_cond_wait
functions.description: Atomically releases the given lock and waits on the condition variable; upon wakeup, re-acquires the lock before returning.
requirements: cond must be a non-NULL condition created by r_th_cond_new.
lock must be a non-NULL lock created by r_th_lock_new and must be held by the calling thread before calling wait (standard condition variable use pattern).
May block indefinitely until signaled.

functions.name: r_th_cond_free
functions.description: Destroys a condition variable and frees its resources.
requirements: cond may be NULL (no-op) or must be a condition created by r_th_cond_new.
No threads should be waiting on cond when it is freed.

functions.name: r_atomic_store
functions.description: Atomically stores the boolean value v into the atomic boolean data.
requirements: data must be a non-NULL pointer to a variable of type R_ATOMIC_BOOL with appropriate alignment for atomic operations.
Memory ordering semantics are implementation-defined (unknown).

functions.name: r_atomic_exchange
functions.description: Atomically sets data to v and returns the previous boolean value.
requirements: data must be a non-NULL pointer to a variable of type R_ATOMIC_BOOL with appropriate alignment for atomic operations.
Memory ordering semantics are implementation-defined (unknown).

functions.name: r_lib_dl_open
functions.description: Open a dynamic library by filename and return an opaque handle suitable for symbol lookups and later closing. Typically used as the first step before r_lib_dl_sym and r_lib_dl_close. The safe_mode flag enables a safer/isolated loading path if supported.
requirements: libname must be a non-null, valid path or soname for a loadable dynamic library on the host platform.
The returned handle (if non-NULL) must be passed to r_lib_dl_sym and r_lib_dl_close; do not pass other pointers.
Call r_lib_dl_close with the returned handle once you are done to release resources.
safe_mode usage effects are implementation-defined; callers should not rely on specific behavior beyond potentially safer loading.

functions.name: r_lib_dl_sym
functions.description: Resolve the address of a symbol exported by a previously opened dynamic library. Use the handle returned by r_lib_dl_open and the symbol name to retrieve a function or data pointer.
requirements: handler must be a non-NULL handle previously returned by r_lib_dl_open for the same process.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated symbol name present in the loaded library.
The returned pointer may be NULL if the symbol is not found; callers must check for NULL before use.
The returned pointer must be cast to the appropriate function or data type by the caller before invocation or access.

functions.name: r_lib_dl_close
functions.description: Close/unload a dynamically loaded library previously opened with r_lib_dl_open. Frees resources associated with the handle.
requirements: handler must be a valid non-NULL handle previously obtained from r_lib_dl_open and not already closed.
After a successful call, the handler becomes invalid and must not be used again.
Returns true on success and false on failure; callers should check the return value.

functions.name: r_lib_new
functions.description: Create and initialize a new RLib instance, configuring the symbol names used to locate plugin descriptors/functions (e.g., radare_plugin and radare_plugin_function). Use this as the entry point for high-level plugin management APIs.
requirements: symname may be NULL or a string specifying the plugin struct symbol name; same for symnamefunc. If non-NULL, they must be valid, null-terminated strings.
The returned RLib pointer must be freed with r_lib_free when no longer needed.
Callers must check the return value for NULL to detect allocation/initialization failure before further use.

functions.name: r_lib_free
functions.description: Destroy an RLib instance and release all associated resources, including any loaded plugins tracked by the instance as per implementation. After this call, the RLib pointer must not be used.
requirements: lib must be a pointer previously returned by r_lib_new or NULL. If non-NULL, it must not be used after this call.

All handles and resources associated with the RLib that require explicit closing by the caller (if any) should be released before calling r_lib_free if required by implementation; exact ownership semantics for plugins and lists are unknown.

functions.name: r_lib_run_handler
functions.description: Invoke the registered constructor or destructor handler for a plugin within the given RLib context, using the provided plugin and its exported symbol structure. Typically used internally during plugin load/unload flows.
requirements: lib must be a valid, initialized RLib pointer from r_lib_new.
plugin must be a valid, initialized RLibPlugin tracked by lib.
symbol must point to a valid RLibStruct as exported by the plugin (e.g., via the radare_plugin symbol).
Returns true on success, false on failure; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: r_lib_get_handler
functions.description: Retrieve the registered handler for a given plugin type from the RLib instance. Handlers encapsulate constructor/destructor callbacks used to manage plugins of that type.
requirements: lib must be a valid RLib pointer.
type must be a valid plugin type value within [0, R_LIB_TYPE_LAST).
Returns NULL if no handler is registered for the specified type; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: r_lib_open
functions.description: Load and register a plugin from the given file path into the RLib instance using its configured symbol names and handlers. Performs dynamic loading and validation according to the library’s rules.
requirements: lib must be a valid RLib pointer created by r_lib_new.
file must be a non-NULL path to a loadable plugin library file compatible with the current platform and ABI.
Returns true on success and false on failure; callers must check the return value.
The plugin must export the expected symbols as configured in lib (e.g., symname/symnamefunc); otherwise loading will fail.

functions.name: r_lib_opendir
functions.description: Scan a directory and attempt to load/register all compatible plugin libraries found within, using the RLib instance’s configuration and handlers.
requirements: lib must be a valid RLib pointer.
path must be a non-NULL directory path accessible to the process.
Returns true if the operation succeeds according to implementation criteria (e.g., directory processed), false otherwise; callers must check the return value.
Only files matching platform-specific plugin extensions (e.g., .so, .dylib, .dll) and ABI constraints will be considered; exact filtering is implementation-defined.

functions.name: r_lib_open_ptr
functions.signature: R_API bool r_lib_open_ptr(RLib *lib, const char *file, void *handler, RLibStruct *stru);
functions.description: Register a plugin into the RLib instance using an already opened dynamic library handle and the plugin’s exported RLibStruct, optionally associating a file path. This bypasses opening by filename.
requirements: lib must be a valid RLib pointer.
handler must be a valid dynamic library handle obtained from r_lib_dl_open (or equivalent platform handle).
stru must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid RLibStruct exported by the plugin.
file may be NULL or a path string used for bookkeeping; if non-NULL it must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Returns true on success, false on failure; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: r_lib_validate_plugin
functions.signature: R_API bool r_lib_validate_plugin(RLib *lib, const char *file, RLibStruct *stru);
functions.description: Validate that the given plugin structure is compatible with the current RLib instance and runtime (e.g., ABI/version checks, type correctness) before or during loading.
requirements: lib must be a valid RLib pointer.
stru must be a non-NULL pointer to a filled RLibStruct originating from the plugin.
file may be NULL or a path string for diagnostics; if non-NULL it must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Returns true if the plugin passes validation (including ABI compatibility), false otherwise; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: r_lib_get_loaded_plugins
functions.description: Return the list of plugins currently loaded/registered in the RLib instance. The list elements are RLibPlugin pointers.
requirements: lib must be a valid RLib pointer.
Returns a pointer to an RList (possibly NULL if none or on failure); callers must check for NULL.
Ownership and lifetime of the returned list and its elements are implementation-defined/unknown; callers should not free or modify unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: r_lib_path
functions.description: Construct or resolve a filesystem path for a library/plugin name, likely applying platform-specific search rules or extensions (e.g., adding .so/.dylib/.dll).
requirements: libname must be a non-NULL, null-terminated library name.
Returns a char* which may be dynamically allocated; ownership and required deallocation are unknown from this header—callers must consult implementation to avoid leaks.

functions.name: r_lib_list
functions.description: List or enumerate plugins/handlers associated with the RLib instance, typically by printing to the configured output/log. Primarily a diagnostic/helper function.
requirements: lib must be a valid RLib pointer or NULL if the implementation tolerates it; behavior for NULL is unspecified.
No return value; callers should not assume any particular output format.

functions.name: r_lib_add_handler
functions.signature: R_API bool r_lib_add_handler(RLib *lib, int type, const char *desc, RLibCallback ct, RLibCallback dt, void *user);
functions.description: Register a handler for a given plugin type in the RLib instance, specifying constructor and destructor callbacks and an optional user pointer. Handlers govern how plugins of that type are initialized and torn down.
requirements: lib must be a valid RLib pointer.
type must be a valid plugin type within [0, R_LIB_TYPE_LAST).
desc may be NULL or a descriptive, null-terminated string; if non-NULL it should remain valid for the duration required by the implementation (storage semantics unknown).
ct (constructor) and dt (destructor) may be NULL depending on use; if provided, they must conform to RLibCallback and be safe to call with provided arguments.
user is an opaque pointer passed to callbacks; may be NULL.
Returns true on success, false on failure; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: r_lib_del_handler
functions.description: Unregister and remove the handler for the specified plugin type from the RLib instance.
requirements: lib must be a valid RLib pointer.
type must be a valid plugin type within [0, R_LIB_TYPE_LAST).
Returns true on success, false on failure (e.g., if no handler exists for type); callers must check the return value.

functions.name: r_lib_close
functions.description: Unload or deregister a previously loaded plugin identified by its file path from the RLib instance, running any necessary teardown via handlers.
requirements: lib must be a valid RLib pointer.
file must be a non-NULL, null-terminated path string that identifies a plugin previously opened in this RLib.
Returns true on success, false on failure; callers must check the return value.
After successful close, any pointers to the plugin’s data become invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: r_lib_meta_pj
functions.description: Serialize or emit plugin metadata into a PJ (print/json) context. Useful for producing JSON or structured output describing a plugin (name, desc, author, version, license, contact, copyright, status).
requirements: pj must be a valid, initialized PJ context pointer.
meta must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid RPluginMeta structure with fields either filled or NULL as appropriate.
No return value; callers must ensure pj remains valid for the duration of the operation.

functions.name: r_esil_new
functions.signature: R_API REsil *r_esil_new(int stacksize, int iotrap, unsigned int addrsize);
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new ESIL interpreter instance with the requested evaluation stack size, IO-trap setting, and address size mask. Intended as the basic constructor before further setup.
requirements: stacksize must be >= 0 and large enough for expected ESIL stack usage
addrsize specifies address width (in bits) and should match the target architecture
Returns NULL on allocation/initialization failure; caller must check for NULL
Returned REsil* must be released with r_esil_free()

functions.name: r_esil_init
functions.signature: R_API bool r_esil_init(REsil *esil, int stacksize, bool iotrap, ut32 addrsize, REsilRegInterface *reg_if, REsilMemInterface *mem_if);
functions.description: Initializes an existing ESIL instance with stack size, IO trap mode, address size, and external register/memory interfaces. Use when constructing ESIL in-place.
requirements: esil must be a valid, zeroed or newly allocated REsil object
reg_if and mem_if should point to valid interfaces with required function pointers set (read/write/size/switch as applicable)
stacksize must be >= 0
Returns false on failure; on failure the esil object may be partially initialized and should be cleaned with r_esil_fini() or freed accordingly

functions.name: r_esil_new_ex
functions.signature: R_API REsil *r_esil_new_ex(int stacksize, bool iotrap, ut32 addrsize, REsilRegInterface *reg_if, REsilMemInterface *mem_if);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new ESIL with given stack size, IO-trap mode, address size, and provided register/memory interfaces in one call.
requirements: reg_if and mem_if must describe valid backends (non-NULL functions required for operations you will perform)
stacksize must be >= 0
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check and call r_esil_free() on success to release

functions.name: r_esil_new_simple
functions.description: Convenience constructor that creates an ESIL instance for the given address size and binds simple register and IO backends. The exact expected backend types are those used by radare2 (e.g., RReg and RIO bindings), but types are opaque here.
requirements: addrsize must match the target architecture address width
reg and iob must be valid pointers to compatible radare2 register and IO contexts
Returns NULL on failure; free with r_esil_free() on success

functions.name: r_esil_add_voyeur
functions.signature: R_API ut32 r_esil_add_voyeur(REsil *esil, void *user, void *vfn, REsilVoyeurType vt);
functions.description: Registers a voyeur (observer) callback for ESIL events (reg/mem reads/writes or op). Returns a unique voyeur id to later remove it.
requirements: esil must be a valid initialized instance
vfn must be a function pointer of the correct signature for the specified vt (REsilVoyeurType)
user is passed back to the callback and may be NULL
Returns a 32-bit id; value may encode type in high bits as per VOYEUR_* macros

functions.name: r_esil_del_voyeur
functions.description: Unregisters a previously added voyeur callback by id.
requirements: esil must be valid
vid must be an id previously returned by r_esil_add_voyeur() for this esil
No return value; if vid is invalid, the call has no effect

functions.name: r_esil_reset
functions.description: Resets ESIL state (stack, flags, and internals) to a clean state while keeping the instance and bindings.
requirements: esil must be valid and previously initialized

functions.name: r_esil_set_pc
functions.description: Sets the ESIL program counter to the specified address.
requirements: esil must be valid
addr must be representable under the configured address size

functions.name: r_esil_setup
functions.signature: R_API bool r_esil_setup(REsil *esil, struct r_anal_t *anal, bool romem, bool stats, bool nonull);
functions.description: Configures ESIL using an r_anal handle and options such as read-only memory, statistics collection, and handling of null values. Typically called after construction to bind analysis context and prepare IO/regs.
requirements: esil must be valid and not yet fully configured
anal must be a valid r_anal_t pointer compatible with the target
Returns false on failure; on failure state may be partially set up

functions.name: r_esil_setup_ops
functions.description: Initializes ESIL operation table(s) for the current architecture/plugin set so expressions can be parsed and executed.
requirements: esil must be valid and associated with an architecture (via setup/anal)
Returns false on failure

functions.name: r_esil_fini
functions.description: Finalizes and deinitializes an ESIL instance, releasing internal resources but not freeing the REsil struct itself.
requirements: esil must be valid; safe to call once per r_esil_init/new_ex/new_simple
After calling, the object should not be used until re-initialized

functions.name: r_esil_free
functions.description: Frees an ESIL instance allocated by r_esil_new/new_ex/new_simple and releases associated resources.
requirements: esil may be NULL (no-op) or a valid pointer returned by r_esil_new/new_ex/new_simple
Must not be used after free

functions.name: r_esil_runword
functions.description: Executes a single ESIL word/operator against the current ESIL state and stack.
requirements: esil must be initialized and have op table set
word must be a valid, null-terminated ESIL token
Returns false on execution/parsing failure

functions.name: r_esil_parse
functions.description: Parses and evaluates an ESIL expression string, affecting registers/memory via the configured interfaces.
requirements: esil must be initialized and configured with reg/mem interfaces
str must be a valid null-terminated ESIL expression

functions.name: ptrace_wrap_instance_start
functions.description: Initialize and start a ptrace-wrap instance’s internal worker thread and synchronization primitives (semaphores). Call this before using the instance with other ptrace_wrap_* APIs. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure (exact error semantics unknown).
requirements: inst must be a valid, writable pointer to a ptrace_wrap_instance storage that remains alive until ptrace_wrap_instance_stop returns.
Must be called before any other function that uses this instance (e.g., ptrace_wrap, ptrace_wrap_fork, ptrace_wrap_func).
Should not be called more than once per instance without an intervening ptrace_wrap_instance_stop (restarting semantics are unknown).
Not thread-safe to call concurrently on the same instance (call exactly once during setup).
On non-zero return, the instance should be considered not started; do not use it with other APIs.

functions.name: ptrace_wrap_instance_stop
functions.description: Stop and clean up a previously started ptrace-wrap instance, terminating its worker thread and releasing resources. After this call, the instance must not be used unless restarted.
requirements: inst must be a valid pointer to an instance that was successfully started with ptrace_wrap_instance_start.
Do not call concurrently with ptrace_wrap_instance_start or any in-flight request functions that use the same instance (ordering must ensure no further requests are submitted after stop begins).
After this call returns, the instance must not be used again unless reinitialized via ptrace_wrap_instance_start.

functions.name: ptrace_wrap
functions.signature: long ptrace_wrap(ptrace_wrap_instance *inst, ptrace_wrap_ptrace_request request, pid_t pid, void *addr, void *data);
functions.description: Perform a ptrace operation via the ptrace-wrap instance’s worker thread. This is a wrapper around the ptrace() system call that marshals the request to the worker thread and returns the ptrace result value.
requirements: inst must be a non-NULL pointer to an instance that has been successfully started with ptrace_wrap_instance_start.
request must be a valid ptrace request code (enum __ptrace_request on glibc, otherwise an integral value) corresponding to the intended ptrace operation.
pid must refer to the target process/thread as required by the specific ptrace request; values and meaning depend on the request (e.g., a non-negative PID).

addr and data must meet the semantic and alignment/validity requirements for the specific ptrace request (e.g., some requests require NULL, others require a valid user-space address or integer cast through a pointer).

The caller must handle errors according to ptrace semantics: typically returns -1 on failure and sets errno (exact propagation is inferred from being a wrapper around ptrace; specifics beyond that are unknown).
Do not call concurrently from multiple threads on the same instance unless the implementation documents such usage as safe (thread-safety beyond request serialization is unknown).

functions.name: ptrace_wrap_fork
functions.description: Fork a new process via the ptrace-wrap worker thread. Optionally invokes child_callback(child_callback_user) in the child process context before returning. Returns standard fork semantics: >0 in the parent (child PID), 0 in the child, and -1 on error (errno set).
requirements: inst must be a non-NULL pointer to an instance that has been successfully started with ptrace_wrap_instance_start.
If provided, child_callback must be a valid function pointer; child_callback_user is passed through as its argument.

In the child process created from a multithreaded program, only async-signal-safe operations are permitted before an exec or _exit according to POSIX. Therefore, child_callback must restrict itself to async-signal-safe functions, or immediately call an exec-family function or _exit; performing non-async-signal-safe operations in the child is unsafe.
The caller must handle errors per fork semantics: return value -1 indicates failure and errno is set (further error detail beyond this standard behavior is unknown).
Do not call concurrently from multiple threads on the same instance unless documented as safe (unknown).

functions.name: ptrace_wrap_func
functions.description: Execute an arbitrary user-supplied function in the ptrace-wrap worker thread context. Calls func(user) and returns its result pointer to the caller.
requirements: inst must be a non-NULL pointer to an instance that has been successfully started with ptrace_wrap_instance_start.

data_types.description: A generic buffer of arbitrary bytes with no encoding or format constraints. Can contain any values including NULs. Suitable for functions that treat input as opaque data or construct C strings by truncating/adding a NUL terminator.
A NUL-terminated ASCII string consisting of hexadecimal digits optionally with separators as supported by the library (e.g., "90CC00", "90 cc 00"). Intended to represent raw bytes in hex form.
A NUL-terminated string containing a regular expression in the syntax supported by the target library/engine. May include metacharacters, quantifiers, character classes, anchors, and grouping.
A NUL-terminated textual command intended to be interpreted by the analysis subsystem’s command interface. May include subcommands, options, and arguments; format depends on the active plugin.
A NUL-terminated string containing assembly mnemonic and operands for the currently selected architecture (e.g., "mov eax, ebx", "nop"). Parsed/assembled by the active backend.

A NUL-terminated text buffer containing valid or invalid C language source code snippets (declarations, typedefs, function definitions, etc.). May include types, structs, function prototypes, and statements. Used by parsers to integrate types/signatures.
A filename whose referenced file contains C language source text. The file data is read and parsed as C code (can be valid or malformed C).

A NUL-terminated string containing an ESIL (Evaluable Strings Intermediate Language) expression used by radare2 to model instruction semantics (e.g., "1,rax,="). May reference registers/memory, constants, and ESIL operators.

A NUL-terminated string encoded in UTF-8 with no embedded NUL bytes inside the data. May contain any valid UTF-8 byte sequences; used where APIs require textual input without interior NULs (e.g., QR code text encoder).

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate an arbitrary byte string designed to be broadly useful for many stubs:
# - Mix printable ASCII and binary bytes
# - Include NULs and repeated patterns
# - Include sequences that look like hex, base64, assembly-like tokens, regex, and paths
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes
# - Results are deterministic for a given seed

PRINTABLE = bytes(string.printable, 'ascii')
HEXCHARS = b"0123456789abcdef"
B64CHARS = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/="

def _rand_choice(r: random.Random, data: bytes, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(data[r.randrange(0, len(data))] for _ in range(n))

def _make_path(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create a plausible UNIX-like path or URL-ish path
    parts = []
    depth = r.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        seglen = r.randint(1, 8)
        seg = _rand_choice(r, PRINTABLE.replace(b"/", b""), seglen)
        # sanitize to filename-safe subset
        seg = bytes(ch if (32 <= ch < 127 and ch not in b"\\/:*?\"<>|") else ord('_') for ch in seg)
        parts.append(seg)
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        # sometimes make it look like a URL prefix
        scheme = r.choice([b"http", b"https", b"file"]) + b"://"
        return scheme + b"/".join(parts)
    return b"/" + b"/".join(parts)

def _make_hex(r: random.Random, minlen=8, maxlen=64) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(minlen, maxlen)
    s = _rand_choice(r, HEXCHARS, n)
    return s

def _make_b64(r: random.Random, minlen=12, maxlen=80) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(minlen, maxlen)
    s = _rand_choice(r, B64CHARS, n)
    return s

def _make_regex(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # simple regex fragments
    parts = [
        b"^", b"[A-Za-z0-9_]+", b"\\s*", b"(foo|bar)?", b"[0-9]{1,3}", b"$",
        b"(.*)", b"\\w+", b"(?:abc)?", b"[\\x00-\\xff]"
    ]
    r.shuffle(parts)
    return b"".join(parts[:r.randint(2, 5)])

def _make_asm_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # small assembly-like snippet
    ops = [b"nop", b"mov eax, ebx", b"push rbp", b"pop rbp", b"ret", b"add r0, r1, #1", b"ldr r0, [r1]", b"jmp 0x90"]
    n = r.randint(1, 4)
    return b"; ".join(r.sample(ops, n))

def _make_c_string(r: random.Random, minlen=1, maxlen=64) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(minlen, maxlen)
    s = _rand_choice(r, PRINTABLE, n)
    # ensure no embedded NUL for C-string contexts sometimes
    s = s.replace(b"\x00", b"_")
    return s

def _make_binary_chunk(r: random.Random, minlen=8, maxlen=128) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(minlen, maxlen)
    chunk = bytearray(n)
    for i in range(n):
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            chunk[i] = 0  # include NULs
        elif r.random() < 0.2:
            chunk[i] = 0xFF
        else:
            chunk[i] = r.randrange(0, 256)
    return bytes(chunk)

def _repeat_pattern(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    base = r.choice([b"\x90", b"\xCC", b"\x00", b"AB", b"\r\n"])
    reps = r.randint(4, 40)
    return base * reps

def _make_equ_lines(r: random.Random, nlines=3) -> bytes:
    out = []
    for _ in range(nlines):
        key = _make_c_string(r, 1, 12)
        val = _make_c_string(r, 0, 24)
        out.append(key + b"=" + val)
    return b"\n".join(out)

def _make_optstring(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # getopt-like string with letters and colons
    letters = bytes(string.ascii_letters, 'ascii')
    s = bytearray()
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 12)):
        ch = r.choice(letters)
        s.append(ch)
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            s.append(ord(':'))
            if r.random() < 0.2:
                s.append(ord(':'))
    return bytes(s)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Header marker to help some scanners
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(b";FUZZ\n")

    # Include a mix of useful segments
    parts.append(_make_c_string(r, 3, 32))
    parts.append(b"\n")
    parts.append(_make_path(r) + b"\n")
    parts.append(_make_hex(r) + b"\n")
    parts.append(_make_b64(r) + b"\n")
    parts.append(_make_regex(r) + b"\n")
    parts.append(_make_asm_like(r) + b"\n")
    parts.append(_make_optstring(r) + b"\n")

    # EQU-like lines
    parts.append(_make_equ_lines(r, nlines=r.randint(2, 5)) + b"\n")

    # Binary chunks interleaved with textual sections
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        parts.append(_make_binary_chunk(r))
        parts.append(b"\n")
        parts.append(_repeat_pattern(r))
        parts.append(b"\n")

    # Potential JSON-ish and XML-ish snippets for grep/console
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(b"{\"key\": \"" + _make_c_string(r, 3, 12) + b"\", \"num\": " + str(r.randint(0, 999)).encode() + b"}\n")
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(b"<tag attr=\"" + _make_c_string(r, 1, 8) + b"\">" + _make_c_string(r, 1, 12) + b"</tag>\n")

    # Some lines with potential demangling tokens
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(b"_Z3foov\n")
        parts.append(b"?func@@YAHXZ\n")
        parts.append(b"$s4Test3fooyyF\n")

    # Ensure total size <= 4096
    buf = b"".join(parts)
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]

    # Randomly decide to add trailing NUL (useful for C-string consumers)
    if r.random() < 0.5 and len(buf) < 4096:
        buf += b"\x00"

    return buf

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# We want to generate bytes that will be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR and numeric FUZZ_PARAM types.
# Target stubs use:
# - A regex string (r_search_keyword_new_regexp): NUL-terminated C string with regex syntax
# - r_core_asm_strsearch: needs several integers (ut64, unsigned int x5) and a search pattern string
#
# The fuzzer framework will slice the buffer to fulfill FUZZ_PARAM requests in order.
# We'll pack data in this order to match both stubs:
# 1) Regex string (NUL-terminated)
# 2) ut64 from
# 3) unsigned int span seed
# 4) unsigned int maxhits seed
# 5) unsigned int regexp flag seed
# 6) unsigned int everyByte flag seed
# 7) unsigned int mode seed
# 8) Search pattern string (NUL-terminated)
#
# We provide multiple alternative regex strings and search patterns, picked via seed, to cover features:
# - simple literals
# - character classes, ranges
# - anchors ^ $
# - quantifiers *, +, ?, {m,n}
# - groups (), alternation |
# - escaped specials, word boundaries, digits
# - unicode classes if supported via escapes
#
# We keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

def _pick_regex(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    regex_pool: List[str] = [
        r"a+b+",
        r"^hello$",
        r"(foo|bar|baz)",
        r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*",
        r"\b\d{1,3}(?:\.\d{1,3}){3}\b",  # IPv4-ish (non-capturing if supported)
        r"^\s*#.*$",
        r"colou?r",
        r"[\x00-\x1F\x7F]",
        r"(ab){2,4}",
        r"^.*$",
        r"(?i)caseinsensitive",  # inline flag if supported
        r"\w+@\w+\.(com|net|org)",
        r"^([0-9a-fA-F]{2}:){5}[0-9a-fA-F]{2}$",  # MAC-like
        r"^\d+$",
        r"[\s\S]*?end",  # non-greedy all if supported
    ]
    s = r.choice(regex_pool)
    # Occasionally generate a longer composite regex
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        parts = [r.choice(regex_pool) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5))]
        joiner = r.choice([".*", ".+", ".*?", "|"])
        s = joiner.join(parts)
    # Ensure bounded length (library clamps to 128)
    s = s[:120]
    return s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"

def _pick_pattern(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # r_core_asm_strsearch accepts either literal or regex depending on flag; we provide a mix.
    literal_pool = [
        b"NOP",
        b"\x90\x90",        # x86 NOPs as bytes
        b"push",
        b"mov rax,",
        b"call",
        b"ELF",
        b"MZ",
        b"/bin/sh",
        b"radare2",
        b"TODO",
        b"%PDF-",
        b"PK\x03\x04",
    ]
    regex_pool = [
        r"NOP|INT3".encode(),
        r"^MZ".encode(),
        r"\x7fELF".encode(),
        r"call\s+[\w_]+".encode(),
        r"mov\s+e?ax,\s*0x[0-9a-fA-F]+".encode(),
        r"[ -~]{4,}".encode(),  # printable run
    ]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        s = r.choice(literal_pool)
    else:
        s = r.choice(regex_pool)
    # Limit to 64 as stub will clamp
    s = s[:60]
    return s + b"\x00"

def _rand_ut64(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Choose useful offsets: small, page-aligned, large
    choices = [
        0,
        r.randrange(0, 0x10000),
        (r.randrange(0, 0x1000) << 12),  # page aligned-ish
        r.randrange(0, 1 << 32),
    ]
    return r.choice(choices)

def _pack_u64(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<Q', v & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)

def _pack_u32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    buf = bytearray()

    # 1) Regex string for r_search_keyword_new_regexp
    buf += _pick_regex(r)

    # 2) ut64 from
    from_off = _rand_ut64(r)
    buf += _pack_u64(from_off)

    # 3) unsigned int seeds (span, maxhits, regexp, everyByte, mode)
    # Span seed: we keep it modest; stub will mod 1024
    span_seed = r.randrange(0, 4096)
    buf += _pack_u32(span_seed)

    # maxhits up to small number; stub mods 16
    maxhits_seed = r.randrange(0, 64)
    buf += _pack_u32(maxhits_seed)

    # regexp flag seed (0 or 1 via %2); randomize
    regexp_seed = r.randrange(0, 8)
    buf += _pack_u32(regexp_seed)

    # everyByte flag seed
    every_seed = r.randrange(0, 8)
    buf += _pack_u32(every_seed)

    # mode seed (0..3 via %4)
    mode_seed = r.randrange(0, 16)
    buf += _pack_u32(mode_seed)

    # 4) Search pattern string (NUL-terminated)
    buf += _pick_pattern(r)

    # Ensure cap
    return bytes(buf[:4096])

    "af @ {addr}",              # analyze function at addr
    "afn f_{hex} @ {addr}",     # rename function
    "afr {hex} @ {addr}",       # set function range
    "af+ {addr} {size}",        # add function with size
    "afb+ {addr} {size}",       # add basic block
    "axt @ {addr}",             # find xrefs to
    "axf @ {addr}",             # xrefs from
    "aai @ {addr}",             # analyze imports around addr
    "aat @ {addr}",             # analyze all things at addr
    "ahi {bits}",               # set hint bits
    "ahb {bits} @ {addr}",      # hint bits at addr
    "ah+ str,{len} @ {addr}",   # add hint string
    "agf @ {addr}",             # graph of function at addr
    "afsr {addr} {addr2}",      # set function range start/end
    "axg {addr} {addr2}",       # build xref graph between
]

BITS_CHOICES = [8, 16, 32, 64]
SIZES = [0x10, 0x20, 0x40, 0x80, 0x100]
STR_LENS = [4, 8, 12, 16]

def _hex(n: int) -> str:
    return f"0x{n:x}"

def _rand_hex_token(rng: random.Random, min_bits: int = 16, max_bits: int = 32) -> str:
    # produce a short hex token for names
    val = rng.randrange(1 << (min_bits - 1), 1 << max_bits)
    return f"{val:x}"

def _choose_addr(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(ARG_ADDR)
    # random aligned address
    base = rng.choice([0x100, 0x400, 0x1000, 0x401000, 0x7fff0000])
    offs = rng.choice([0, 0x10, 0x20, 0x30, 0x100])
    return _hex(base + offs)

def _choose_addr2(rng: random.Random, a1: int | None = None) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        a, b = rng.choice(RANGES)
        return b
    return _choose_addr(rng)

def _make_composite(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    tpl = rng.choice(COMPOSITES)
    addr = _choose_addr(rng)
    addr2 = _choose_addr2(rng)
    bits = rng.choice(BITS_CHOICES)
    size = rng.choice(SIZES)
    slen = rng.choice(STR_LENS)
    hexname = _rand_hex_token(rng)
    cmd = tpl.format(addr=addr, addr2=addr2, bits=bits, size=size, len=slen, hex=hexname)
    return cmd

def _maybe_join(cmds: List[str], rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Chain multiple commands with ';' so a single string executes several
    if not cmds:
        return ""
    # limit total length to keep under 4096
    out: List[str] = []
    total = 0
    for c in cmds:
        if total + len(c) + 1 > 3800:
            break
        out.append(c)
        total += len(c) + 1
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            break
    return ";".join(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Strategy: build a command sequence mixing base and composite commands.
    n = rng.randint(1, 6)
    parts: List[str] = []

    # Occasionally start with a global analysis sweep to enable richer state
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(rng.choice(["aa", "aaa", "aae", "aap", "aav"]))

    for _ in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.55:
            parts.append(_make_composite(rng))
        else:
            base = rng.choice(ANAL_CMDS_BASE)
            # Some base cmds can take an address with @
            if rng.random() < 0.5 and ("af" in base or base in {"ab", "ax", "agf", "ag"}):
                parts.append(f"{base} @ {_choose_addr(rng)}")
            else:
                parts.append(base)

    cmdline = _maybe_join(parts, rng)
    if not cmdline:
        cmdline = "aa"

    # Ensure it's ASCII without NUL; r_anal_cmd expects a C string.
    cmdline = ''.join(ch for ch in cmdline if ch != '\\x00')
    # Trim to <= 4096
    cmdline = cmdline[:4000]
    return cmdline.encode("utf-8")

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate assembly-like strings suitable for various common architectures.
# Fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR for:
# - r_anal_opasm: expects assembly text to assemble
# - r_anal_hint_set_opcode: opcode hint text
# - r_core_asm_search / r_core_asm_strsearch: pattern text (may be asm or plain)
# Provide a mix of valid mnemonics/operands across x86/x86_64/ARM/MIPS/RISCV/AVR/SPARC.
# Keep output under 4096 bytes.

X86_REGS32 = ["eax","ebx","ecx","edx","esi","edi","ebp","esp"]
X86_REGS64 = ["rax","rbx","rcx","rdx","rsi","rdi","rbp","rsp",
              "r8","r9","r10","r11","r12","r13","r14","r15"]
X86_REGS16 = ["ax","bx","cx","dx","si","di","bp","sp"]
X86_REGS8  = ["al","ah","bl","bh","cl","ch","dl","dh"]

ARM_REGS = ["r0","r1","r2","r3","r4","r5","r6","r7","r8","r9","r10","r11","r12","sp","lr","pc"]
RISCV_REGS = ["x0","x1","x2","x3","x4","x5","x6","x7","x8","x9","x10","x11","x12","x13","x14","x15"]
MIPS_REGS = ["$zero","$at","$v0","$v1","$a0","$a1","$a2","$a3","$t0","$t1","$t2","$t3","$t4","$t5","$t6","$t7",
             "$s0","$s1","$s2","$s3","$s4","$s5","$s6","$s7","$t8","$t9","$k0","$k1","$gp","$sp","$fp","$ra"]

# Pools of known-good mnemonics per arch
X86_MN = [
    "nop",
    "mov {dst}, {src}",
    "add {dst}, {src}",
    "sub {dst}, {src}",
    "xor {dst}, {src}",
    "or {dst}, {src}",
    "and {dst}, {src}",
    "lea {dst}, [{base}+{imm}]",
    "push {reg}",
    "pop {reg}",
    "inc {reg}",
    "dec {reg}",
    "call {imm}",
    "jmp {imm}",
    "test {dst}, {src}",
    "cmp {dst}, {src}",
    "mov [{base}+{imm}], {reg}",
    "mov {reg}, [{base}+{imm}]",
]

ARM_MN = [
    "nop",
    "mov {rd}, {rs}",
    "add {rd}, {rn}, #{imm}",
    "sub {rd}, {rn}, #{imm}",
    "ldr {rd}, [{rn}, #{imm}]",
    "str {rd}, [{rn}, #{imm}]",
    "bx {rs}",
    "bl #{imm}",
    "b #{imm}",
]

RISCV_MN = [
    "nop",
    "addi {rd}, {rs}, {imm}",
    "add {rd}, {rs}, {rt}",
    "xor {rd}, {rs}, {rt}",
    "lw {rd}, {imm}({rs})",
    "sw {rd}, {imm}({rs})",
    "jal {rd}, {imm}",
    "jalr {rd}, {rs}, {imm}",
]

MIPS_MN = [
    "nop",
    "add {rd}, {rs}, {rt}",
    "addu {rd}, {rs}, {rt}",
    "sub {rd}, {rs}, {rt}",
    "xor {rd}, {rs}, {rt}",
    "lw {rt}, {imm}({rs})",
    "sw {rt}, {imm}({rs})",
    "jal {imm}",
    "jr {rs}",
]

AVR_MN = [
    "nop",
    "ldi r{rd}, {imm}",
    "add r{rd}, r{rs}",
    "sub r{rd}, r{rs}",
    "sts {imm}, r{rs}",
    "lds r{rd}, {imm}",
]

SPARC_MN = [
    "nop",
    "set {imm}, %o0",
    "add %o0, %o1, %o2",
    "sub %o2, %o1, %o0",
    "ba {imm}",
]

GENERIC_PATTERNS = [
    # Strings that are useful for search stubs even if not valid mnemonics
    "; comment line",
    "// inline comment",
    "mov eax, 0x{hex}",
    "push 0x{hex} ; push imm",
    "call 0x{hex}",
    "ldr r0, [r1, #{imm}] ; ARM",
    "addi x1, x2, {imm} ; RISC-V",
    "add $t0, $t1, $t2 ; MIPS",
]

HEX_CHARS = string.hexdigits.lower()


def _rand_hex(rng: random.Random, nbytes: int = 4) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(HEX_CHARS[:16]) for _ in range(nbytes * 2))


def _rand_imm(rng: random.Random, bits: int = 12) -> int:
    # produce small immediates frequently, with occasional larger ones
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.randrange(0, 1 << min(bits, 12))
    return rng.randrange(0, 1 << min(bits, 32))


def _pick(rng: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:
    return arr[rng.randrange(len(arr))]


def gen_x86(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    reg_sizes = rng.choice([8, 16, 32, 64])
    if reg_sizes == 8:
        rA = _pick(rng, X86_REGS8)
        rB = _pick(rng, X86_REGS8)
    elif reg_sizes == 16:
        rA = _pick(rng, X86_REGS16)
        rB = _pick(rng, X86_REGS16)
    elif reg_sizes == 32:
        rA = _pick(rng, X86_REGS32)
        rB = _pick(rng, X86_REGS32)
    else:
        rA = _pick(rng, X86_REGS64)
        rB = _pick(rng, X86_REGS64)
    base = _pick(rng, (X86_REGS64 if reg_sizes == 64 else X86_REGS32))
    imm = _rand_imm(rng, 16)
    tmpl = _pick(rng, X86_MN)
    s = tmpl.format(dst=rA, src=rB, reg=rA, base=base, imm=imm)
    # sometimes add size overrides or suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = "db 0x" + _rand_hex(rng, 1)  # raw data directive valid in many assemblers
    return s


def gen_arm(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    rd = _pick(rng, ARM_REGS)
    rs = _pick(rng, ARM_REGS)
    rn = _pick(rng, ARM_REGS)
    imm = _rand_imm(rng, 12)
    tmpl = _pick(rng, ARM_MN)
    return tmpl.format(rd=rd, rs=rs, rn=rn, imm=imm)


def gen_riscv(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    rd = _pick(rng, RISCV_REGS)
    rs = _pick(rng, RISCV_REGS)
    rt = _pick(rng, RISCV_REGS)
    imm = _rand_imm(rng, 12)
    tmpl = _pick(rng, RISCV_MN)
    return tmpl.format(rd=rd, rs=rs, rt=rt, imm=imm)


def gen_mips(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    rd = _pick(rng, MIPS_REGS)
    rs = _pick(rng, MIPS_REGS)
    rt = _pick(rng, MIPS_REGS)
    imm = _rand_imm(rng, 16)
    tmpl = _pick(rng, MIPS_MN)
    return tmpl.format(rd=rd, rs=rs, rt=rt, imm=imm)


def gen_avr(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    rd = rng.randrange(0, 32)
    rs = rng.randrange(0, 32)
    imm = _rand_imm(rng, 8)
    tmpl = _pick(rng, AVR_MN)
    return tmpl.format(rd=rd, rs=rs, imm=imm)


def gen_sparc(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    imm = _rand_imm(rng, 22)
    return _pick(rng, SPARC_MN).format(imm=imm)


def gen_generic(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    tmpl = _pick(rng, GENERIC_PATTERNS)
    return tmpl.format(imm=_rand_imm(rng, 16), hex=_rand_hex(rng, 4))


def gen_program(rng: random.Random, max_lines: int) -> str:
    gens = [gen_x86, gen_arm, gen_mips, gen_riscv, gen_avr, gen_sparc, gen_generic]
    lines = []
    n = rng.randint(1, max_lines)
    for _ in range(n):
        g = _pick(rng, gens)
        lines.append(g(rng))
    # Occasionally add labels to help pattern searches
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        lines.insert(0, "label_{}:".format(_rand_hex(rng, 1)))
    return "\n".join(lines)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a content style: single instruction, short sequence, or mixed program.
    style = rng.random()
    if style < 0.4:
        # Single instruction tuned to likely archs
        s = _pick(rng, [gen_x86, gen_arm, gen_mips, gen_riscv])(rng)
    elif style < 0.8:
        # Short program to exercise search APIs
        s = gen_program(rng, max_lines=rng.randint(2, 8))
    else:
        # Longer mixed program but keep under size limit
        s = gen_program(rng, max_lines=rng.randint(8, 32))
    # Ensure size <= 4096
    enc = s.encode('utf-8')
    if len(enc) > 4096:
        enc = enc[:4096]
    # NUL-terminated string expected by C APIs
    return enc + b"\x00"

import random
from typing import List

# Generator for C source code snippets to feed r_anal_cparse
# Goal: produce small, valid C programs/snippets that exercise types, typedefs,
# structs/unions/enums, attributes, function prototypes/definitions, pointers,
# arrays, qualifiers, statements, and various integer widths.
# Output must be NUL-terminated text buffer content (as bytes when returned).

IDENT_CHARS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"
IDENT_CHARS_NUM = IDENT_CHARS + "0123456789"

INT_TYPES = [
    "char", "signed char", "unsigned char",
    "short", "unsigned short",
    "int", "unsigned int",
    "long", "unsigned long",
    "long long", "unsigned long long",
    "int8_t", "uint8_t", "int16_t", "uint16_t",
    "int32_t", "uint32_t", "int64_t", "uint64_t",
    "size_t", "ssize_t",
]

QUALIFIERS = ["", "const ", "volatile ", "restrict ", "const volatile "]
STORAGE = ["", "static ", "extern "]
FUNC_ATTRS = ["", "__attribute__((unused)) ", "__attribute__((noreturn)) "]
POINTER_QUALS = ["*", "* const", "* volatile", "* restrict"]

# Some common includes to unlock stdint_t etc.
INCLUDE_SETS = [
    ["#include <stdint.h>", "#include <stddef.h>", "#include <stdarg.h>"]
]

BIN_OPS = ["+", "-", "*", "/", "%", "|", "&", "^", "<<", ">>"]
CMP_OPS = ["==", "!=", "<", ">", "<=", ">="]
LOG_OPS = ["&&", "||"]


def rnd_ident(rng: random.Random, minlen=1, maxlen=12) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(minlen, maxlen)
    s = rng.choice(IDENT_CHARS)
    s += ''.join(rng.choice(IDENT_CHARS_NUM) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return s


def pick(rng: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:
    return rng.choice(arr)


def gen_typedefs(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> str:
    out = []
    for _ in range(count):
        base = pick(rng, INT_TYPES)
        name = rnd_ident(rng)
        ptrlvl = rng.choices([0, 1, 2], weights=[5, 3, 2])[0]
        decl = base
        if ptrlvl:
            decl += " " + " ".join(pick(rng, POINTER_QUALS) for _ in range(ptrlvl))
        out.append(f"typedef {decl} {name};")
    return "\n".join(out)


def gen_struct_union_enum(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    kind = rng.choice(["struct", "union", "enum"])
    tag = rnd_ident(rng)
    if kind == "enum":
        members = []
        for i in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
            name = rnd_ident(rng)
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                members.append(f"{name} = {rng.randint(-5, 20)}")
            else:
                members.append(name)
        return f"enum {tag} {{ {', '.join(members)} }};\n"
    else:
        fields = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
            t = pick(rng, INT_TYPES)
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                t = rnd_ident(rng)  # refer possible typedef
            arr = ""
            if rng.random() < 0.4:
                arr = f"[{rng.randint(1, 8)}]"
            fields.append(f"    {t} {rnd_ident(rng)}{arr};")
        return f"{kind} {tag} {{\n" + "\n".join(fields) + "\n};\n"


def gen_function_sig(rng: random.Random, name: str = None, define: bool = False) -> str:
    rtype = pick(rng, INT_TYPES + ["void"]) if rng.random() < 0.8 else rnd_ident(rng)
    qual = pick(rng, QUALIFIERS)
    storage = pick(rng, STORAGE)
    attr = pick(rng, FUNC_ATTRS)
    fname = name or rnd_ident(rng)
    nargs = rng.randint(0, 4)
    params = []
    for i in range(nargs):
        pt = pick(rng, INT_TYPES)
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            pt = rnd_ident(rng)
        # maybe pointer
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            pt += " *"
        params.append(f"{pt} {rnd_ident(rng)}")
    if nargs == 0 and rng.random() < 0.5:
        paramstr = "void"
    else:
        paramstr = ", ".join(params)
    sig = f"{storage}{attr}{qual}{rtype} {fname}({paramstr})"
    if not define:
        return sig + ";"
    else:
        body = gen_function_body(rng, rtype, params)
        return sig + " {\n" + body + "\n}"


def expr_int(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    v = rng.randint(0, 255)
    return str(v)


def gen_expr(rng: random.Random, depth: int = 0) -> str:
    if depth > 2 or rng.random() < 0.3:
        return expr_int(rng)
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.4:
        return f"({gen_expr(rng, depth+1)} {pick(rng, BIN_OPS)} {gen_expr(rng, depth+1)})"
    elif choice < 0.7:
        return f"({gen_expr(rng, depth+1)} {pick(rng, CMP_OPS)} {gen_expr(rng, depth+1)})"
    else:
        return f"({gen_expr(rng, depth+1)} {pick(rng, LOG_OPS)} {gen_expr(rng, depth+1)})"


def gen_function_body(rng: random.Random, rtype: str, params: List[str]) -> str:
    lines = []
    # local declarations
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        t = pick(rng, INT_TYPES)
        name = rnd_ident(rng)
        init = f" = {expr_int(rng)}" if rng.random() < 0.7 else ""
        lines.append(f"    {t} {name}{init};")
    # control flow
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        lines.append(f"    if {gen_expr(rng)} {{")
        lines.append("        ;")
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            lines.append("    } else {")
            lines.append("        ;")
        lines.append("    }")
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        it = rnd_ident(rng)
        lines.append(f"    for (int {it}=0; {it} < {rng.randint(1,6)}; {it}++) {{ ; }}")
    # return
    if rtype.strip() == "void":
        lines.append("    return;")
    else:
        lines.append(f"    return {gen_expr(rng)};")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def gen_global_vars(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> str:
    out = []
    for _ in range(count):
        t = pick(rng, INT_TYPES)
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            t = rnd_ident(rng)
        name = rnd_ident(rng)
        arr = ""
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            arr = f"[{rng.randint(2, 10)}]"
        init = ""
        if arr and rng.random() < 0.6:
            vals = ", ".join(str(rng.randint(0, 5)) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)))
            init = f" = {{ {vals} }}"
        elif not arr and rng.random() < 0.6:
            init = f" = {rng.randint(0, 42)}"
        stor = pick(rng, STORAGE)
        qual = pick(rng, QUALIFIERS)
        out.append(f"{stor}{qual}{t} {name}{arr}{init};")
    return "\n".join(out)


def gen_snippet(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = []
    # Includes
    parts.extend(pick(rng, INCLUDE_SETS))
    parts.append("")
    # Some typedefs first (so later names can reference them)
    parts.append(gen_typedefs(rng, rng.randint(2, 6)))
    # A struct/union/enum or two
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        parts.append(gen_struct_union_enum(rng))
    # Some globals
    parts.append(gen_global_vars(rng, rng.randint(1, 4)))
    # Function prototypes
    protos = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        protos.append(gen_function_sig(rng, define=False))
    parts.extend(protos)
    # A few function definitions
    defs = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        defs.append(gen_function_sig(rng, define=True))
    # Ensure at least one trivial function that is obviously valid
    defs.append("int f(int a){ return a + 1; }")
    parts.extend(defs)
    return "\n".join(p.strip() for p in parts if p is not None)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Compose multiple snippets occasionally to increase variety
    n = 1 if rng.random() < 0.7 else 2
    txt_parts = []
    for i in range(n):
        txt_parts.append(gen_snippet(rng))
        if i + 1 < n:
            txt_parts.append("\n/* ---- splitter ---- */\n")
    text = "\n".join(txt_parts)
    # Truncate to 4000 bytes to stay within 4096 when adding trailing NUL
    b = text.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")[:4000]
    # Ensure non-empty and NUL-terminated
    if not b:
        b = b"typedef int T; int f(int a){return a;}"
    return b

import random
import struct
import itertools

# Generate valid ESIL expressions focusing on registers and simple ops used in stubs
# The fuzzer harness pulls a std::string via FUZZ_PARAM_STR for expressions and sometimes
# an ut64 for an address. We emit a buffer that contains multiple NUL-terminated strings
# and fixed-width integers so the harness can slice from it. Keep it self-contained.

REGS = [
    "rax", "eax", "rbx", "ebx", "rcx", "ecx", "rdx", "edx",
    "rsi", "esi", "rdi", "edi", "rsp", "esp", "rbp", "ebp",
    "r0", "r1", "r2", "r3", "x0", "x1", "x2", "x3"
]

# ESIL mini building blocks
OPS_BIN = ["+", "-", "*", "/", "&", "|", "^"]
ASSIGN = ",="
PUSH = ","

# Some small, valid expressions known to exercise DFG/filter/config paths
SEED_TEMPLATES = [
    # write const to reg
    "{imm}{p}{reg}{assign}",
    # reg to reg move
    "{reg2}{p}{reg}{assign}",
    # binary op with immediate then assign
    "{imm}{p}{reg2}{p}{op}{p}{reg}{assign}",
    # memory read/write simple forms
    # write reg into [addr]
    "{reg}{p}{imm}{p}=[1]",
    # read [addr] into reg
    "{imm}{p}[[1]]{p}{reg}{assign}",
    # set flags-like sequence: rax++, store
    "1{p}{reg}{p}+{p}{reg}{assign}",
]

# Optionally include a few standalone constant assignments for minimal cases
FALLBACKS = [
    "1,rax,=",
    "0,rbx,=",
    "42,r0,=",
]


def _rand_imm(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # small constants are common; sometimes large
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 255, 256, 1024, 4096]
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        val = rng.randrange(0, 1 << 16)
    else:
        val = rng.choice(choices)
    return str(val)


def _rand_reg(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(REGS)


def _rand_op(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(OPS_BIN)


def build_esil_expr(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # choose a template and fill placeholders
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        return rng.choice(FALLBACKS)
    tpl = rng.choice(SEED_TEMPLATES)
    expr = tpl.format(
        imm=_rand_imm(rng),
        reg=_rand_reg(rng),
        reg2=_rand_reg(rng),
        op=_rand_op(rng),
        p=PUSH,
        assign=ASSIGN,
    )
    return expr


def pack_u64(x: int) -> bytes:
    # harness masks to 0xffff, but we still provide a full u64
    return struct.pack("<Q", x & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)


def build_buffer(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts = []

    # 1) Address seed (u64)
    off = rng.randrange(0, 0x10000)  # small as the stub masks it to 0xffff
    parts.append(pack_u64(off))

    # 2) Primary ESIL expression string (NUL-terminated)
    expr = build_esil_expr(rng)
    parts.append(expr.encode("ascii") + b"\x00")

    # 3) Secondary strings to allow multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls to pull valid data
    # Include a few variations to exercise different code paths
    extra_exprs = [
        build_esil_expr(rng),
        build_esil_expr(rng),
        rng.choice(FALLBACKS),
    ]
    for s in extra_exprs:
        parts.append(s.encode("ascii") + b"\x00")

    # 4) Some registers as strings (targets in dfg_filter_expr)
    regs_to_emit = rng.sample(REGS, k=min(4, len(REGS)))
    for r in regs_to_emit:
        parts.append(r.encode("ascii") + b"\x00")

    # 5) A couple of 32-bit integers for boolean flags selection in stubs
    # The harness uses ((*FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)) & 1/2)
    flags = [0, 1, 2, 3]
    rng.shuffle(flags)
    for f in flags:
        parts.append(struct.pack("<I", f))

    blob = b"".join(parts)
    return blob[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return build_buffer(rng)
